Parity plan 0.2.0

Default Secondary Destructive Outline Ghost Link
); } ``` ## With an icon Pair a short label with an icon; the text still communicates the status without depending on the icon or colour. ```tsx import { CheckIcon, ClockIcon, GitBranchIcon } from "lucide-react"; import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge"; export function BadgeIcons() { return (
Verified Pending main
); } ``` ## As a link `render` replaces the element, so a badge stays a `span` unless you ask for something else. The `[a&]` selectors only switch on hover when it really is a link. These anchors use native focus and Enter navigation to the changelog. ```tsx import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge"; export function BadgeLinks() { return (
}>3 releases }>Changelog
); } ``` ## When to use - A short status: `Active`, `Beta`, `Deprecated`, `3 open`. - A category or tag next to a title, where the colour carries the grouping. - A count attached to a navigation item or a filter chip. ## When not to use - Anything the user must click to act; use `button` (a badge has no focus, no press feedback, and no keyboard path). - More than about three words. A long label belongs in running text or in a `card` header, not in a pill. - A status that changes while the user watches; use `toast` or an inline message, because a badge swap is easy to miss. ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------ | | `variant` | `"default" \| "secondary" \| "outline" \| "ghost" \| "destructive" \| "link"` | `"default"` | Visual weight. | | `render` | `ReactElement \| (props, state) => ReactElement` | – | Base UI composition; replaces `asChild`. | | `className` | `string` | – | Merged last. | `data-slot="badge"` and `data-variant` are rendered from the component's state, so you can restyle per variant from CSS without touching this file. All native span props are forwarded. ## Motion contract No motion (T0). A badge labels content; it does not enter, leave, or move. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ----------------------------------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | `transition-[color,box-shadow]` is state feedback on the design tokens (hover on a linked badge, the focus ring), not motion: it never moves the box and never runs on mount. ## Accessibility - The badge is a `span`, so it is not in the tab order and has no role — the text itself is the message. - Colour is never the only signal: every variant still carries readable text. - When rendered as a link it inherits the anchor's semantics, focus ring, and keyboard behaviour, and gains `[a&]:hover` styles automatically. ## Responsiveness and performance Badges keep intrinsic width and do not wrap their text. Keep labels short; let the parent wrap a collection or provide an overflow strategy for long labels. T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. Base UI behavior requires hydration; native HTML behavior remains browser-owned. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. items.title: Kbd
items.description: Keyboard shortcuts in tooltips, menus, and command lists.
items.docs: ## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/kbd ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Kbd, KbdGroup } from "@/components/cadence/kbd"; export function ShortcutHint() { return ( Search ⌘K ); } ``` ## Single key Use one `Kbd` for one physical key. It is a hint, with no focus stop or keyboard handler. ```tsx import { Kbd } from "@/components/cadence/kbd"; export function EscapeHint() { return Esc; } ``` ## A combination `KbdGroup` renders the keys with one gap between them and keeps the sequence together for screen readers. ```tsx import { Kbd, KbdGroup } from "@/components/cadence/kbd"; export function CommandHint() { return ( Ctrl Shift P ); } ``` ## Inside a tooltip A `Kbd` inside `data-slot="tooltip-content"` inverts its colours automatically, so the hint stays legible on the tooltip surface. Focus or hover the trigger to see it. Install `@cadence/tooltip` and `@cadence/button` for this composition; the application owns any save action or shortcut handler. Tooltip and Button keep their own motion contracts and inherit the site's motion settings. ```tsx import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { Kbd, KbdGroup } from "@/components/cadence/kbd"; import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tooltip"; export function SaveHint() { return ( }>Save changes Save ⌘S ); } ``` ## When to use - A shortcut hinted next to a command: search, save, new item. - A key the user should press in a flow: `Tab`, `Esc`, `↑ ↓`. - Inside a `tooltip` or a `dropdown-menu` item, where space is short. ## When not to use - A key that is part of running text. Write it in prose; a pill interrupts the sentence. - A button that runs a command. A `kbd` is a label, not a control — it has no keyboard path and no press state. - Long sequences of more than three keys. Put the shortcut in a table instead. ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | ---------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | | `Kbd` | native `kbd` props | One key. `data-slot="kbd"`. | | `KbdGroup` | native `div` props | Wraps several keys with `data-slot="kbd-group"`. | KbdGroup keeps the pinned native div prop type while rendering a `kbd` element. ## Motion contract No motion (T0). A key hint is a label; it must not pulse or slide while the user is reading it. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | ## Accessibility - Renders a real `` element, which assistive technology reports as keyboard input — the same information a sighted user reads from the key shape. - The shortcut is text, so it survives every reduced-motion mode and every colour theme. - If a hint is icon-only, put the key name in `aria-label` on the `Kbd`. - Do not attach `tabIndex`; a shortcut hint is not focusable. ## Responsiveness and performance Keys and key groups use intrinsic inline sizes. The caller owns wrapping or scrolling long shortcut descriptions; these labels do not register keyboard shortcuts. T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive children and application handlers still need their own client code. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately. ## Notes for AI - Use the platform's own glyphs (`⌘`, `⇧`, `↵`) rather than words, and keep one `Kbd` per physical key. - If the shortcut is a live command, render a `button` and put the `Kbd` inside it.

This self-contained illustration can be replaced by your own image. ```tsx "use client"; import { AspectRatio } from "@/components/cadence/aspect-ratio"; export function SquareImage() { return (
); } ``` ## Video A `16 / 9` frame reserves room for video before it loads. Native controls belong to the media itself and stay usable; there is no autoplay. This silent sample loads from MDN only when requested. Replace its source with your own clip and supply captions when it contains speech. ```tsx "use client"; import { AspectRatio } from "@/components/cadence/aspect-ratio"; export function VideoFrame() { return (

Here `4 / 3`, `1`, and `3 / 4` reserve different shapes at the same column width. {[{ ratio: 4 / 3, label: "4 : 3" }, { ratio: 1, label: "1 : 1" }, { ratio: 3 / 4, label: "3 : 4" }].map(({ ratio, label }) => ( ))}
); } ``` ## When to use - An image, video, or embed whose intrinsic size is unknown until it loads. - A thumbnail grid that must not reflow as the images arrive. - A placeholder that will be replaced by media of a known shape. ## When not to use - Fixed-size icons or avatars; give them a size and be done. - Text blocks. A ratio box around text clips exactly the content that needs to grow. - A container whose height should follow its content — that is a normal block. ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | | `ratio` | `number` | – | Width ÷ height. items.name: alert
items.title: Alert
items.description: Errors, warnings, and page-level status messages.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/alert
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { CircleAlert } from "lucide-react";
import { Alert, AlertDescription, AlertTitle } from "@/components/cadence/alert";

export function QuotaNotice() {
  return (
    <Alert>
      <CircleAlert />
      <AlertTitle>You are close to the build limit</AlertTitle>
      <AlertDescription>12 of 15 builds used this month.</AlertDescription>
    </Alert>
  );
}
```

## With an action

`AlertAction` spans both grid rows, so it stays on the first line when the
description wraps.

```tsx
<Alert variant="destructive">
  <TriangleAlert />
  <AlertTitle>Deploy failed</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>Build 42 exited with code 1.</AlertDescription>
  <AlertAction>
    <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Retry</Button>
  </AlertAction>
</Alert>
```

## Without an icon

The icon column collapses to zero, so title and description sit flush left. Add an
icon only when it tells the user something the title does not.

```tsx
<Alert>
  <AlertTitle>Read-only mode</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>Billing needs attention before you can edit.</AlertDescription>
</Alert>
```

## Destructive

`variant="destructive"` colours the text and leaves the surface as a card. A red
block is harder to read and competes with the page it sits on.

```tsx
<Alert variant="destructive">Payment declined</Alert>
```

## When to use

- The result of an action the user just took, where the outcome needs a sentence of
  explanation: a failed deploy, a partial import, a quota that is nearly full.
- A state of the page that is not an error but changes what is possible — degraded
  mode, read-only mode, a plan that expired yesterday.
- A warning attached to a region rather than to a control, so it survives scrolling
  away from the field it is about.

## When not to use

- A confirmation that needs no reading ("Saved"). Use `toast`: an alert stays in the
  layout, and stale success messages become noise.
- A decision that blocks progress. That is `alert-dialog`, which traps focus on
  purpose.
- Ordinary guidance or onboarding copy. An `alert` is a live region; using it for
  static text makes screen readers interrupt the user for nothing.

## API

| Part               | Props                    | Notes                                                          |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Alert`            | `variant`, native props  | `variant`: `"default" \| "destructive"`. Always `role="alert"`. |
| `AlertTitle`       | native div props         | One line, medium weight, second grid column.                    |
| `AlertDescription` | native div props         | Muted text; paragraphs inside keep relaxed leading.             |
| `AlertAction`      | native div props         | Third grid column, spans both rows.                            |

Every part sets `data-slot` (`alert`, `alert-title`, `alert-description`,
`alert-action`), so a consumer can restyle without new props:
`[&>[data-slot=alert-title]]:text-base`.

Destructive descriptions use the full destructive text token for readable contrast in both themes. An action has its own grid column so it cannot cover the title or description.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). An alert that slides or fades in draws attention to the animation
instead of the message, and a message that is already on screen when the page loads
did not change — animating it is decoration (P9).

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

The border and text colours are state feedback on the design tokens; they are not
animated and carry no timing.

## Accessibility

- `role="alert"` makes the alert an assertive live region. Mount it when the state
  appears; do not keep a permanent alert in the tree and toggle its text, because
  every change interrupts whatever the screen reader was saying.
- The icon is decorative — mark it `aria-hidden` if it duplicates the title. An
  icon inside a link or a button is different: that one needs its own name.
- `variant="destructive"` is colour plus a title that says what happened. Never rely
  on the colour alone: the message has to be readable in greyscale.
- The action is a real control. If it is the only way forward, it must be reachable
  by keyboard and come after the message in DOM order (it does).

## Responsiveness and performance

Alerts fill their parent and reserve separate columns for icon, text and optional action. Keep
action labels short or adapt the composition for narrow containers; the caller owns long-content
wrapping.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive
children and application handlers still need their own client code. Server-rendered markup does not
imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for
this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Use an alert for a state that persists; use `toast` for a moment.
- Keep exactly one `role="alert"` per message. Nesting parts does not add roles —
  only `Alert` sets one.
- Do not pass an `onClose` and hide it with opacity; that is a toast, not an alert.

items.name: empty
items.title: Empty
items.description: Lists, tables, and panels with nothing to show yet.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/empty
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Inbox } from "lucide-react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import {
  Empty,
  EmptyContent,
  EmptyDescription,
  EmptyHeader,
  EmptyMedia,
  EmptyTitle,
} from "@/components/cadence/empty";

export function InvoicesEmpty() {
  return (
    <Empty>
      <EmptyHeader>
        <EmptyMedia variant="icon">
          <Inbox />
        </EmptyMedia>
        <EmptyTitle>No invoices yet</EmptyTitle>
        <EmptyDescription>Invoices you send will land here.</EmptyDescription>
      </EmptyHeader>
      <EmptyContent>
        <Button size="sm">Create invoice</Button>
      </EmptyContent>
    </Empty>
  );
}
```

## Bounded or unbounded

The root is a dashed container with generous padding, so it can stand in for a whole
panel. Drop the boundary with a class when it already sits inside a bordered card.

```tsx
<Empty className="border">…</Empty>
```

## A second action

`EmptyContent` is a column with a gap; put the secondary action underneath, or side
by side with a row wrapper.

```tsx
<EmptyContent>
  <Button size="sm">Import CSV</Button>
  <Button size="sm" variant="ghost">Start from a template</Button>
</EmptyContent>
```

## Icon or illustration

`variant="icon"` puts the glyph on a muted surface; `default` leaves the media
transparent for an illustration or a small chart.

```tsx
<EmptyMedia variant="icon">
  <Inbox />
</EmptyMedia>
```

## When to use

- A list, table, or panel that is legitimately empty: no invoices, no results for
  this filter, a folder nobody has filled yet.
- An empty state that teaches the next step — a primary action, a link to a
  template, or a line that explains what will appear here.
- A region whose emptiness is a state, not a mistake: an inbox at zero, a fresh
  workspace.

## When not to use

- While loading. Use `skeleton` when the shape of the incoming content is known,
  and `spinner` when it is not.
- A search that returned nothing because of a typo. That case needs the query echoed
  back and the filter explained, not a generic illustration.
- An error. An empty region is a normal state; a failed request is an `alert`.

## API

| Part               | Props                   | Notes                                                          |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Empty`            | native div props        | Centred flex column, dashed boundary, `md:p-12`.               |
| `EmptyHeader`      | native div props        | Stacks media, title, description; `max-w-sm`.                  |
| `EmptyTitle`       | native div props        | Large, medium weight. Renders a `div`, not a heading.          |
| `EmptyDescription` | native props for `p`    | Renders a `div` (upstream too): the copy often holds a block.  |
| `EmptyMedia`       | `variant`               | `"default" \| "icon"`, exposed as `data-variant`.              |
| `EmptyContent`     | native div props        | Actions; full width, `max-w-sm`, own gap.                      |

`data-slot` values are `empty`, `empty-header`, `empty-title`,
`empty-description`, `empty-icon`, `empty-content`.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). An empty state is a resting state: it is what the region looks like
when nothing is happening. Fading it in would make it look like content arriving,
which is the one thing it is not.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

When the region swaps from empty to populated, that transition belongs to the list
(`list.stagger` or `data.transition`), not to this component.

## Accessibility

- The root is a plain container: no role, no live region. Announce the change of
  state in the region that owns it (`aria-live="polite"` on the list), not here.
- `EmptyTitle` renders a `div`. If the empty state is the main content of a page,
  put a real heading inside it so it appears in the outline.
- The media is decorative. Pass `aria-hidden` to the icon, or give the surrounding
  text the whole message — an icon alone never carries meaning.
- Keep at least one action focusable. An empty state with no way forward is a dead
  end; the primary action is the reason this component exists.

## Responsiveness and performance

The root can shrink with its parent and increases padding at md. Header and content have bounded
widths; the caller owns the surrounding height and wrapping action rows.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive
children and application handlers still need their own client code. Composed controls retain their
own dependencies and motion contracts. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction
works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped
source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- One primary action per empty state. Two competing buttons read as a decision the
  user is not ready to make.
- Do not build an empty state out of `Card` plus padding; the boundary, the rhythm,
  and the description width are already decided here.
- Do not use `Empty` for a loading placeholder — `skeleton` keeps the layout stable,
  which `Empty` does not.

items.name: field
items.title: Field
items.description: Form controls that need a label, help text, and error.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/field
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Field, FieldContent, FieldDescription, FieldLabel } from "@/components/cadence/field";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";

export function CompanyField() {
  return (
    <Field>
      <FieldLabel htmlFor="company">Company</FieldLabel>
      <FieldContent>
        <Input id="company" />
        <FieldDescription>Appears on the invoice header.</FieldDescription>
      </FieldContent>
    </Field>
  );
}
```

## Vertical, horizontal, responsive

`orientation` decides where the label sits. `responsive` keeps a column until the
`FieldGroup` reaches `md`, then turns into a row — the group is the container query
root, so it works inside a sidebar or a dialog without a breakpoint for each.

```tsx
<FieldGroup>
  <Field orientation="horizontal">…</Field>
  <Field orientation="responsive">…</Field>
</FieldGroup>
```

## An error, from the caller

`FieldError` renders what it is given and returns `null` when it has nothing. Two
messages become a list; duplicates collapse.

```tsx
<Field data-invalid="true">
  <FieldLabel htmlFor="vat">VAT number</FieldLabel>
  <FieldContent>
    <Input id="vat" aria-invalid aria-describedby="vat-error" />
    <FieldError id="vat-error" errors={[{ message: "Required" }, { message: "Not a work email" }]} />
  </FieldContent>
</Field>
```

## A set, a legend, and a divider

```tsx
<FieldSet>
  <FieldLegend>Billing details</FieldLegend>
  <FieldGroup>
    <Field>…</Field>
    <FieldSeparator>or</FieldSeparator>
    <Field>…</Field>
  </FieldGroup>
</FieldSet>
```

## A choice card

`FieldLabel` recognises a `Field` inside it and becomes the card: full width, border,
padding, and a primary tint when the inner control is checked.

```tsx
<FieldLabel>
  <Field orientation="horizontal">
    <FieldContent>
      <FieldTitle>Team plan</FieldTitle>
      <FieldDescription>Unlimited projects.</FieldDescription>
    </FieldContent>
    <Checkbox name="plan" value="team" />
  </Field>
</FieldLabel>
```

## When to use

- Any control that needs a visible label plus a line of help: text, select, checkbox
  group, radio group, a segmented choice.
- A form where the error has to sit next to the control it belongs to, not in a
  summary at the top.
- A choice card — a `Field` that contains a whole control card — where the label is
  the surface and the checked state is the selection.

## When not to use

- A single input with no label and no help. Do not wrap it; `input` already carries
  its own border and focus ring.
- A validation module. `Field` renders messages; it never produces them (P11).
- A toolbar of loose controls. Group those with `button-group`, which has no label
  semantics to offer.

## API

| Part               | Props                        | Notes                                                          |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Field`            | `orientation`, native props  | `vertical \| horizontal \| responsive`; `role="group"`, `data-orientation`. |
| `FieldLabel`       | `Label` props                | A real `label`; click focuses the control.                      |
| `FieldTitle`       | native div props             | Label-weight text that is not tied to a control.                |
| `FieldDescription` | native props for `p`         | Muted help text, balanced in horizontal orientation.            |
| `FieldError`       | `errors`, native div props   | `errors`: `{ message?: string }[]`. `role="alert"`, `null` when empty. |
| `FieldGroup`       | native div props             | Container query root; vertical rhythm between fields.           |
| `FieldContent`     | native div props             | Control plus description/error stack.                           |
| `FieldSet`         | native props for `fieldset`  | Groups related fields; pairs with `FieldLegend`.                |
| `FieldLegend`      | `variant`                    | `legend \| label` sizes the legend text.                        |
| `FieldSeparator`   | `children`                   | Rule with optional centred text; exposes `data-content`.        |

`data-slot` values: `field`, `field-label`, `field-description`, `field-error`,
`field-group`, `field-content`, `field-set`, `field-legend`, `field-separator`,
`field-separator-content`.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). A field never animates — not on mount, not when the error appears.
The error is the one thing the user must read immediately; fading or sliding it in
delays the only information that matters, and it moves the control the user's cursor
is in.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

`data-[invalid=true]` recolours the field's text on the destructive token. That is a
colour change, not a motion, and it is never the only signal.

## Accessibility

- `FieldLabel` is a `label`, so clicking it focuses the control it names. Always pass
  `htmlFor` matching the control's `id`; a `FieldTitle` is not a substitute.
- An error is `role="alert"`: it is announced when it appears. Point the control at it
  with `aria-describedby` so the message is also part of the control's description.
- `aria-invalid` on the control is what makes the state machine-readable; the
  destructive colour is the sighted half of the same signal.
- A horizontal field puts the label after the content in source order when the content
  holds the control. Keep the DOM order label → control for a simple pair.

## Validation and data ownership

P11 draws the line: the component renders state, you decide state.

| `Field` does                                            | You do                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Renders the message it is given (`children` or `errors`) | Deciding what is invalid (required, format, async checks)  |
| Marks the error `role="alert"`                           | Wiring `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` on the control |
| Colours the field when `data-invalid` / `aria-invalid`   | Form state, submit, retry, focus management                |
| Shows a description and an error at once                 | Writing the copy and the ids                               |

There is no `schema`, `resolver`, `validate`, or `rules` prop, and no validation
library is imported. `FieldError` accepts messages, not rules: the decision that a
value is wrong, and the copy that says so, stay in your form code.

## Responsiveness and performance

FieldGroup establishes a named container. Responsive orientation switches from column to row at its
md container query; explicit vertical and horizontal orientations remain caller-selected. Labels,
error text and controls must fit the available width.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive
children and application handlers still need their own client code. Composed controls retain their
own dependencies and motion contracts. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction
works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped
source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Do not add an `error` prop to `Input`; put the message in `FieldError` and point
  `aria-describedby` at it.
- Use `FieldGroup` as the container, not a `space-y-*` div: the responsive
  orientation depends on being inside a container query root.
- `FieldError` returns `null` when it has no content, so it is safe to keep mounted.

items.title: Button Group
items.description: Toolbars and related actions on the same object.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button-group
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { ButtonGroup } from "@/components/cadence/button-group";

export function TextStyle() {
  return (
    <ButtonGroup aria-label="Text style">
      <Button variant="outline" size="icon-sm" aria-label="Bold">
        <Bold />
      </Button>
      <Button variant="outline" size="icon-sm" aria-label="Italic">
        <Italic />
      </Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

## Vertical

`orientation="vertical"` stacks the same rules: only the outer corners are rounded,
and the shared borders collapse.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup orientation="vertical" aria-label="Order">
  <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Move up</Button>
  <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Move down</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

## Static text inside the group

`ButtonGroupText` takes `render`, so the label can be a `label`, a `span`, or the
router's own element without extra wrappers.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Zoom">
  <ButtonGroupText>-</ButtonGroupText>
  <Button variant="outline" size="sm">100%</Button>
  <ButtonGroupSeparator />
  <ButtonGroupText>+</ButtonGroupText>
</ButtonGroup>
```

## A rule between two controls

`ButtonGroupSeparator` stretches to the cross axis, so one component works in both
orientations.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button>Cut</Button>
  <ButtonGroupSeparator />
  <Button>Copy</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

## When to use

- Two to five controls that act on the same object: bold/italic/underline, cut/copy,
  approve/reject, a zoom stepper.
- A segmented control where the current option is a button state (`variant="default"`
  vs `"ghost"`), not a radio group.
- A label plus an action, where the label should read as part of the control — use
  `ButtonGroupText` for the static half.

## When not to use

- More than about five options. Beyond that the shape stops helping and a `select` or
  a menu is faster.
- Mutually exclusive choices that need arrow-key navigation and a form value. That is
  `toggle-group`, or a `radio-group` inside a `field`.
- A single button. The group adds nothing; use `button`.

## API

| Part                    | Props                     | Notes                                                          |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ButtonGroup`           | `orientation`, native div | `horizontal \| vertical`; `role="group"`, `data-orientation`.  |
| `ButtonGroupText`       | `render`, native div      | Static label; swapped element via Base UI `render`.            |
| `ButtonGroupSeparator`  | `Separator` props         | Vertical by default; `self-stretch`, `bg-input`.               |
| `buttonGroupVariants`   | `orientation`             | Exported for composing a custom group root.                    |

The joining rules are `[&>*]` selectors, so any child that renders a `data-slot` — a
button, an input, a select trigger — participates without a prop.

`ButtonGroupSeparator` accepts Base state callbacks for `className` and `style`, merged after defaults. `ButtonGroupText` uses native string classes and style objects.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). The group does not animate. Adjacent buttons share a border, and the
only depth cue is `focus-visible:relative` plus `z-10`, which lifts the focused
control above its neighbours so its ring is not clipped.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

The buttons inside keep their own press feedback; the group never adds a second
animation on top of it.

## Accessibility

- `role="group"` needs a name: pass `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) when there is
  no visible heading. Without one, a screen reader says "group" and nothing else.
- Tab order follows DOM order, not visual order. In `vertical`, keep the DOM order the
  same as the visual stack.
- Icon-only buttons inside a group must each carry an `aria-label`; the group label
  does not name them.
- Do not mark the active segment with colour alone — use `aria-pressed` on a toggle
  button, or a `data-state` attribute your CSS keys off.

## Responsiveness and performance

Groups use intrinsic width and a caller-selected orientation; no breakpoint switches it
automatically. Stack or constrain long groups at the application level rather than hiding focused
controls.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. Base UI behavior requires hydration; native
HTML behavior remains browser-owned. Composed controls retain their own dependencies and motion
contracts. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript.
The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped source; dependencies and
application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Use `ButtonGroup` for actions on one object, `toggle-group` for a value the form
  reads. They look alike and behave differently.
- Do not add gaps between children: the rounded/border collapse is what makes the
  group read as one control.
- `ButtonGroupSeparator` is already `self-stretch`; do not set a height.

items.title: Input Group
items.description: Currency fields, URLs, and inputs with inline actions.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/input-group
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  InputGroup,
  InputGroupAddon,
  InputGroupInput,
  InputGroupText,
} from "@/components/cadence/input-group";

export function Domain() {
  return (
    <InputGroup>
      <InputGroupAddon>
        <InputGroupText>https://</InputGroupText>
      </InputGroupAddon>
      <InputGroupInput placeholder="cadence.dev" aria-label="Domain" />
    </InputGroup>
  );
}
```

## Alignments

`align` decides where the addon sits: `inline-start`, `inline-end`, `block-start`,
`block-end`. The frame turns into a column for the block alignments, and the control
gives up the padding on that side.

```tsx
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupAddon align="block-start">Recipient</InputGroupAddon>
  <InputGroupInput aria-label="Recipient" />
</InputGroup>
```

## A button in the frame

`InputGroupButton` sizes itself on the addon scale (`xs`, `sm`, `icon-xs`,
`icon-sm`), so it never towers over a 36px field. A click on a real button does not
steal focus from the input — the addon's focus handler steps aside.

```tsx
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupInput placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search" />
  <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
    <InputGroupButton size="icon-xs" aria-label="Clear">×</InputGroupButton>
  </InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>
```

## A textarea with a footer

```tsx
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupTextarea aria-label="Note" />
  <InputGroupAddon align="block-end">
    <InputGroupText>0/280</InputGroupText>
    <InputGroupButton size="sm" className="ml-auto">Send</InputGroupButton>
  </InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>
```

## When to use

- A field with a fixed prefix or suffix: a currency symbol, `https://`, a unit, a
  domain.
- A control that needs one inline action: search with a shortcut hint, a chooser with
  a clear button, an invite field with a submit button.
- A textarea with a footer — a character count, a send button — where the footer must
  look attached to the field.

## When not to use

- A bare text field. Use `input`; the group would only re-create its border.
- A whole toolbar of actions. Use `button-group` beside the field, or a `form` layout:
  four buttons inside one field is a cramped target.
- A label. Use `field` and `FieldLabel`; an addon is not an accessible name.

## API

| Part                  | Props                    | Notes                                                          |
| --------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `InputGroup`          | native div props         | The frame; `role="group"`, focus and invalid state via `:has()`. |
| `InputGroupAddon`     | `align`, native div      | `inline-start \| inline-end \| block-start \| block-end`, `data-align`. |
| `InputGroupButton`    | `size`, `variant`, `type`| `xs \| sm \| icon-xs \| icon-sm`; ghost by default.            |
| `InputGroupText`      | native span props        | Muted text or an icon; not a label.                            |
| `InputGroupInput`     | `input` props            | Control with the frame's chrome removed; `data-slot="input-group-control"`. |
| `InputGroupTextarea`  | `textarea` props         | Same, for multi-line.                                          |

The frame watches `[data-slot=input-group-control]` for `:focus-visible` and
`[aria-invalid=true]`, which is why the control can be borderless and the group still
shows the ring.

`InputGroupButton` preserves Button state callbacks for `className` and `style`, with caller classes last. The input and textarea wrappers keep their native props.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). The frame never animates. `transition-[color,box-shadow]` covers the
focus ring and the invalid border — state feedback that takes no space and does not
run on mount.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Accessibility

- The addon text is not a name. Give the control an `aria-label`, or put a `FieldLabel`
  around the group through `field`.
- `role="group"` on the frame and on each addon groups the pieces for assistive tech;
  add `aria-label` to the frame only if the group needs a name of its own.
- The addon focuses the input on click — a convenience for pointer users. Keyboard
  users tab straight into the control, which is already the shortest path.
- Buttons inside the frame keep their own names. An icon-only clear button needs
  `aria-label="Clear"`.
- `aria-invalid` must be on the control, not on the frame; the frame reacts to it.

## Validation and data ownership

P11: the group shows invalid state, it never decides it.

| `InputGroup` does                                        | You do                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Draws the destructive border when a control is invalid    | Deciding what is invalid                                 |
| Moves focus to the input when the addon is clicked        | Wiring `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`             |
| Renders the buttons you give it                           | Submit, retry, error mapping                             |

There is no `validate`, `schema`, or `resolver` prop, and no validation library is
imported. [Field](/components/field) shows how the invalid state and its message are wired.

## Responsiveness and performance

The group fills its parent and permits shrinking. Block-start/end addons use column layout; inline
addons share the input row. The caller owns long addon labels, button wrapping and narrow-screen
composition.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive
children and application handlers still need their own client code. Composed controls retain their
own dependencies and motion contracts. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction
works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped
source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Never wrap `input` in this group to "add a border"; the input already has one.
- Put state on `InputGroupInput` (`aria-invalid`, `disabled`, `readOnly`) — the frame is
  chrome, and it inherits the appearance.
- Use `InputGroupButton`, not `Button`, inside the frame: the sizes are on the addon
  scale, and the addon's click handler recognises it as a button.

items.title: Pagination
items.description: Long result sets, tables, and search results.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/pagination
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Pagination,
  PaginationContent,
  PaginationItem,
  PaginationLink,
  PaginationNext,
  PaginationPrevious,
} from "@/components/cadence/pagination";

export function Pages({ page }: { page: number }) {
  return (
    <Pagination>
      <PaginationContent>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationPrevious href={`?page=${page - 1}`} />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationLink href="?page=1" isActive={page === 1}>
            1
          </PaginationLink>
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationNext href={`?page=${page + 1}`} />
        </PaginationItem>
      </PaginationContent>
    </Pagination>
  );
}
```

## A collapsed range

`PaginationEllipsis` marks the pages that are not rendered. It is hidden from
assistive tech, so the list stays short for a screen reader too.

```tsx
<PaginationItem>
  <PaginationEllipsis />
</PaginationItem>
```

## Custom labels

`PaginationPrevious` and `PaginationNext` take `text`; the label is hidden below `sm`,
where the chevron carries the meaning and the accessible name still says "Go to
previous page".

```tsx
<PaginationPrevious href="?page=1" text="Back" />
<PaginationNext href="?page=3" text="Forward" />
```

## Without a page in the URL

Keep the anchor and intercept the click; do not swap it for a button. The anchor keeps
middle-click, copy-link, and the "link" announcement.

```tsx
<PaginationLink
  href="#"
  onClick={(event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    setPage(3);
  }}
>
  3
</PaginationLink>
```

## When to use

- A result set that is paged for a reason: the total is unknown, the data is remote, or
  the URL should carry the page so it can be shared and reloaded.
- A list where the user needs to jump to a specific page, not only step forward.
- A table footer on the server, where the count lives in the response.

## When not to use

- A finite list that is already in memory. Render it, or a "load more" button — paging
  something you already have is a worse experience than scrolling.
- An infinite feed. There is no page to link to, so an anchor-based control lies.
- A carousel or a wizard. Those step through slides or steps, and their controls are
  buttons.

## API

| Part                  | Props                    | Notes                                                          |
| --------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Pagination`          | native nav props         | `aria-label="pagination"`, `role="navigation"`.                |
| `PaginationContent`   | native ul props          | Row with a one-unit gap.                                       |
| `PaginationItem`      | native li props          | One slot in the list.                                          |
| `PaginationLink`      | `isActive`, `size`, anchors | Always an `<a>`; `aria-current="page"` and `data-active` when active. |
| `PaginationPrevious`  | `text`, link props       | Chevron left; `aria-label="Go to previous page"`.              |
| `PaginationNext`      | `text`, link props       | Chevron right; `aria-label="Go to next page"`.                 |
| `PaginationEllipsis`  | native span props        | `aria-hidden`; contains `sr-only` "More pages".                |

`size` comes from the button variants (`icon` by default), so the shape matches a
button without becoming one.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). A page change is a navigation: the content that changes is the list,
not the control. Animating the pagination would animate the one thing that stays the
same.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

If the new page's rows should arrive in sequence, that is `list.stagger` on the list.

## Accessibility

- `aria-label="pagination"` names the landmark, so it can be skipped or listed.
- The current page is `aria-current="page"`. Colour and the outline variant are the
  sighted half of the same signal — never the only one.
- Previous and next carry a written `aria-label`, because their visible text is hidden
  below `sm`. The chevron alone is not a name.
- A disabled end state (`page 1`, no previous) should render the control without an
  `href` and with `aria-disabled="true"`, not a link that 404s.
- The ordered list gives the count; the ellipsis is decorative and must not be
  focusable.

## Responsiveness and performance

Navigation fills its parent while the inner list remains a single row. The caller chooses the page
range and ellipses and may hide optional text on small screens; page counts are not computed by the
component.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive
children and application handlers still need their own client code. Composed controls retain their
own dependencies and motion contracts. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction
works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped
source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Every control is an anchor. Do not replace it with `Button` — the shape comes from
  `buttonVariants`, and Base UI's button would put `role="button"` on a link.
- Keep `href` real (`?page=3`) even when a click handler takes over: it is what makes
  the control shareable and middle-clickable.
- Do not render more than about seven items; collapse the middle with
  `PaginationEllipsis`.

Loading the registry…
); } ``` ## Inside a button The button keeps its width because the spinner replaces nothing: keep the label and put the spinner in front of it, or reserve the label's space with `aria-live`. ```tsx ``` ## Sized by the caller The icon is `size-4` by default and inherits `currentColor`, so one class resizes and recolours it. ```tsx ``` ## A specific label "Loading" is the default. Say what is loading when the surrounding text does not. ```tsx ``` ## Under `data-motion="none"` The rotation stops; the icon stays and the label still says "Loading". A stopped spinner is still a state, which is why `none` does not remove it from the tree. ```tsx ``` ## When to use - An action the user just triggered: save, send, invite, publish. The spinner sits where the user is looking — inside the button, or immediately beside it. - A wait with no measurable progress: a request that returns when it returns. - A region that is loading and whose shape you cannot predict. When you *can* predict it, use `skeleton` instead: it keeps the layout stable. ## When not to use - A wait under about 300 ms. The spinner appears and disappears before it can be read, which reads as a flicker. Keep the button's label and disable it. - A known percentage. Use `progress`; a spinning wheel after "60%" is a regression. - A page that is loading its first paint. There is nothing to spin inside yet — a skeleton or a server-rendered shell is better. - A decorative "we're working on it" on a marketing page. Motion without a state change is decoration (P9). ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ----------- | -------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | | `className` | `string` | – | Merged last — size and colour live here (`size-3`, `text-…`). | | `aria-label`| `string` | `"Loading"` | The accessible name; pass a specific one when it helps. | All native `svg` props are forwarded. `data-slot="spinner"` and `data-motion` are always set, and `role="status"` with the label is the announcement. ## Motion contract Recipe: `data.transition`, continuous form. The loop is CSS (`animate-spin`) rather than Motion, for the same reason as `skeleton`: a spinner is by definition next to work the user is waiting on, and it must not add a frame callback to it. Only `transform` (rotation) changes, so the loop can never trigger layout. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------- | | spin | `rotate 0 → 360deg` | `data.transition` / `animate-spin` (theme timing) | yes (CSS) | | reduced | same rotation | `animate-spin` | yes (CSS) | | none | none; icon static | `animate-none` | – | Reduced keeps the rotation on purpose: M5 removes travel and scale, and a rotation in place is neither. A spinner that freezes under reduced motion would read as a frozen app. `none` stops it completely, which is what a screenshot test or a print stylesheet needs. ## Keyboard interactions None. The spinner is not focusable and takes no input; focus stays on the control that started the work, which is where the user's next action will be. ## Accessibility - `role="status"` is a polite live region: the label is announced when the spinner appears, without interrupting. Do not wrap it in another `aria-live` region. - The label must carry the meaning. The rotation is never the only signal, and under `data-motion="none"` it is not a signal at all. - Give the busy region `aria-busy="true"` and remove it when the work finishes, so the state survives even if the spinner unmounts early. - Do not replace a button's label with a spinner and nothing else. Keep the word, or add an `sr-only` copy, or the control loses its name mid-action. - Do not stack spinners. One per action; a page with five is a page with no feedback. ## Responsive behavior The spinner is an inline icon, so it follows the text it sits in. Inside a button it keeps the button's height; inside a heading, size it down (`size-3`) or it will dominate the line. On touch targets, keep the surrounding button at least 44×44 by size, not by growing the icon. ## Performance - One CSS animation per element, on `transform` only; no JS loop, no layout read. - Compositor-friendly, but the animation-system budget still applies: fewer than twenty simultaneously animating elements. For a list of pending rows, render one spinner for the list, not one per row. - No `will-change`: the browser promotes a transform animation on its own. ## Notes for AI - Use `spinner` for an action, `skeleton` for a layout. Getting this backwards is the most common loading-state mistake: a skeleton in a button, or a spinner where the content shape was known all along. - Keep the button's text; add the spinner in front of it and disable the button. - Under `data-motion="none"` the icon stays visible. Do not hide it to "respect" the preference — the state still has to be visible.

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description: Focused tasks such as renaming, inviting, or confirming.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/dialog
```

This also installs `button`, which the dialog uses for its close control.

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dialog";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function DeleteProject() {
  return (
    <Dialog>
      <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Delete project</DialogTrigger>
      <DialogContent>
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>Delete this project?</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>This removes every deployment and cannot be undone.</DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>
        <DialogFooter>
          <DialogClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Cancel</DialogClose>
          <Button variant="destructive">Delete project</Button>
        </DialogFooter>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <DialogContent>…</DialogContent>
</Dialog>;
```

## Without the built-in close button

```tsx
<DialogContent showCloseButton={false}>…</DialogContent>
```

## Footer with a close action

```tsx
<DialogFooter showCloseButton>
  <Button>Save</Button>
</DialogFooter>
```

## When to use

- A focused task that must interrupt the page: rename, invite, confirm.
- Content that needs a modal, a focus trap, and an obvious escape route.
- A short form whose result matters more than the page behind it.

## When not to use

- Non-blocking hints and menus; use `popover` or `tooltip`.
- Long multi-step flows; use a page or a wizard.
- Mobile sheets with drag gestures; use `drawer`.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Dialog` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` | Base UI root. |
| `DialogTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the dialog. |
| `DialogContent` | `showCloseButton`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay, and popup. |
| `DialogOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `DialogContent`. |
| `DialogClose` | native button props, `render` | Closes the dialog. |
| `DialogHeader` / `DialogFooter` | `className` | Layout only. |
| `DialogTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. |
| `DialogDescription` | `className` | Optional supporting text. |

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | overlay `opacity 0 → 1`; panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` / `duration.base` | yes |
| exit | overlay `opacity → 0`; panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` / `duration.base` | yes (reopen mid-exit) |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (overlay 96ms, panel 132ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so no transition runs | – | – |

The panel stays mounted while its exit transition runs; Base UI delays unmount until the
transition ends, so reopening mid-exit reverses cleanly.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside the dialog. |
| Escape | Closes the dialog and returns focus to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused control. |

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`,
  focus trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and Escape handling.
- The close button is a real button with a screen-reader-only label.
- `DialogTitle` is required; a dialog without an accessible name is invalid.
- Content is unmounted after the exit transition, so focus is never lost mid-flight.

## Responsive behavior

The panel is centred and capped at `max-w-lg`; on narrow viewports it keeps a 1rem gutter.
Long content scrolls inside the popup rather than the page.

## Performance

- One popup tree is mounted only while open.
- Animates opacity and scale only; no layout reads and no JavaScript animation loop.

## Notes for AI

- Always render a `DialogTitle`; it is the accessible name.
- Keep the confirming action specific ("Delete project", not "OK").
- Do not animate height inside the dialog; mount content instead.

## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/checkbox ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Checkbox } from "@/components/cadence/checkbox"; import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label"; export function Terms() { return (
); } ``` `id` lands on the hidden input, so `htmlFor` on a `label` names the control and clicking the label toggles it. ## Checked by default, and indeterminate ```tsx ``` `indeterminate` is a visual third state; `aria-checked="mixed"` is what a screen reader hears. It never replaces the checked state — pass `checked` too if the form needs a value. ## Controlled ```tsx const [accepted, setAccepted] = useState(false); ; ``` ## Invalid, with a described error ```tsx

You must accept the terms to continue.

``` The ring turns destructive because `aria-invalid` is set. The component does not decide that anything is wrong. ## In a row of settings ```tsx

Every Monday, 09:00.

``` ## When to use - One independent yes/no choice: accept the terms, remember this device, include archived items. - A set of choices where several can be true at once; use one checkbox per row. - A parent row that summarises children: pass `indeterminate` while the children disagree. - A table row selection, where each row is its own decision. ## When not to use - Exactly one of several options; use `radio-group`, which also gives arrow-key navigation. - An immediate setting that applies the moment it is flipped; use `switch`. - A formatting command that acts on a selection; use `toggle`. ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ------------------ | --------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | | `checked` | `boolean` | – | Controlled state. | | `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | `false` | Uncontrolled initial state. | | `onCheckedChange` | `(checked, details) => void` | – | Fired on click and on Space. | | `indeterminate` | `boolean` | `false` | Mixed visual state for a parent row. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Ignores interaction and form submission. | | `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Focusable, submitted, not changeable. | | `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Blocks form submission until checked. | | `name`, `value` | `string` | – | Form field identity and submitted value. | | `className` | `string` / state callback | – | Merged last. | All native attributes are forwarded, including `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`. ## Motion contract Recipe: `state.morph`. The tick is the protagonist — it fades in and settles from 0.96 to full size when the box is checked, and reverses when it is cleared. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- | ------------- | | check | `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` | `state.morph` | yes (re-click) | | clear | the same pair, reversed | `state.morph` | yes | | reduced | `opacity` only | `state.morph` | yes | | none | no transition | – | – | Only the indicator moves. The box itself keeps a `transition-shadow` for the focus ring and the invalid ring, which is colour/shadow state feedback, not motion. ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | ------------- | ------------------------------------------ | | `Tab` | Moves focus to the checkbox. | | `Space` | Toggles checked, unless `readOnly`. | | `Shift+Tab` | Moves focus to the previous control. | ## Accessibility - Base UI renders `role="checkbox"` on the visible element plus a hidden ``, so the control is in the form and in the tab order. - The tick is not the announcement: the state lives in `aria-checked`, which is why the reduced and `none` branches stay usable. - Always pair the box with a `Label` (`htmlFor`) or an `aria-label`; a bare box has no accessible name. - `indeterminate` announces as "mixed". Do not use it as a substitute for `checked` in a form. ## Validation and data ownership | The component does | You do | | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | | Styles `aria-invalid` and forwards it to the input | Deciding whether the box must be checked | | Forwards `required`, `name`, `value`, `disabled` | Building the submitted payload | | Announces `aria-checked` for all three states | Mapping the error to the field with `aria-describedby` | There is no `validate`, `schema`, or `rules` prop. [Field](/components/field) shows how the invalid state and its message are wired. ## Responsive behavior The control is fixed at 16px with a 44px touch target (the `after:` pseudo element extends the hit area), so it behaves the same at every breakpoint. Put the label beside it, not inside it; wrapping a checkbox in a label removes the `aria-describedby` chain. ## Performance No JS animation loop: one Motion element per box, animating only `opacity` and `transform`. A list of 50 checkboxes is 50 short transitions on demand, never a running loop. ## Notes for AI - Use `aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby` for errors; there is no `error` prop. - Do not add press animation to a checkbox; the tick is the only protagonist. - For "one of N", use `radio-group`; for an instant setting, use `switch`.

## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/radio-group ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/radio-group"; import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label"; export function Plan() { return (
); } ``` Every item needs a `value`. The group is one form field: `name` goes on the group, not on the items. ## Controlled ```tsx const [plan, setPlan] = useState("team"); … ; ``` `onValueChange` receives the new value plus Base UI's event details. ## Invalid ```tsx …

Choose a plan to continue.

``` `aria-invalid` on the group styles the items and is announced with the group. ## Disabled item ```tsx ``` A disabled item is still visible and still announced, so the option does not appear to vanish. ## When to use - A small, fixed set of options where exactly one applies: a plan, a priority, a shipping method. - Anywhere seeing all the options at once matters more than saving space. - A setting that applies on submit, not immediately. ## When not to use - Several answers can be true; use `checkbox`. - The setting applies the moment it changes; use `switch`. - More than about seven options, or a list that is filtered as you type; use `select` or `combobox`, which handle long lists and search. ## API ### `RadioGroup` | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- | | `value` | `string` | – | Controlled selection. | | `defaultValue` | `string` | – | Uncontrolled initial selection. | | `onValueChange` | `(value, details) => void` | – | Fired when the selection changes. | | `name` | `string` | – | Form field name, submitted with the selection. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables every item. | | `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Blocks submit until something is selected. | | `className` | `string` / state callback | – | Merged last; the default is `grid gap-3`. | ### `RadioGroupItem` | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ----------- | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------- | | `value` | `string` | – | Required. Identifies this option. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Keeps the option visible but unselectable.| | `className` | `string` / state callback | – | Merged last. | ## Motion contract Recipe: `state.morph`. The dot of the newly selected item fades in and settles from 0.96 to full size; the previously selected dot reverses. Nothing else in the row moves, so the eye follows the choice. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | --------- | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------- | | select | `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` | `state.morph` | yes | | deselect | the same pair, reversed | `state.morph` | yes | | reduced | `opacity` only | `state.morph` | yes | | none | no transition | – | – | ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Tab` | Enters the group at the selected item (or the first one). | | `Arrow Right/Down` | Selects the next item and moves focus. | | `Arrow Left/Up` | Selects the previous item and moves focus. | | `Space` | Selects the focused item. | There is one tab stop for the whole group, not one per item: that is the roving tabindex Base UI implements. ## Accessibility - The group renders `role="radiogroup"`; each item renders `role="radio"` with a hidden input, so the form still submits a value. - `aria-checked` carries the state on its own. The dot animation is never the only signal. - Name the group with `aria-labelledby` pointing at a visible heading, or with `aria-label` when a heading would be redundant. - `aria-invalid` belongs on the group: it describes the whole choice. ## Validation and data ownership | The component does | You do | | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | Styles and announces `aria-invalid` on the group | Deciding that a choice is required | | Forwards `name`, `required`, and the selection | Server-side validation of the submitted value | | Keeps arrow-key navigation within the group | Focus policy after a failed submit | There is no `validate` or `schema` prop. [Field](/components/field) shows how the invalid state and its message are wired. ## Responsive behavior Items stack by default (`grid gap-3`). For a horizontal row of short labels, set `className="flex flex-wrap gap-6"`; do not shorten the labels to fit — wrap them. ## Performance One Motion element per item, each animating only `opacity` and `transform`, and only when the selection changes. No layout thrash: the dot is absolutely sized by CSS, so no measurement happens. ## Notes for AI - Use `radio-group` for "one of N" and `checkbox` for "any of N". - Put `name` and `aria-invalid` on the group, not on the items. - Do not build a radio group out of buttons with `aria-pressed`; the radio role is what gives arrow-key navigation and form submission.
