items.name: slider
items.title: Slider
items.description: Volume, brightness, zoom, and price ranges.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/slider
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Slider } from "@/components/cadence/slider";

export function Volume() {
  return <Slider defaultValue={[60]} max={100} aria-label="Volume" />;
}
```

`defaultValue` and `value` accept a number for one thumb, or an array with one entry per thumb. `aria-label`
on the slider is forwarded to every thumb's native range input, which is what a
screen reader announces. A range slider gets one accessible name per thumb —
`Price (minimum)` and `Price (maximum)` — because two inputs with the same name
are indistinguishable.

## Controlled

```tsx
const [volume, setVolume] = useState([60]);

<Slider value={volume} onValueChange={setVolume} aria-label="Volume" />;
```

## Range

```tsx
<Slider defaultValue={[120, 480]} min={0} max={600} step={10} aria-label="Price" />
```

Two entries in the array give two thumbs; `minStepsBetweenValues` keeps them from
crossing.

## Vertical

```tsx
<Slider orientation="vertical" defaultValue={[40]} className="h-56" aria-label="Level" />
```

Give the vertical slider a height; the track fills it.

## Disabled

```tsx
<Slider defaultValue={[40]} disabled aria-label="Volume" />
```

## When to use

- A value where the rough position matters more than the exact number: volume,
  brightness, zoom, opacity.
- A range (two thumbs): price between, time window, budget band.
- A filter where the user should feel the bounds instead of typing them.

## When not to use

- An exact number matters and the range is wide; pair a `slider` with an `input`,
  or use `input` alone.
- Fewer than about five discrete options; use `radio-group` or `toggle-group`.
- A value with no natural order, like picking a colour name.

## API

| Prop                 | Type                              | Default        | Description                                     |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `value`              | `number \| readonly number[]`     | –              | Controlled value, one entry per thumb.          |
| `defaultValue`       | same as `value`                   | –              | Uncontrolled initial value.                     |
| `onValueChange`      | `(value, details) => void`        | –              | Fired while dragging and on keyboard steps.     |
| `min`, `max`         | `number`                          | `0`, `100`     | Bounds.                                         |
| `step`               | `number`                          | `1`            | Snap increment.                                 |
| `orientation`        | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"`      | `"horizontal"` | Axis.                                           |
| `disabled`           | `boolean`                         | `false`        | Ignores pointer and keyboard.                   |
| `aria-label`         | `string`                          | –              | Forwarded to each thumb, suffixed per thumb.    |
| `className`          | `string` / state callback                          | –              | Merged last.                                    |

Base UI's `format`, `locale`, and `minStepsBetweenValues` are forwarded unchanged.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `feedback.press`. The dragged thumb compresses to 0.97 and springs back on
release — the same press language as `button` and `toggle`.

| Phase   | Properties              | Token            | Interruptible |
| ------- | ----------------------- | ---------------- | ------------- |
| drag    | `scale 1 → 0.97`        | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| release | `scale 0.97 → 1`        | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| reduced | no scale; the ring grows on focus/hover | – | –             |
| none    | no scale                | –                | –             |

The fill is deliberately not animated: it is glued to the pointer, and a
transition would make it trail the thumb by one frame per move.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys                | Action                                  |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`               | Moves focus to the thumb.               |
| `Arrow Right/Up`    | Increases by one `step`.                |
| `Arrow Left/Down`   | Decreases by one `step`.                |
| `Page Up`/`Page Down` | Moves by a larger increment.           |
| `Home`/`End`        | Jumps to `min` / `max`.                 |

## Accessibility

- Every thumb contains a native `input[type=range]`, so the control works with
  assistive technology without a custom role.
- Always pass `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) — the fill has no text.
- Show the current value as text next to the slider when the number matters.
  Dragging is not a way to read a value.
- `aria-invalid` styles the control; validation is the caller's job (P11).

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                                | You do                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Reports the value through `onValueChange`         | Deciding whether the range is acceptable            |
| Styles `aria-invalid`                             | Writing the error text and its `aria-describedby` id |
| Steps and clamps the value to `min`/`max`         | Server-side bounds and business rules               |

[Field](/components/field) shows how the invalid state and its message are wired.

## Responsive behavior

Horizontal sliders fill their container (`w-full`); vertical ones fill their
height. On touch screens the thumb keeps a 16px visual size but the range input
covers the whole control, so drag targets stay reachable.

## Performance

The value updates on pointer move without React re-rendering the whole form: Base
UI moves the thumb with a CSS custom property, and Motion animates only the press
scale. No `layout` animation, no measurement per frame.

## Notes for AI

- A numeric value renders one thumb; an array renders one thumb per entry. Omitting both values retains the upstream two-thumb default.
- Do not animate the fill. Motion here is press feedback only.
- Pair with an `input` when the exact number must be typeable.

items.name: toggle
items.title: Toggle
items.description: Bold, italic, preview, and other on/off modes.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/toggle
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Bold } from "lucide-react";
import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle";

export function BoldToggle() {
  return (
    <Toggle aria-label="Bold" defaultPressed>
      <Bold />
    </Toggle>
  );
}
```

An icon-only toggle needs `aria-label`; the glyph is not a name.

## Variants and sizes

```tsx
<Toggle>Default</Toggle>
<Toggle variant="outline">Outline</Toggle>

<Toggle size="sm">Small</Toggle>
<Toggle size="lg">Large</Toggle>
```

`outline` gives the toggle a border, for toolbars that sit on a busy surface.

## With a label

```tsx
<Toggle variant="outline">
  <Bold />
  Bold
</Toggle>
```

`gap-2` is already in the base classes, so an icon and a label space themselves.

## Controlled

```tsx
const [on, setOn] = useState(false);

<Toggle pressed={on} onPressedChange={setOn} aria-label="Bold" />;
```

## Inside a form

```tsx
<Toggle name="bold" defaultPressed value="bold" />
```

A pressed toggle submits its `value`; an unpressed one submits nothing, like a
checkbox.

## When to use

- A formatting or mode command that stays on until it is turned off: bold,
  italic, a preview pane, a grid/list switch.
- A compact toolbar button whose pressed state is visible next to its neighbours.
- A setting the user toggles repeatedly while working.

## When not to use

- The action is one-shot (save, delete, open); use `button`.
- A setting that takes effect immediately and permanently, like a preference; use
  `switch`.
- A group of related toggles that should read as one control; use `toggle-group`.

## API

| Prop               | Type                          | Default     | Description                              |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `pressed`          | `boolean`                     | –           | Controlled state.                        |
| `defaultPressed`   | `boolean`                     | `false`     | Uncontrolled initial state.              |
| `onPressedChange`  | `(pressed, details) => void`  | –           | Fired on click and on Space/Enter.       |
| `variant`          | `"default" \| "outline"`      | `"default"` | Visual weight.                           |
| `size`             | `"sm" \| "default" \| "lg"`   | `"default"` | Height and minimum width.                |
| `disabled`         | `boolean`                     | `false`     | Ignores interaction.                     |
| `className`        | `string` / state callback                      | –           | Merged last.                             |

`toggleVariants` is exported, so a custom part can share the same classes.

The default press button preserves native React `onAnimationStart`, `onDrag`,
`onDragStart` and `onDragEnd` events, including capture and cancellation. Callback
and object refs follow the same button; replacing a callback runs its React 19
cleanup before assigning the next ref. A caller `render` replaces the default
renderer and owns spreading its supplied props.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `feedback.press`. The button compresses to 0.97 while the pointer is down
and springs back on release.

| Phase   | Properties       | Token            | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------------- | ---------------- | ------------- |
| press   | `scale 1 → 0.97` | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| release | `scale 0.97 → 1` | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| reduced | no scale; the pressed background is the only change | – | – |
| none    | no scale         | –                | –             |

The pressed background is a colour transition, which is state feedback and stays
in every mode — otherwise a `none` user could not see the state.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys    | Action                          |
| ------- | ------------------------------- |
| `Tab`   | Moves focus to the toggle.      |
| `Space` | Toggles the pressed state.      |
| `Enter` | Toggles the pressed state.      |

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders a real `<button type="button">` with `aria-pressed`, so assistive
  technology announces it as a toggle button, not a plain button.
- Icon-only toggles need `aria-label`; the pressed state is announced separately.
- The pressed state is never colour-only: the fill and `aria-pressed` change
  together, and the press scale is never the only feedback.
- Avoid toggles in a navigation bar; a link that changes style is still a link.

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                            | You do                                     |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Forwards `name`, `value`, `disabled`          | Deciding what a pressed toggle means       |
| Exposes `aria-invalid` styling                | Validation and error text                  |
| Keeps the pressed state in `aria-pressed`     | Persisting it                              |

[Field](/components/field) shows how the invalid state and its message are wired.

## Responsive behavior

Sizes are fixed; in a toolbar that must shrink, drop to `size="sm"` rather than
scaling the button with a transform, which would blur the icon.

## Performance

One Motion element, pressing only on pointer down. No layout animation, no
measurement.

## Notes for AI

- Use `toggle` for a command that stays on; use `switch` for a preference that
  saves itself.
- Always provide `aria-label` for icon-only toggles.
- Do not add a `state.morph` label swap to a toggle; the press scale is the whole
  contract.

items.name: toggle-group
items.title: Toggle Group
items.description: Text alignment, view density, and other mode sets.

props.reason: base defaults spacing to 2, new-york-v4 to 0. Cadence follows the visuals: 0 is the segmented control every shadcn example shows, and the gap is one prop away.

items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/toggle-group
```

Installing the group also installs `toggle`, because the items share its variant
classes.

## Usage

```tsx
import { AlignCenter, AlignLeft, AlignRight } from "lucide-react";
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group";

export function Alignment() {
  return (
    <ToggleGroup variant="outline" defaultValue={["left"]} aria-label="Text alignment">
      <ToggleGroupItem value="left" aria-label="Align left">
        <AlignLeft />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="center" aria-label="Align center">
        <AlignCenter />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="right" aria-label="Align right">
        <AlignRight />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
  );
}
```

## Multiple

```tsx
<ToggleGroup multiple defaultValue={["bold"]} aria-label="Text style">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="bold" aria-label="Bold">
    <Bold />
  </ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="italic" aria-label="Italic">
    <Italic />
  </ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>
```

Without `multiple`, pressing an item releases the others and the selected fill
slides to it. Pressing the selected item again clears the selection, matching
Base UI. With `multiple`, fills fade and settle independently; adjacent pressed
items join into one shape when `spacing={0}`.

## Segmented

Use `variant="segmented"` for a pill-shaped track with a raised selection fill.
This is a Toggle Group variant, with the same parts, array value and keyboard
behavior as the toolbar variants.

```tsx
const [range, setRange] = useState(["week"]);

<ToggleGroup
  variant="segmented"
  value={range}
  onValueChange={(next) => {
    if (next.length) setRange(next);
  }}
  aria-label="Time range"
>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="day">Day</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="week">Week</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="month">Month</ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>;
```

Ignoring an empty array makes a controlled selection required. The visual
variant does not silently change selection semantics or activate items on focus.

## Spacing

```tsx
<ToggleGroup variant="outline" spacing={0} aria-label="Range">
  …
</ToggleGroup>

<ToggleGroup variant="outline" spacing={1} aria-label="Range">
  …
</ToggleGroup>
```

`spacing={0}` joins adjacent pressed fills in a multiple group; a positive value
keeps them apart in Tailwind spacing steps. The strip keeps its outer surface in
both cases. Single selection slides between items at either spacing.

## Vertical

```tsx
<ToggleGroup orientation="vertical" aria-label="Zoom">
  …
</ToggleGroup>
```

## Controlled

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState(["center"]);

<ToggleGroup value={value} onValueChange={setValue} aria-label="Alignment">
  …
</ToggleGroup>;
```

The value is always an array, even without `multiple`.

## When to use

- A small set of modes that belong to one control: text alignment, view density,
  a time range.
- A formatting toolbar where several marks can be active at once
  (`multiple`).
- Icon toolbars with a shared tinted fill (`default` or `outline`), or short text
  choices on a pill-shaped track (`segmented`).

## When not to use

- Exactly one option with a text label and a longer list; use `radio-group`, which
  exposes radio semantics rather than a row of toggle buttons.
- A single independent on/off command; use `toggle`.
- Navigation between pages; use `tabs`, which owns `role="tablist"`.

## API

### `ToggleGroup`

| Prop            | Type                                        | Default        | Description                              |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `readonly string[]`                         | –              | Controlled pressed values.               |
| `defaultValue`  | `readonly string[]`                         | `[]`           | Uncontrolled initial values.             |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string[], details) => void`        | –              | Fired when any item changes.             |
| `multiple`      | `boolean`                                   | `false`        | Allow more than one pressed item.        |
| `spacing`       | `number`                                    | `0`            | Gap in Tailwind spacing steps.           |
| `orientation`   | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"`                | `"horizontal"` | Axis, also drives arrow keys.            |
| `variant`       | `"default" \| "outline" \| "segmented"`     | `"default"`    | Shared strip, bordered strip, or pill track. |
| `size`          | `"sm" \| "default" \| "lg"`                 | `"default"`    | Inherited by every item.                 |

### `ToggleGroupItem`

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                          |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `value`     | `string` | –       | Required. Identifies the item.       |
| `disabled`  | `boolean`| `false` | Keeps it visible but unpressable.    |
| `className` | `string` / state callback | –       | Merged last.                         |

The default press button preserves native React `onAnimationStart`, `onDrag`,
`onDragStart` and `onDragEnd` events, including capture and cancellation. Callback
and object refs follow the same button; replacing a callback runs its React 19
cleanup before assigning the next ref. A caller `render` replaces the default
renderer and owns spreading its supplied props.

## Motion contract

Single selection uses one shared decorative fill scoped to each group. Multiple
selection keeps one local fill per item. Neither changes the buttons' layout
boxes; corner changes that join neighboring fills are immediate state styling.

| Phase   | Properties       | Token            | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------------- | ---------------- | ------------- |
| press   | `scale 1 → 0.97` | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| release | `scale 0.97 → 1` | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| single selection | fill transform between items | `layout.shared` | yes |
| multiple selection | fill opacity and `scale 0.96 → 1` | `state.morph` | yes |
| reduced | shared fill jumps; local fills fade; no press scale | – | – |
| none | immediate selection, opacity and press state; zero duration | – | – |

Press scale applies only to the content, keeping the button and decorative fill
in the group's common stacking context. A travelling fill stays below all labels
and icons, including the items it crosses and the focused destination.

Full mode uses the velocity-preserving shared spring. Reduced, none and a zero
recipe clock render a static single-selection fill, cancelling an in-flight
projection without replacing the focused button. Local fills keep opacity under
reduced and settle immediately under none. All animated parts expose
`data-motion`; every duration, scale and spring comes from Cadence tokens.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys               | Action                                        |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`              | Enters the group at the last pressed item.    |
| `Arrow Right/Down` | Moves focus to the next item.                 |
| `Arrow Left/Up`    | Moves focus to the previous item.             |
| `Space` / `Enter`  | Presses the focused item.                     |

With `loopFocus` (default) the arrows wrap around at the ends.

## Accessibility

- The group renders `role="group"`; each item is a `<button>` with `aria-pressed`.
- Name the group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` — a row of icon buttons
  with no group name is announced as unrelated buttons.
- Icon-only items need their own `aria-label`; the group name does not describe
  them.
- Do not use a toggle group where `role="tablist"` is correct; tabs imply a panel
  that is shown, a toggle group implies state.
- Selection fills are decorative (`aria-hidden`) and never receive focus.

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                              | You do                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Forwards `disabled` and the pressed values      | Deciding whether a selection is required  |
| Renders the visual pressed state                | Persisting the choice                     |
| Exposes `aria-invalid` styling on items         | Validation and error text                 |

[Field](/components/field) shows how the invalid state and its message are wired.

## Responsive behavior

Horizontal groups do not wrap; with more than about five items on a narrow screen,
switch to `orientation="vertical"` or replace the group with a `select`.

## Performance

One shared layout identity per single-selection group; Motion measures the fill
when selection changes. Multiple selection uses one local opacity/scale fill per
item. Press feedback stays on demand. No observers, timers or render-time layout
reads; use small option sets rather than long lists.

## Notes for AI

- `value` is an array in every mode, with or without `multiple`.
- Use `variant="segmented"` for a pill-shaped control; no separate component is needed.
- Use `multiple` for independent pressed fills; `spacing={0}` joins neighbors.
- To require a selection, control the value and ignore empty change requests.
- For "one of N" with text labels, prefer `radio-group`; for panels, `tabs`.

items.name: input-otp
items.title: Input OTP
items.description: Login codes, email verification, and device pairing.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/input-otp
```

The component wraps [`input-otp`](https://github.com/guilhermerodz/input-otp),
which owns the single hidden input, paste handling, and the caret position.

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  InputOTP,
  InputOTPGroup,
  InputOTPSeparator,
  InputOTPSlot,
} from "@/components/cadence/input-otp";

export function Code() {
  return (
    <InputOTP maxLength={6} aria-label="Verification code">
      <InputOTPGroup>
        <InputOTPSlot index={0} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={1} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={2} />
      </InputOTPGroup>
      <InputOTPSeparator />
      <InputOTPGroup>
        <InputOTPSlot index={3} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={4} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={5} />
      </InputOTPGroup>
    </InputOTP>
  );
}
```

`maxLength` must equal the number of slots. Each `InputOTPSlot` needs its `index`.

## Controlled, with completion

```tsx
const [code, setCode] = useState("");

<InputOTP maxLength={6} value={code} onChange={setCode} onComplete={verify}>
  …
</InputOTP>;
```

`onComplete` fires once the last slot is filled. It is the right place to submit
the code, not an effect that watches `code.length`.

## Invalid

```tsx
<InputOTP maxLength={4} aria-label="Code" aria-invalid>
  <InputOTPGroup>
    <InputOTPSlot index={0} aria-invalid />
    …
  </InputOTPGroup>
</InputOTP>
```

`aria-invalid` on a slot styles its border; the text beside the field carries the
message.

## Disabled

```tsx
<InputOTP maxLength={6} disabled aria-label="Code">
  …
</InputOTP>
```

## Without a separator

```tsx
<InputOTP maxLength={4} aria-label="PIN" containerClassName="justify-center">
  <InputOTPGroup>
    <InputOTPSlot index={0} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={1} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={2} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={3} />
  </InputOTPGroup>
</InputOTP>
```

## When to use

- A short code the user reads from another surface: a login code, an email
  verification, a device pairing code.
- Anywhere a single input would force the user to count characters.
- A code that arrives by SMS or authenticator app, where `autocomplete="one-time-code"`
  lets the OS offer it.

## When not to use

- A password the user chooses; use `input type="password"`.
- A long token that is pasted, not typed; use `input` with paste handling.
- A numeric field that is not a code, like a quantity; use `input type="number"`.

## API

### `InputOTP`

| Prop               | Type                        | Default | Description                                    |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `maxLength`        | `number`                    | –       | Required. Number of characters.                |
| `value`            | `string`                    | –       | Controlled value.                              |
| `defaultValue`     | `string`                    | –       | Uncontrolled initial value.                    |
| `onChange`         | `(value: string) => void`   | –       | Fired on every change, including paste.        |
| `onComplete`       | `(value: string) => void`   | –       | Fired when the code is full.                   |
| `disabled`         | `boolean`                   | `false` | Ignores input.                                 |
| `containerClassName` | `string`                  | –       | Classes for the wrapper that positions the slots. |
| `className`        | `string`                    | –       | Classes for the input itself.                  |

### `InputOTPSlot`

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                          |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `index`     | `number` | –       | Required. Which character it shows.  |
| `className` | `string` | –       | Merged last.                         |

`InputOTPGroup` and `InputOTPSeparator` are plain wrappers with `data-slot` values
`input-otp-group` and `input-otp-separator`.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `state.morph`. A character lands in its slot with a short fade and settles
from 0.96 to full size. Deleting a character is instant — an exit animation would
leave a ghost in a field the user is racing against.

| Phase   | Properties                        | Token         | Interruptible |
| ------- | --------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| type    | `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` | `state.morph` | yes           |
| delete  | none (instant)                    | –             | –             |
| reduced | `opacity` only                    | `state.morph` | yes           |
| none    | no transition                     | –             | –             |

The character span stays mounted when its value changes; updates replay the recipe on that same node. Mode changes cancel the running entry, and `none` renders filled slots immediately, including on the first render.

The caret is drawn but does not blink. A blink is a continuous loop that would
have to be declared as `data.transition`; the active slot's ring already shows
where the next character goes, so the loop buys nothing.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys              | Action                                                    |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Any character     | Fills the active slot and advances.                       |
| `Backspace`       | Clears the current slot, then moves back.                 |
| `Arrow Left/Right`| Moves the active slot without changing the value.         |
| `Cmd/Ctrl + V`    | Pastes the whole code, filling every slot from the start. |

## Accessibility

- `input-otp` renders a single real input with `aria-label` and
  `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so assistive technology sees one field, not six.
- The slots are visual mirrors; they are not focusable and carry no role.
- `onComplete` is where the code is judged. The component never decides that a
  code is wrong.
- Keep the field visible while verifying and announce the result next to it, not
  through the slots' animation.

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                                  | You do                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Styles `aria-invalid` on the slots                  | Deciding that the code is wrong or expired        |
| Reports every change and the completed value        | Verifying the code and mapping the server error   |
| Keeps the paste path working                        | Re-sending a code, throttling attempts            |

There is no `validate`, `schema`, or `rules` prop. [Field](/components/field) shows how the
invalid state and its message are wired.

## Responsive behavior

Slots are 36px squares; six of them plus a separator fit a 320px viewport. For
longer codes, drop the separator group or reduce the gap in `containerClassName`
before shrinking the slots below 32px.

## Performance

One Motion element per slot, animating `opacity` and `transform` only when a
character changes. No per-keystroke layout read: the caret position comes from the
input, not from measurement.

## Notes for AI

- `maxLength` and the slot count must agree; a mismatch silently drops characters.
- Use `onComplete` to submit, not an effect that watches `value.length`.
- The caret does not blink on purpose. Do not re-add a `animate-caret-blink`
  loop without declaring the recipe.

items.title: Progress
items.description: Uploads, imports, and other work with a measurable end.
items.docs:
## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/progress ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Progress } from "@/components/cadence/progress"; export function Upload() { return ; } ``` `value` is required and may be `null` for indeterminate work. `Progress` renders its own track and indicator; `ProgressLabel` and `ProgressValue` go inside it as children. ## Labelled, with the number ```tsx
Uploading assets
``` `ProgressValue` formats the value with `Intl.NumberFormat`; pass `format` or `locale` to the root to change it. ## Indeterminate ```tsx ``` The fill fills the track and pulses. There is no sweep: a moving gradient says "indeterminate" with motion alone, which is exactly the anti-pattern in the motion system. ## Custom range ```tsx ``` `ProgressValue` renders `60%` for `3/5`; use `getAriaValueText` if you want "step 3 of 5" announced instead. ## Composed track ```tsx ``` This adds a composed track alongside the default track, matching the upstream root composition. The indicator still reads the value from the root, so it keeps animating. ## When to use - Work with a measurable end: an upload, an import, a multi-step build. - Work long enough that the user would otherwise wonder whether anything is happening, and short enough that they will watch the bar. - A determinate value next to other numbers, where the bar is a second reading of the same fact. ## When not to use - Work of unknown duration. Pass `value={null}` for an indeterminate bar, or use `spinner` when there is no bar to fill. - A page that is simply loading its own content; use `skeleton`. - A value that is not progressing toward an end, like a score. Render the number. ## API ### `Progress` | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ----------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- | | `value` | `number \| null` | – | Required. `null` means indeterminate. | | `min`, `max` | `number` | `0`, `100` | Range. | | `format` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` | – | How `ProgressValue` formats the number. | | `getAriaValueText`| `(value, raw) => string` | – | Human-readable value for assistive tech. | | `className` | `string` / state callback | – | Merged last; the default is a wrap layout. | ### `ProgressTrack`, `ProgressIndicator`, `ProgressLabel`, `ProgressValue` Plain wrappers over Base UI's parts; each forwards `className` and native props. `ProgressIndicator` carries the motion. ## Motion contract Recipe: `data.transition`, in both of its documented forms. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------- | ------------- | | value change | `scaleX old → new` (one-shot) | `data.transition`| yes | | indeterminate | `opacity` pulse (continuous) | `data.transition`| yes | | reduced | value jumps; pulse kept, opacity only | `data.transition` | yes | | none | no transition, `animate-none` | – | – | The fill is a `scaleX` transform on an element that keeps the full track width, so a value change never triggers layout. Under `reduced` the fill jumps to the new value — position is information, the animation is not — while the indeterminate pulse survives, because opacity-only loading feedback is what M5 keeps. ## Keyboard interactions No keyboard interaction: the progress bar is not focusable. If the user can cancel the work, put a `button` next to it. ## Accessibility - Base UI puts `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuenow` on the root; `value={null}` omits `aria-valuenow`. - Give it a name with `aria-label`, or render `ProgressLabel` inside the root and let Base UI wire it. - Announce completion outside the bar (text or `toast`); a full bar is not announced by a screen reader on its own. - Never hide the percentage behind the animation: `ProgressValue` is the readable copy of the same fact. ## Responsive behavior The bar fills its container and stays 8px tall at every breakpoint. When it sits in a card header, keep the label and value on one line and let the bar take the next line — the default `flex-wrap` layout does this without extra classes. ## Performance One Motion element. A determinate update animates a transform; an indeterminate bar runs a CSS opacity loop that the compositor owns, so a page with several bars does not schedule main-thread frames. Avoid driving `value` from `requestAnimationFrame` yourself; pass the real value and let the transition smooth it. ## Notes for AI - `value` is required; pass `null` for indeterminate, never `undefined`. - Use `scaleX`, not width. A width transition relayouts the track every frame. - For work with no measurable end and no bar, use `spinner`, not a fake percentage.

items.name: alert-dialog
items.title: Alert Dialog
items.description: Destructive or irreversible actions that need confirmation.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/alert-dialog
```

This also installs `button`, which the two actions render through.

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/alert-dialog";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function DeleteProject() {
  return (
    <AlertDialog>
      <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Delete project</AlertDialogTrigger>
      <AlertDialogContent>
        <AlertDialogHeader>
          <AlertDialogTitle>Delete this project?</AlertDialogTitle>
          <AlertDialogDescription>
            Every deployment and its logs go with it. This cannot be undone.
          </AlertDialogDescription>
        </AlertDialogHeader>
        <AlertDialogFooter>
          <AlertDialogCancel>Keep project</AlertDialogCancel>
          <AlertDialogAction variant="destructive">Delete project</AlertDialogAction>
        </AlertDialogFooter>
      </AlertDialogContent>
    </AlertDialog>
  );
}
```

## A compact confirmation

`size="sm"` caps the panel at `max-w-xs` and turns the footer into a two-column grid, which is what a
yes/no question looks like. The dialog is centred and its header is centred with it.

```tsx
<AlertDialogContent size="sm">
  <AlertDialogHeader>
    <AlertDialogTitle>Archive this project?</AlertDialogTitle>
    <AlertDialogDescription>It stops deploying. You can unarchive it later.</AlertDialogDescription>
  </AlertDialogHeader>
  <AlertDialogFooter>
    <AlertDialogCancel>Cancel</AlertDialogCancel>
    <AlertDialogAction>Archive</AlertDialogAction>
  </AlertDialogFooter>
</AlertDialogContent>
```

## With an icon

`AlertDialogMedia` is a slot, not a decoration: put an icon in it and the header switches to the
left-aligned, icon-first layout on `size="default"`.

```tsx
<AlertDialogHeader>
  <AlertDialogMedia>
    <Trash2 aria-hidden="true" />
  </AlertDialogMedia>
  <AlertDialogTitle>Delete this project?</AlertDialogTitle>
  <AlertDialogDescription>Every deployment goes with it.</AlertDialogDescription>
</AlertDialogHeader>
```

## Controlled

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<AlertDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <AlertDialogContent>…</AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>;
```

## A confirmation that is still working

The component never owns a request. The caller passes the in-flight state, and the library keeps the
button a button:

```tsx
<AlertDialogAction disabled={isDeleting} onClick={() => mutate()}>
  {isDeleting ? "Deleting…" : "Delete project"}
</AlertDialogAction>
```

## When to use

- A destructive or irreversible action — deleting a project, revoking a key, overwriting a draft — that the
  user must confirm on purpose.
- A decision the page cannot make for the user: move the workspace, leave without saving, end the session.
- A step that must be acknowledged before anything else continues, where an accidental dismissal would be
  the bug.

## When not to use

- A task with more than one decision or a form to fill in. Use `dialog`: it can be dismissed, and it should be.
- A message that does not block anything. Use `alert` where it belongs on the page, or `toast` for a moment.
- A hint attached to a control. Use `tooltip`.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AlertDialog` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `onOpenChangeComplete` | Base UI root. Always modal; pointer dismissal is fixed off. |
| `AlertDialogTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the dialog. |
| `AlertDialogContent` | `size` (`"default" \| "sm"`), `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay, and popup. |
| `AlertDialogOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `AlertDialogContent`. |
| `AlertDialogHeader` / `AlertDialogFooter` | `className` | Layout only. |
| `AlertDialogMedia` | `className` | Icon slot; changes the header layout. |
| `AlertDialogTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. |
| `AlertDialogDescription` | `className` | Supporting text; wire it to the decision, not the product. |
| `AlertDialogAction` | `variant`, `size`, `onClick`, `render` | Confirming Button. The caller owns closing via the root’s controlled `open` value. |
| `AlertDialogCancel` | `variant` (`outline`), `size`, `onClick`, `render` | Dismissing button. Also closes the dialog. |

`AlertDialogCancel` renders Base UI’s Close. `AlertDialogAction` matches the pinned upstream
Button: clicking it invokes the caller’s handler and leaves the popup open. Use controlled
`open` / `onOpenChange` to close when the caller decides the action is complete.

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | overlay `opacity 0 → 1`; panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` / `duration.base` | yes |
| exit | overlay `opacity → 0`; panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` / `duration.base` | yes (reopen mid-exit) |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (overlay 96ms, panel 132ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so no transition runs | – | – |

The entrance is the dialog's, because this is the same popup: a fade under a 0.96-scale settle. The
motion is CSS-only — Base UI toggles `data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style` and the class list
reads the duration tokens — so there is no JavaScript animation loop and nothing to interrupt by hand.
Reopening during the exit reverses the fade rather than restarting it.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside the dialog. Focus never reaches the page behind it. |
| Escape | Cancels: the dialog closes and focus returns to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused button — confirm or cancel, whichever has focus. |

The outside press is the one path that is deliberately missing: clicking the overlay does nothing,
which is the difference between this component and `dialog`.

## Accessibility

The destructive action uses foreground text on a tinted destructive background. This preserves the warning colour while meeting text contrast in both themes.

- Base UI provides `role="alertdialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, focus
  trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and the Escape path.
- `AlertDialogTitle` is required: an alert dialog without an accessible name is invalid, and it is
  announced as the first thing inside the popup. `AlertDialogDescription` becomes the description, so
  put the consequence there, not in a second paragraph.
- Focus lands on the cancel control, the first tabbable element inside the popup, not on the destructive
  action — so a stray Enter cancels rather than confirms. Put `AlertDialogCancel` first in the footer for
  that reason; the footer's column-reverse layout still shows the confirming action on top.
- Destructive styling is colour plus a specific verb ("Delete project", not "OK"). Never rely on the
  red alone; the label has to carry the meaning in greyscale and in a screen reader.
- `AlertDialogMedia` is decorative when the title already says what happened. Mark the icon
  `aria-hidden="true"` unless it is the only signal.

## Responsive behavior

The panel is centred with a 1rem gutter on narrow viewports: `max-w-lg` for the default size and
`max-w-xs` for `size="sm"`. The footer stacks its buttons in reverse DOM order (the confirming action
on top) below `sm`, and becomes a row that ends on the right above it. With `size="sm"` the two
buttons split the width instead of stacking, so the two answers stay side by side at every size.

## Performance

- One popup tree is mounted only while open; the overlay and panel unmount after the exit transition.
- Animates `opacity` and `scale` only: no layout reads, no `width`/`height` transition, and no
  JavaScript animation running while the dialog sits open.
- `AlertDialogAction` and `AlertDialogCancel` are ordinary `Button`s, so the press feedback is the
  button's (a 0.97 scale that the same motion mode can drop).

## Notes for AI

- Reach for `alert-dialog` only when the answer must be deliberate. A form, a longer task, or anything
  the user may want to dismiss belongs in `dialog`.
- Always render `AlertDialogTitle`; it is the accessible name. Use `AlertDialogDescription` for the
  consequence of the action, in one sentence.
- Name the confirming button after its effect ("Delete project", "Leave without saving"), never "OK".
- Cancel closes automatically. The confirming Action stays open; use the root’s controlled `open` value when the caller decides to close.
- Use `AlertDialogMedia` for an icon, not for an illustration: the slot is a 4rem square that changes
  the header layout.

items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/tooltip
```

Optionally wrap the app in `TooltipProvider` once to set one delay for every tooltip; Base UI does not
require it.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipProvider, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tooltip";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function BoldTooltip() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider delay={200}>
      <Tooltip>
        <TooltipTrigger render={<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" />} aria-label="Bold">
          <Bold />
        </TooltipTrigger>
        <TooltipContent>Bold (⌘B)</TooltipContent>
      </Tooltip>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

## Side and alignment

`side` defaults to `top` and the label flips when there is no room. The arrow moves with it; the panel
grows out of `--transform-origin`, so the scale starts where the trigger meets the label.

```tsx
<TooltipContent side="right" align="start">
  Right, aligned to the start
</TooltipContent>
```

## A delay for the whole app

`TooltipProvider` sets the delay once. Without it, Base UI's own default applies.

```tsx
<TooltipProvider delay={300}>
  <App />
</TooltipProvider>
```

## Disabled controls

A disabled button does not emit pointer events, so wrap it and put the hint on the wrapper:

```tsx
<Tooltip>
  <TooltipTrigger render={<span className="inline-flex" />}>
    <Button disabled>Deploy</Button>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipContent>Finish the required fields first</TooltipContent>
</Tooltip>
```

## When to use

- An icon-only control whose meaning is not obvious from the icon alone.
- The full value behind a truncated label, or a keyboard shortcut next to an action.
- A hint that helps the first use of a dense control and is useless once learned.

## When not to use

- Anything the user must read to act: a tooltip disappears on scroll, touch, and Escape. If the content
  matters, put it on the page or in a `popover`.
- Interactive content. A tooltip cannot hold a button or a link; use `popover`.
- The accessible name of a button that already has text. Two labels that disagree is worse than one.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TooltipProvider` | `delay` | Optional. One delay for every tooltip inside. |
| `Tooltip` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | Base UI root. |
| `TooltipTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Hover or focus target; carries `aria-describedby`. |
| `TooltipContent` | `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, positioner, popup, and arrow. `side` defaults to `top`, `sideOffset` to `4`. |

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | label `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` from the anchor origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| exit | label `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (96ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the label appears on the first frame | – | – |

A tooltip is small enough that `duration.fast` is already at the edge of readable: nothing here waits
for an exit to finish. The arrow is part of the popup and moves with it, so it is never animated
separately.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focus shows the label; leaving hides it. |
| Escape | Hides the label and leaves focus on the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the trigger. The tooltip does not swallow the press. |

Hover alone is never the only path: the tooltip opens on keyboard focus too, which is what makes it
usable on touch and from a screen reader.

## Accessibility

- Base UI's own tooltip adds neither `role="tooltip"` nor `aria-describedby`; Cadence wires both. The
  trigger points at the popup only while it is open — a closed popup would otherwise leave a dangling
  id, which axe reports — and the popup is `role="tooltip"`.
- The tooltip must not be the only name of a control. Give an icon button a real `aria-label`; the
  tooltip is the extra sentence, not the name.
- Text stays readable in both themes: `bg-foreground` / `text-background` invert, so the label keeps
  contrast against whatever surface it floats over.
- Escape dismisses it without moving focus, so a tooltip never traps a keyboard user.

## Responsive behavior

The label is `w-fit` with a `max-w-xs` cap and wraps at word boundaries (`text-balance`) instead of
running off screen. Base UI flips the side and shifts the alignment when the viewport cannot fit it.

## Performance

- The popup tree is mounted only while the label is open; a page can carry dozens of tooltips without
  paying for them all.
- Animates `opacity` and `scale` only — no layout read, no measuring loop, no JavaScript animation.
  Hover is not a state the component polls.

## Notes for AI

- Use a tooltip to name or explain a control, never to deliver information the user needs to proceed.
- Do not put a link, button, or form inside it; use `popover`.
- Give every icon-only trigger an `aria-label`: the tooltip complements the name, it does not replace it.

items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/drawer
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Drawer,
  DrawerClose,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerDescription,
  DrawerFooter,
  DrawerHeader,
  DrawerTitle,
  DrawerTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/drawer";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function MoveConversation() {
  return (
    <Drawer showSwipeHandle>
      <DrawerTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Move conversation</DrawerTrigger>
      <DrawerContent>
        <DrawerHeader>
          <DrawerTitle>Move conversation</DrawerTitle>
          <DrawerDescription>Drag down to dismiss, or pick a destination.</DrawerDescription>
        </DrawerHeader>
        {/* the destinations */}
        <DrawerFooter>
          <DrawerClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Cancel</DrawerClose>
        </DrawerFooter>
      </DrawerContent>
    </Drawer>
  );
}
```

## A visible swipe handle

`showSwipeHandle` draws the handle that says "drag me". It is `aria-hidden`: the drag is an accelerator,
never the only way out — the close controls and Escape still work.

```tsx
<Drawer showSwipeHandle>…</Drawer>
```

## Swiping from another edge

`swipeDirection` moves the sheet, its placement, and the direction it closes in. The default is `"down"`.

```tsx
<Drawer swipeDirection="right">…</Drawer>
<Drawer swipeDirection="up">…</Drawer>
```

## Snap points

`snapPoints` lets the sheet rest at more than one height; the peek is the smallest value. The overlay
stays in step with the swipe, so the page behind returns as the sheet travels.

```tsx
<Drawer snapPoints={[0.5, 1]}>…</Drawer>
```

## Non-modal

A drawer that should not lock the page passes `modal={false}`; the backdrop is skipped and the page
stays interactive.

```tsx
<Drawer modal={false}>…</Drawer>
```

## When to use

- A short task opened from the bottom of the screen, where the thumb is: move to, share, quick actions.
- A list or explanation that the page behind should stay visible for — a bottom sheet covers the bottom,
  not the context.
- A panel the user expects to swipe away, because that is how sheets behave on touch devices.

## When not to use

- A decision that must be answered. Use `alert-dialog`; a drawer can be dragged shut.
- A hint on a control. Use `tooltip` or `hover-card`.
- A long multi-step flow. Use a page or a `sheet` with a footer; dragging half-way through a form is a
  worse experience than a full surface.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Drawer` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal`, `snapPoints`, `swipeDirection`, `showSwipeHandle` | `showSwipeHandle` is additive; `swipeDirection` defaults to `"down"` and `modal` to `true`. |
| `DrawerTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the drawer. |
| `DrawerContent` | `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay (when modal), viewport, popup, and content. |
| `DrawerOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `DrawerContent`. |
| `DrawerSwipeHandle` | `className` | The handle; rendered for you when `showSwipeHandle` is set. |
| `DrawerClose` | native button props, `render` | Closes the drawer. |
| `DrawerHeader` / `DrawerFooter` | `className` | Stacking and spacing only. |
| `DrawerTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. |
| `DrawerDescription` | `className` | Supporting text. |

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | sheet `opacity 0 → 1` + `transform` from `--closed-transform`; backdrop `opacity 0 → 1` | `popup.anchored` · `duration.slow` / `duration.fast` | yes |
| drag | `transform` follows `--drawer-swipe-movement-*`; backdrop opacity is `1 - --drawer-swipe-progress` | Base UI gesture (no authored recipe) | yes (it is the gesture) |
| exit | sheet back to `--closed-transform` + `opacity → 0`; backdrop `opacity → 0` | `exit.fade` · `duration.slow` / `duration.fast` | yes |
| reduced | fade only: the closed-state slide is dropped, so the sheet appears and disappears in place | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the sheet is in place on the first frame | – | – |

The drag keeps tracking the finger under `reduced`: that movement is the user's own, not authored motion,
and a sheet that ignored the drag would be worse than one that follows it. The release animation uses the
token duration rather than a velocity-scaled one — the swipe physics decide *where* the sheet settles,
the token decides how long the settle takes.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside a modal drawer. |
| Escape | Closes the drawer and returns focus to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused control. |

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`, focus
  trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and Escape handling while the drawer is modal.
- `DrawerTitle` is required: a drawer without an accessible name is invalid.
- The swipe handle is `aria-hidden="true"` and is never the only way out. A user who cannot drag gets
  the close controls, Escape, and the overlay press (for a modal drawer).
- The content region scrolls on its own (`overflow-y-auto`), so a long list inside the sheet does not
  move the page behind it.

## Responsive behavior

The default sheet sits at the bottom, spans the width, and caps its height at `calc(100dvh - 3rem)` so a
strip of the page stays visible. `swipeDirection="left"` / `"right"` becomes a side panel at `w-3/4`,
capped at `max-w-sm` from `sm` up. Snap points change the resting height without changing any of that
geometry.

## Performance

- The drag writes CSS variables and a `transform`; it never touches layout or React state per frame.
- The backdrop opacity is a `calc()` on the same variable, so the page behind dims as the sheet moves
  without a second animation.
- Entry and exit animate `transform` and `opacity` only. Nothing is measured during render.

## Notes for AI

- Use `drawer` for a short touch-first task from the bottom edge; use `sheet` for a side panel that
  holds a form, and `alert-dialog` when the answer must be deliberate.
- Always render `DrawerTitle`. `DrawerDescription` is the second line of the announcement.
- Never make the swipe the only dismissal: keep a `DrawerClose`, and let Escape work.
- For a list of actions, each row is a `DrawerClose` so choosing one closes the sheet.
