items.title: Combobox
items.description: Picking from a long list you can filter by typing.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/combobox
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxEmpty,
  ComboboxInput,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxList,
} from "@/components/cadence/combobox";

const frameworks = ["Next.js", "SvelteKit", "Nuxt.js", "Remix", "Astro"];

export function FrameworkPicker() {
  return (
    <Combobox items={frameworks}>
      <ComboboxInput placeholder="Select a framework" aria-label="Framework" />
      <ComboboxContent>
        <ComboboxEmpty>No framework found.</ComboboxEmpty>
        <ComboboxList>
          {(item) => (
            <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
              {item}
            </ComboboxItem>
          )}
        </ComboboxList>
      </ComboboxContent>
    </Combobox>
  );
}
```

`ComboboxList` takes a render function, so the list is data, not markup: `items` on the root is what the
popup filters and what the render callback receives.

## Groups and separators

Long catalogues read better in labelled groups. Give each `ComboboxGroup` its own `items` so filtering
can drop a group as a whole.

```tsx
<Combobox items={groups}>
  <ComboboxInput placeholder="Assign reviewer" aria-label="Reviewer" />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxEmpty>No reviewer found.</ComboboxEmpty>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(group) => (
        <ComboboxGroup key={group.value} items={group.items}>
          <ComboboxLabel>{group.value}</ComboboxLabel>
          {group.items.map((item) => (
            <ComboboxItem key={item.value} value={item}>
              {item.label}
            </ComboboxItem>
          ))}
        </ComboboxGroup>
      )}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>
```

## Clear and trigger controls

`showClear` adds the undo affordance once a value is set; the chevron steps aside while both would be
fighting for the same 24px. Turn the chevron off entirely with `showTrigger={false}` when the field is
inside a form that submits on Enter.

```tsx
<Combobox items={frameworks} defaultValue="Astro">
  <ComboboxInput showClear placeholder="Select a framework" aria-label="Framework" />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(item) => (
        <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
          {item}
        </ComboboxItem>
      )}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>
```

## Multiple values

`multiple` turns the field into a tag editor: `ComboboxChips` is the frame, each `ComboboxChip` is a
value, and `ComboboxChipsInput` is the caret. Anchor the popup to the chips container so it lines up with
the field rather than with the input inside it.

```tsx
const anchor = useComboboxAnchor();

<Combobox multiple items={topics} defaultValue={["design"]}>
  <ComboboxChips ref={anchor}>
    <ComboboxValue>
      {(value: string[]) => (
        <React.Fragment>
          {value.map((topic) => (
            <ComboboxChip key={topic}>{topic}</ComboboxChip>
          ))}
          <ComboboxChipsInput placeholder="Add topic" aria-label="Topics" />
        </React.Fragment>
      )}
    </ComboboxValue>
  </ComboboxChips>
  <ComboboxContent anchor={anchor}>
    <ComboboxEmpty>No topic found.</ComboboxEmpty>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(item) => (
        <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
          {item}
        </ComboboxItem>
      )}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>;
```

## Filtering a server list

For a remote catalogue, keep the list the server returned and hand it to `items`; Base UI filters what it
is given, so a new response replaces the list without the component deciding what to fetch.

```tsx
const [results, setResults] = useState<string[]>([]);

<Combobox items={results} onInputValueChange={(query) => search(query).then(setResults)}>
  <ComboboxInput placeholder="Search a city" aria-label="City" />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxEmpty>No city found.</ComboboxEmpty>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(item) => (
        <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
          {item}
        </ComboboxItem>
      )}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>;
```

## When to use

- Choosing one value from a list too long to scan: countries, assignees, repositories.
- A search field that should also accept a typed value, for example a tag the catalogue does not list.
- Several values from the same catalogue, where each choice should stay visible as a chip.
- A picker whose options arrive from a search endpoint rather than from a constant.

## When not to use

- Fewer than about eight fixed options. Use `select`; a popup that has to be opened to show three items is
  slower than three radios.
- Commands rather than values — navigation, actions, "go to file". Use `command`.
- Free text with no catalogue behind it. Use `input`.
- A control that must not accept typing, such as a language picker in a settings form. Use `select`.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Combobox` | `items`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `multiple`, `disabled`, `name`, `required`, `onInputValueChange`, `itemToStringLabel` | Base UI root. `items` drives what the popup filters and what the render callbacks receive. |
| `ComboboxInput` | `showTrigger` (`true`), `showClear` (`false`), `disabled`, native input props | The field: a bare input inside an input-group frame, with the chevron and the optional clear button. |
| `ComboboxTrigger` | native button props | The chevron on its own, for a field built by hand. |
| `ComboboxValue` | render callback or children | The selected label; in the chips layout it renders the chips. |
| `ComboboxContent` | `side` (`"bottom"`), `sideOffset` (`6`), `align` (`"start"`), `alignOffset` (`0`), `anchor` | Portals, positions, and sizes to `--anchor-width`. |
| `ComboboxList` | children or render function `(item, index) => ReactNode` | Scrolls, and takes the height the popup has left. |
| `ComboboxItem` | `value`, `disabled` | Renders the label and the tick. |
| `ComboboxGroup` / `ComboboxLabel` | `items` on the group | Structural; the group's `items` let filtering drop it whole. |
| `ComboboxEmpty` | children | Shown when the filter matches nothing. |
| `ComboboxSeparator` | separator props | A hairline between unrelated groups. |
| `ComboboxChips` / `ComboboxChip` / `ComboboxChipsInput` | `showRemove` (`true`) on the chip | The multi-value layout. |
| `ComboboxCollection` | collection props | Escape hatch for virtualised lists. |
| `useComboboxAnchor` | – | A ref to anchor the popup to the chips frame. |

`ComboboxClear` is internal on purpose: it belongs to `ComboboxInput`'s layout, and a component that owns
an undo affordance should not also hand out half of one.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | popup `opacity` 0→1, `scale` `--motion-scale-in`→1 | `popup.anchored` | yes: a CSS transition, so reopening reverses it |
| close | popup `opacity` 1→0 | `exit.fade` | yes |
| select | tick `scale` `0.96`→1, `opacity` 0→1 | `state.morph` | yes: a spring, retargeted from the current value |
| filter | none — rows are replaced, not moved | – | – |
| reduced | popup fades without scaling, tick appears at full size | – | – |
| none | every duration is zero | – | – |

The scale grows out of `--transform-origin`, which Base UI writes from the positioner, so the panel opens
from the field rather than from its own centre. The list itself never animates: a filter runs on every
keystroke, and a row that is still travelling when the next character arrives is a list the reader has to
chase.

Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside
`none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel
geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the
first mounted frame. The preview's **Popup motion** selector changes the local mode on the
same component tree. Base UI `className(state)` and `style(state)` callbacks are evaluated
before merging; caller utilities and styles win. Native `render`, events and ref cleanup
remain owned by the primitive. Base UI 1.9's typeable focus manager hides background
nodes from assistive technology while leaving their tab stops enabled. Cadence adds native
temporary negative tab indices only to newly hidden focus stops, preserving outside pointer activation; Tab releases them before normal focus navigation and
Base UI's blur dismissal. Existing hidden/inert nodes and parent dialogs keep their owners; cleanup preserves caller tabindex changes. `ComboboxInput` string classes style the field frame;
state callback classes style the native input with its real Base UI input state.

## Keyboard interactions

- `ArrowDown` or `Alt+ArrowDown` opens the popup; with it open, `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move the highlight.
- Typing filters the list and moves the highlight to the first match.
- `Enter` selects the highlighted item and closes the popup.
- `Escape` closes the popup without choosing anything; the typed query stays in the field.
- `Tab` closes the popup and moves focus to the next control.
- `Backspace` in the chips layout deletes the last chip when the input is empty.

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders the input as a `combobox` with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, and
  `aria-activedescendant`, and the list as a `listbox` whose rows are `option`s.
- Name the field: `aria-label` on `ComboboxInput`, or a `Field`/`Label` pair around it. The placeholder is
  not a name.
- The selected row keeps `aria-selected="true"`; the tick is a visual duplicate, never the only signal.
- The empty state is a row inside the list, so it is reachable in the reading order and not a modal
  interruption.
- Under reduced motion nothing is conveyed by the panel's scale: the list is there, the tick is at full
  size, and `aria-selected` carries the state.

## Validation and data ownership

The caller owns selection values, validation, error text, submission and any remote
loading/filtering. Render supplied aria-invalid/data-invalid and associate described
errors; this component does not validate or install a form-state library.

## Responsive behavior

The popup is exactly `--anchor-width` wide and at least `--spacing(7)` wider than the field, so a narrow
trigger still shows a readable row. It flips above the field near the viewport edge, and the list — not the
popup — scrolls inside `--available-height`. In the chips layout the frame wraps to a second line instead
of scrolling horizontally, and the popup widens to the chips container.

## Performance

- One CSS transition on `opacity` and `scale` per open and per close; no JS animation loop, and no layout
  read.
- One spring per selected row. The indicator is mounted once and animated in place, so filtering does not
  create and destroy an animation per item.
- The filter is synchronous over whatever `items` holds; a remote list is a debounce in the caller, not a
  behaviour of this component.
- Budget: T2 (10 KB gzip).

## Notes for AI

- Always pass `items` to `Combobox`; it drives filtering and is what the `ComboboxList` render callback
  receives. Without it the list renders nothing.
- Use `value`/`onValueChange` for a controlled picker, `defaultValue` otherwise — same contract as `select`.
- `multiple` requires the chips layout; do not pair `multiple` with a plain `ComboboxInput`.
- Do not add a "loading" prop: async feedback is the caller's state, and `ComboboxEmpty` is for an empty
  result, not for a pending one.
- For invalid state pass `aria-invalid` on `ComboboxInput`; the frame styles the border and the ring from
  the attribute.

items.name: dropdown-menu
items.title: Dropdown Menu
items.description: Row actions, filters, and view settings behind one button.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/dropdown-menu
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function RowActions() {
  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Actions</DropdownMenuTrigger>
      <DropdownMenuContent align="start">
        <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => rename()}>Rename</DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => duplicate()}>Duplicate</DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  );
}
```

## Items, shortcuts, and destructive actions

An item is a `menuitem`: it runs, then the menu closes. `DropdownMenuShortcut` is a
right-aligned hint only — the component binds no keys, so register the shortcut yourself.
`variant="destructive"` colours the label and its icons; `inset` indents an item to line up
with one that has a check mark.

```tsx
<DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => edit()}>
  Edit
  <DropdownMenuShortcut>⌘E</DropdownMenuShortcut>
</DropdownMenuItem>
<DropdownMenuSeparator />
<DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={() => remove()}>
  Delete
  <DropdownMenuShortcut>⌘⌫</DropdownMenuShortcut>
</DropdownMenuItem>
```

## Checkbox and radio items

Both keep the menu open, so a user can set several options in one visit. The mark is the
item's state, not a second control: `aria-checked` carries it for assistive technology, and
the mark scales in as confirmation.

```tsx
<DropdownMenuCheckboxItem defaultChecked onCheckedChange={setDescription}>
  Description
</DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>

<DropdownMenuRadioGroup value={density} onValueChange={setDensity}>
  <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="compact">Compact</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
  <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="comfortable">Comfortable</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
</DropdownMenuRadioGroup>
```

## Submenus

A submenu is a menu anchored to its trigger item. It opens on hover after the pointer rests,
on `ArrowRight`, and on click; `DropdownMenuSubContent` takes the same placement props as the
top-level panel, with `side="right"` as the default.

```tsx
<DropdownMenuSub>
  <DropdownMenuSubTrigger>Move to</DropdownMenuSubTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuSubContent>
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => move("backlog")}>Backlog</DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => move("review")}>In review</DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuSubContent>
</DropdownMenuSub>
```

## Grouping

`DropdownMenuGroup` binds a `DropdownMenuLabel` to the items it holds: the group is labelled
by it, so a screen reader announces "Pull request, group". A label outside a group is a
plain caption above the items, which is what most toolbars want.

```tsx
<DropdownMenuGroup>
  <DropdownMenuLabel>Pull request</DropdownMenuLabel>
  <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => edit()}>Edit</DropdownMenuItem>
  <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => duplicate()}>Duplicate</DropdownMenuItem>
</DropdownMenuGroup>
```

## Controlled open

`open` and `onOpenChange` make the menu controlled, which is how a menu is opened from
outside its trigger — a keyboard shortcut, a row's context, a tour step.

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<DropdownMenu open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Actions</DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent>…</DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>;
```

## When to use

- A row of actions behind one trigger: a table row, a card, a file.
- A filter or view setting where the panel stays open while several options change.
- A command list too long for a toolbar and too short to need search.

## When not to use

- A list of links to another page. Use a `navigation-menu` or plain links: an item that
  navigates is a link, and a menu item is not one.
- A value you select and read back. Use `select`, which keeps the chosen value in the trigger.
- A destructive answer that must be confirmed. Use `alert-dialog`; a menu item is a
  one-keystroke action and closes immediately.
- More than about a dozen entries, or entries the user has to search. Use `command`.

## API

### `DropdownMenu`

| Prop           | Type                       | Default | Description                                     |
| -------------- | -------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `open`         | `boolean`                  | –       | Controlled open state.                          |
| `defaultOpen`  | `boolean`                  | `false` | Uncontrolled initial state.                     |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void`  | –       | Fires on every open and close, including Escape. |
| `modal`        | `boolean`                  | `true`  | Traps focus and makes the page inert while open. |

### `DropdownMenuTrigger`

Native button props and `render`. The trigger owns `aria-haspopup="menu"` and
`aria-expanded`; pass a `Button` through `render` rather than wrapping one, so those land on
the element the user presses.

### `DropdownMenuContent`

| Prop          | Type                                          | Default    | Description                                    |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `side`        | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"`      | `"bottom"` | Preferred side; flips when there is no room.   |
| `align`       | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"`                 | `"start"`  | Alignment along the trigger's edge.            |
| `sideOffset`  | `number`                                      | `4`        | Gap between trigger and panel, in pixels.       |
| `alignOffset` | `number`                                      | `0`        | Shift along the alignment axis.                 |
| `className`   | string or Base UI state callback                                      | –          | Merged last.                                    |

### `DropdownMenuItem`, `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`, `DropdownMenuRadioItem`

| Part                     | Props                                                              | Notes                                             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `DropdownMenuItem`       | `onClick`, `disabled`, `inset`, `variant`, `closeOnClick`            | `variant`: `"default" \| "destructive"`.          |
| `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` | `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange`, `inset`            | Keeps the menu open.                              |
| `DropdownMenuRadioGroup` | `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`                            | One selection for the group.                      |
| `DropdownMenuRadioItem`  | `value` (required), `disabled`, `inset`                             | Keeps the menu open.                              |
| `DropdownMenuSub`        | –                                                                  | Groups a submenu trigger and its content.         |
| `DropdownMenuSubTrigger` | `disabled`, `inset`                                                | Renders the chevron.                              |
| `DropdownMenuSubContent` | Same as `DropdownMenuContent`                                      | `side="right"`, `alignOffset={-3}` by default.    |

### `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuLabel`, `DropdownMenuSeparator`

`DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuLabel`, `DropdownMenuSeparator`,
`DropdownMenuShortcut`, `DropdownMenuPortal`.

## Motion contract

| Phase         | Properties                                        | Token             | Interruptible                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------- |
| open          | panel `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` from the trigger origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes (reopen mid-exit) |
| close         | panel `opacity → 0`, `scale → 0.96`               | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes                |
| check / radio | mark `opacity` + `scale`                          | `state.morph`     | yes                          |
| reduced       | panel fades, no scale; the mark cross-fades at full size | `exit.fade` | yes                         |
| none          | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`; the mark jumps | –      | –                            |

Opening and closing are one CSS transition on `opacity` and `scale`, driven by Base UI's
`data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style`, so an interrupted close reverses rather than
restarts. The panel grows out of `--transform-origin`, which Base UI points at the trigger;
a submenu grows out of its item the same way, because both levels render the same panel.

The highlighted row is a colour change, not motion: `data-highlighted` switches the item's
background. A travelling highlight would be a shared element across items — `layout.move`,
which belongs to `tabs` and `toggle-group`, not to a menu that can be entered at any row.

Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside
`none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel
geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the
first mounted frame. The preview's **Popup motion** selector changes the local mode on the
same component tree. Base UI `className(state)` and `style(state)` callbacks are evaluated
before merging; caller utilities and styles win. Native `render`, events and ref cleanup
remain owned by the primitive.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys                      | Action                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter` / `Space` / `ArrowDown` | Opens the menu and highlights the first item.                 |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp`   | Moves the highlight; it wraps at the ends.                          |
| `Home` / `End`            | First and last item.                                                |
| Typeahead letters         | Highlights the next item whose label starts with them.              |
| `Enter` / `Space`         | Runs the highlighted item and closes the menu.                      |
| `ArrowRight`              | Opens the highlighted submenu; `ArrowLeft` closes it.               |
| `Escape`                  | Closes the menu, returns focus to the trigger, runs nothing.        |
| `Tab`                     | Closes the menu and moves to the next control in the page.          |

## Accessibility

- Base UI wires the trigger with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`, and renders the
  panel as `role="menu"` with `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox`, and `menuitemradio` parts.
- A menu item is not a link. If an entry navigates, render an anchor inside it
  (`render={<a href="…" />}` on a `MenuItem` still needs the role, so prefer a plain link).
- `DropdownMenuLabel` inside a `DropdownMenuGroup` is the group's accessible name. Outside a
  group it is a caption: visible to sighted users, not announced as a label.
- `DropdownMenuShortcut` is text, not a binding. Announce the shortcut in the item's label
  only when it is registered, or the reader is told about a key that does nothing.
- The menu is modal by default: the page behind it is inert while it is open, so a stray
  `Tab` cannot reach a control the user cannot see.

## Responsive behavior

The panel caps at `--available-height` and scrolls, and the positioner flips the side and
shifts along the cross axis to stay inside the viewport. On touch, the menu opens on tap and
the highlighted item follows the tap; there is no hover state to design around. `min-w-[8rem]`
keeps short menus readable, and the panel does not stretch to the trigger's width — a menu
is as wide as its widest item.

## Performance

- One portal per open menu; closing unmounts it after the exit transition.
- The panel animates `opacity` and `scale` only, on one element. Nothing measures layout, and
  no JavaScript runs per frame.
- Items carry no per-item motion: the only animated state is the check mark, and it animates
  two properties on a 14px span.
- Budget: T2 (10 KB gzip). A page with a dozen closed menus pays for one component's source,
  no mounted popups, and no timers.

## Notes for AI

- Put the action on `onClick`. Base UI's menu item has no `onSelect`; a handler that only
  exists on `onSelect` never fires.
- Pass the trigger through `render` so `aria-haspopup` lands on the button, not on a wrapper.
- Group items before labelling them: a `DropdownMenuLabel` outside a `DropdownMenuGroup` is a
  caption, and a group without a label is announced as an unnamed group.
- Do not put a form with validation inside a menu. A menu is a list of commands; `popover`
  is the surface for controls.

The popup owns its `duration.fast` clock, including provider timeScale and the
reduced duration multiplier. An explicit full provider restores the clock inside
an outer none scope. In none mode the popup removes starting/ending opacity and
uses zero duration on the first frame. Function-valued popup `className` and
`style` receive Base UI state and merge after the component defaults.

items.name: context-menu
items.title: Context Menu
items.description: Right-click actions on a file, row, or canvas.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/context-menu
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  ContextMenu,
  ContextMenuContent,
  ContextMenuItem,
  ContextMenuTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/context-menu";

export function FileContextMenu({ file }: { file: File }) {
  return (
    <ContextMenu>
      <ContextMenuTrigger tabIndex={0} className="flex h-32 items-center justify-center rounded-lg border border-dashed text-sm">
        {file.name}
      </ContextMenuTrigger>
      <ContextMenuContent>
        <ContextMenuItem onClick={() => open(file)}>Open</ContextMenuItem>
        <ContextMenuItem onClick={() => rename(file)}>Rename</ContextMenuItem>
      </ContextMenuContent>
    </ContextMenu>
  );
}
```

## Where the panel opens

The menu opens at the pointer, not under an edge of the trigger, so `side` and `align`
describe the fallback used when the pointer is near a viewport edge. The defaults —
`side="right"`, `alignOffset={4}` — place the panel just clear of the cursor.

```tsx
<ContextMenuContent side="bottom" align="center" alignOffset={12}>
  …
</ContextMenuContent>
```

## Beside a row menu

A context menu and a `dropdown-menu` on the same row answer the same question twice, and
users expect the same entries in both. Render the item list once and pass it to both:

```tsx
const actions = (
  <>
    <ContextMenuItem onClick={() => open(file)}>Open</ContextMenuItem>
    <ContextMenuItem onClick={() => rename(file)}>Rename</ContextMenuItem>
  </>
);

<ContextMenu>
  <ContextMenuTrigger>{file.name}</ContextMenuTrigger>
  <ContextMenuContent>{actions}</ContextMenuContent>
</ContextMenu>;
```

## Selection items

`ContextMenuCheckboxItem` and `ContextMenuRadioGroup` / `ContextMenuRadioItem` keep the panel
open, so a user can set options without reopening it. `ContextMenuShortcut` is a
right-aligned hint; the component binds no keys.

```tsx
<ContextMenuCheckboxItem defaultChecked onCheckedChange={setHidden}>
  Hidden files
</ContextMenuCheckboxItem>

<ContextMenuRadioGroup value={sort} onValueChange={setSort}>
  <ContextMenuRadioItem value="name">Name</ContextMenuRadioItem>
  <ContextMenuRadioItem value="date">Date modified</ContextMenuRadioItem>
</ContextMenuRadioGroup>
```

## Submenus

```tsx
<ContextMenuSub>
  <ContextMenuSubTrigger>Open with</ContextMenuSubTrigger>
  <ContextMenuSubContent>
    <ContextMenuItem onClick={() => openWith("editor")}>Editor</ContextMenuItem>
    <ContextMenuItem onClick={() => openWith("preview")}>Preview</ContextMenuItem>
  </ContextMenuSubContent>
</ContextMenuSub>
```

## When to use

- A canvas, map, or list of files where the object itself is the target.
- A table row with more actions than fit in a cell.
- A destructive action that should be one gesture away, not one visible button.

## When not to use

- An action a user needs to discover. A context menu is invisible until someone
  right-clicks; put the primary action in the row and keep the menu for the rest.
- A single toggle. Use a `checkbox` or `switch` that is always visible.
- The same list on a touch device only: a long-press competes with scroll and text
  selection. Keep a visible `dropdown-menu` as well.

## API

### `ContextMenu`

`open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` (default `true`).

### `ContextMenuTrigger`

Native div props and `render`. The trigger is the area that listens for `contextmenu` and
long-press; it renders a `div` by default, so give it the box you want to be right-clickable.

### `ContextMenuContent`

| Prop          | Type                                     | Default     | Description                                   |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `side`        | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"` | `"right"`   | Fallback side when the pointer is at an edge. |
| `align`       | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"`            | `"start"`   | Alignment along that side.                    |
| `sideOffset`  | `number`                                 | `0`         | Gap from the pointer.                         |
| `alignOffset` | `number`                                 | `4`         | Shift along the alignment axis.               |
| `className`   | string or Base UI state callback                                 | –           | Merged last.                                  |

### `ContextMenuItem`, `ContextMenuCheckboxItem`, `ContextMenuRadioItem`

`ContextMenuItem` (`onClick`, `disabled`, `inset`, `variant`), `ContextMenuCheckboxItem`,
`ContextMenuRadioGroup`, `ContextMenuRadioItem`, `ContextMenuSub`, `ContextMenuSubTrigger`,
`ContextMenuSubContent` — the same parts and props as `dropdown-menu`, with context-menu
slots.

### `ContextMenuGroup`, `ContextMenuLabel`, `ContextMenuSeparator`

`ContextMenuGroup`, `ContextMenuLabel`, `ContextMenuSeparator`, `ContextMenuShortcut`,
`ContextMenuPortal`.

## Motion contract

| Phase         | Properties                                        | Token             | Interruptible |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------- |
| open          | panel `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` from the pointer | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| close         | panel `opacity → 0`, `scale → 0.96`               | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| check / radio | mark `opacity` + `scale`                          | `state.morph`     | yes           |
| reduced       | panel fades, no scale; the mark cross-fades at full size | `exit.fade` | yes           |
| none          | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`; the mark jumps | –      | –             |

The panel grows out of the point that was pressed. That is the whole reason the recipe is
anchored rather than centred: a context menu belongs to the place it was summoned, and a
scale from the pointer says so without moving the panel.

Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside
`none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel
geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the
first mounted frame. The preview's **Popup motion** selector changes the local mode on the
same component tree. Base UI `className(state)` and `style(state)` callbacks are evaluated
before merging; caller utilities and styles win. Native `render`, events and ref cleanup
remain owned by the primitive.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys                      | Action                                                        |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Shift+F10` / Context Menu key | Opens the menu at the focused element.                   |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp`   | Moves the highlight.                                          |
| Typeahead letters         | Highlights the next item starting with them.                  |
| `Enter` / `Space`         | Runs the highlighted item.                                    |
| `ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft` | Opens or closes a submenu.                                   |
| `Escape`                  | Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.             |

## Accessibility

- The trigger keeps the browser's own `contextmenu` event: the menu opens from the keyboard
  with `Shift+F10` or the dedicated key, which is what a screen reader user presses.
- The panel is `role="menu"` and the items are `menuitem` / `menuitemcheckbox` /
  `menuitemradio`, so "right-click for options" is announced as a menu, not as a tooltip.
- On touch, Base UI opens the menu on a long press and cancels it if the finger moves —
  which is why the same actions must also be reachable from a visible control.
- Focus returns to the trigger on close, so a keyboard user does not lose their place.

## Responsive behavior

The panel flips to the side with room and shifts along the cross axis to stay inside the
viewport, so a right-click near the bottom-right corner opens up and to the left. On a
narrow screen it caps at `--available-height` and scrolls rather than overflowing.

## Performance

- One portal while open, one CSS transition on `opacity` and `scale`, no per-frame work.
- The trigger adds one listener, not one per item: Base UI handles the event at the root.
- Budget: T2 (10 KB gzip). The item and submenu parts share their classes with
  `dropdown-menu` but not its file, so the two install independently.

## Notes for AI

- Use `onClick` for the action; there is no `onSelect` on Base UI's menu item.
- Do not hide the only path to an action behind a context menu — pair it with a visible
  control, because a context menu is undiscoverable and unavailable on most touch flows.
- `ContextMenuTrigger` is the right-click area, so its content is what the user aims at;
  avoid making the whole page a trigger.

items.name: menubar
items.title: Menubar
items.description: Application menus along the top of a window.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/menubar
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Menubar,
  MenubarContent,
  MenubarItem,
  MenubarMenu,
  MenubarTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/menubar";

export function EditorMenubar() {
  return (
    <Menubar>
      <MenubarMenu>
        <MenubarTrigger>File</MenubarTrigger>
        <MenubarContent>
          <MenubarItem onClick={() => save()}>Save</MenubarItem>
          <MenubarItem onClick={() => publish()}>Publish…</MenubarItem>
        </MenubarContent>
      </MenubarMenu>
      <MenubarMenu>
        <MenubarTrigger>Edit</MenubarTrigger>
        <MenubarContent>
          <MenubarItem onClick={() => undo()}>Undo</MenubarItem>
        </MenubarContent>
      </MenubarMenu>
    </Menubar>
  );
}
```

## Moving between menus

Once a menu is open, `ArrowRight` and `ArrowLeft` switch to the neighbouring top-level menu
without closing the bar. That traversal is the reason to use `menubar` over three
`dropdown-menu`s: the menus know about each other.

```tsx
<Menubar>
  <MenubarMenu>…</MenubarMenu>
  <MenubarMenu>…</MenubarMenu>
  <MenubarMenu>…</MenubarMenu>
</Menubar>
```

## Shortcuts and groups

`MenubarShortcut` right-aligns a key hint, and `MenubarGroup` with `MenubarLabel` splits a
long menu into named sections.

```tsx
<MenubarGroup>
  <MenubarLabel>Export</MenubarLabel>
  <MenubarItem onClick={() => exportAs("pdf")}>
    PDF
    <MenubarShortcut>⇧⌘P</MenubarShortcut>
  </MenubarItem>
  <MenubarItem onClick={() => exportAs("png")}>
    PNG
    <MenubarShortcut>⇧⌘E</MenubarShortcut>
  </MenubarItem>
</MenubarGroup>
```

## Selection items and submenus

The selection parts are the menu's: a checkbox item keeps the panel open while the state
changes, and a submenu opens to the right of the item it belongs to.

```tsx
<MenubarCheckboxItem defaultChecked onCheckedChange={setSidebar}>
  Sidebar
</MenubarCheckboxItem>

<MenubarSub>
  <MenubarSubTrigger>Theme</MenubarSubTrigger>
  <MenubarSubContent>
    <MenubarRadioGroup value={theme} onValueChange={setTheme}>
      <MenubarRadioItem value="light">Light</MenubarRadioItem>
      <MenubarRadioItem value="dark">Dark</MenubarRadioItem>
    </MenubarRadioGroup>
  </MenubarSubContent>
</MenubarSub>
```

## When to use

- A desktop-style application shell with a menu across the top.
- A documentation tool or editor where File / Edit / View are the mental model.
- A dense toolbar whose commands need names, shortcuts, and grouping.

## When not to use

- A web page's main navigation. Use links or `navigation-menu`: a menu bar hides its
  destinations behind a click.
- One trigger with a list of actions. Use `dropdown-menu`.
- Commands a user reaches for a dozen times a minute. First-class buttons beat two clicks.

## API

`Menubar` takes `modal` (default `true`), `disabled`, and `orientation` (default
`"horizontal"`). Every other part mirrors `dropdown-menu` under menubar slots:

| Part                                                                                  | Notes                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MenubarMenu`                                                                         | One top-level menu; wraps the trigger and its content.    |
| `MenubarTrigger`                                                                      | The label in the bar. Opens on click, `Enter`, `ArrowDown`. |
| `MenubarContent`                                                                      | The panel: `min-w-[12rem]`, `sideOffset={8}`, `alignOffset={-4}`. |
| `MenubarItem`                                                                         | `onClick`, `inset`, `variant`.                            |
| `MenubarCheckboxItem` / `MenubarRadioGroup` / `MenubarRadioItem`                        | Selection that keeps the panel open.                      |
| `MenubarSub` / `MenubarSubTrigger` / `MenubarSubContent`                                | A nested menu.                                           |
| `MenubarGroup` / `MenubarLabel` / `MenubarSeparator` / `MenubarShortcut` / `MenubarPortal` | Structure.                                            |

## Motion contract

| Phase         | Properties                                     | Token             | Interruptible |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------- |
| open          | panel `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` from the trigger | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| close         | panel `opacity → 0`, `scale → 0.96`            | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| check / radio | mark `opacity` + `scale`                       | `state.morph`     | yes           |
| reduced       | panel fades, no scale; the mark cross-fades    | `exit.fade`       | yes           |
| none          | every duration resolves to `0ms`               | –                 | –             |

The bar itself does not animate. Switching from one open menu to the next replaces one panel
with another; there is no shared element between them, and a highlight sliding along the bar
would suggest a continuity the markup does not have.

Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside
`none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel
geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the
first mounted frame. The preview's **Popup motion** selector changes the local mode on the
same component tree. Base UI `className(state)` and `style(state)` callbacks are evaluated
before merging; caller utilities and styles win. Native `render`, events and ref cleanup
remain owned by the primitive.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys                        | Action                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight`  | Moves between top-level menus; while open, opens the neighbour. |
| `ArrowDown` / `Enter`       | Opens the focused menu and highlights its first item.          |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown`     | Moves the highlight inside an open menu.                       |
| `Home` / `End`              | First and last item.                                           |
| `Escape`                    | Closes the menu and returns focus to its trigger.              |
| `Tab`                       | Leaves the bar for the next control in the page.               |

## Accessibility

- The root is `role="menubar"` with `aria-orientation`; each trigger is `aria-haspopup="menu"`
  and reports `aria-expanded`, so the bar announces its structure rather than a row of
  buttons that happen to open panels.
- Roving focus keeps one tab stop for the whole bar: `Tab` enters it once and leaves it once,
  which is what makes a menu bar usable without forty presses.
- `MenubarLabel` inside a `MenubarGroup` is that group's accessible name.
- Shortcut hints are text. Register the keys yourself, or a screen reader will announce a
  shortcut that does nothing.

## Responsive behavior

A menubar is a desktop pattern: on a narrow viewport the triggers wrap inside the bordered
bar rather than scrolling horizontally. For touch, prefer `dropdown-menu` behind a single
trigger, or a `navigation-menu`; long-pressing a menu bar is not a gesture anyone expects.

## Performance

- One portal per open menu; a closed bar mounts only its triggers.
- No motion on the bar itself, and the open panel is the same `opacity` + `scale` transition
  as every other popup in the library.
- Budget: T2 (10 KB gzip). The item parts come from `dropdown-menu` through a
  `registryDependencies` entry, so the two install once and the menu behaviour is one file.

## Notes for AI

- Use `menubar` only for an application shell. For a site's navigation, links are the
  correct element and `navigation-menu` is the right component.
- Wrap each top-level menu in `MenubarMenu`; a bare `MenubarTrigger` has no menu to open.
- Keep the bar to a handful of menus. Each one is a click away from invisible content.

items.name: code-block
items.title: Code block
items.description: Install commands, source snippets, and tool output.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/code-block
```

The block installs `button` for the copy and fold controls, and `code-highlight` — the Shiki adapter — for syntax
colouring. That second item is only downloaded when a block actually asks for a `language`.

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  CodeBlock,
  CodeBlockActions,
  CodeBlockContent,
  CodeBlockCopyButton,
  CodeBlockHeader,
  CodeBlockTitle,
} from "@/components/cadence/code-block";

const install = `npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/code-block`;

export function Install() {
  return (
    <CodeBlock language="bash">
      <CodeBlockHeader>
        <CodeBlockTitle>Terminal</CodeBlockTitle>
        <CodeBlockActions>
          <CodeBlockCopyButton value={install} />
        </CodeBlockActions>
      </CodeBlockHeader>
      <CodeBlockContent>{install}</CodeBlockContent>
    </CodeBlock>
  );
}
```

## Line numbers

`lineNumbers` splits a string child into lines and numbers them from `startLine`. The gutter is a `::before` on
each line, so the numbers are not part of a selection and do not travel with copied text.

```tsx
<CodeBlockContent lineNumbers startLine={42}>
  {snippetFromTheMiddleOfAFile}
</CodeBlockContent>
```

## Diff

Map each line to a `CodeBlockLine` and pick its variant. `added` and `removed` carry a `+` / `−` marker as well as
a tint, so the diff survives a monochrome screen and a colour-blind reader.

```tsx
<CodeBlockContent lineNumbers>
  <CodeBlockLine variant="removed">const chunks = await reader.read();</CodeBlockLine>
  <CodeBlockLine variant="added">for await (const chunk of reader) {"{"}</CodeBlockLine>
  <CodeBlockLine>{"  controller.enqueue(chunk);"}</CodeBlockLine>
  <CodeBlockLine variant="added">{"}"}</CodeBlockLine>
</CodeBlockContent>
```

`highlighted` marks a line to call out without claiming it changed.

## Folding a long file

`maxLines` on `CodeBlock` caps the block; `CodeBlockExpandButton` unfolds it. Both are additive props — upstream
shadcn leaves the fold to the consumer, and that composition still works if you would rather wire your own
control to `expanded` / `onExpandedChange`.

```tsx
<CodeBlock maxLines={12}>
  <CodeBlockHeader>
    <CodeBlockTitle>app/api/chat/route.ts</CodeBlockTitle>
    <CodeBlockActions>
      <CodeBlockCopyButton value={source} />
    </CodeBlockActions>
  </CodeBlockHeader>
  <CodeBlockContent lineNumbers>{source}</CodeBlockContent>
  <CodeBlockFooter className="justify-center">
    <CodeBlockExpandButton />
  </CodeBlockFooter>
</CodeBlock>
```

The button renders nothing while the content fits, so a short file never grows a dead control. The fold is
measured from the rendered content, so it follows wrapped lines and whatever font size the page sets.

## Tool output

Output is not source: it wraps instead of scrolling sideways, and it is smaller. Use `variant="destructive"` when
the run failed rather than recolouring the text yourself.

```tsx
<CodeBlock variant="destructive" size="sm">
  <CodeBlockHeader>
    <CodeBlockTitle>run_shell</CodeBlockTitle>
  </CodeBlockHeader>
  <CodeBlockContent wrap className="max-h-64">
    {stderr}
  </CodeBlockContent>
</CodeBlock>
```

## Floating actions

Put `CodeBlockActions` directly inside `CodeBlock`, with no header, and it floats over the top-end corner. It is
revealed on hover and on focus, and it is permanently visible on a device that cannot hover.

```tsx
<CodeBlock>
  <CodeBlockActions>
    <CodeBlockCopyButton value={output} />
  </CodeBlockActions>
  <CodeBlockContent>{output}</CodeBlockContent>
</CodeBlock>
```

## Switching between variants

A snippet often has more than one right form: the same install for three package managers, a source file and
its compiled output, a component and its test. `CodeBlockTabs` is the tab list over the source, `CodeBlockTab`
is one tab, and `CodeBlockPanel` is the source that tab shows.

The selection lives on `CodeBlock`, not on the tab list, because the header's copy button has to follow it: give
`CodeBlockCopyButton` `values` instead of `value` and it copies whichever variant is on screen — a switcher whose
copy button still copies the first command is worse than no switcher.

```tsx
const install = {
  pnpm: "pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @cadence/code-block",
  npm: "npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/code-block",
  yarn: "yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @cadence/code-block",
};

<CodeBlock defaultTab="pnpm">
  <CodeBlockHeader>
    <CodeBlockTabs label="Package manager">
      <CodeBlockTab value="pnpm">pnpm</CodeBlockTab>
      <CodeBlockTab value="npm">npm</CodeBlockTab>
      <CodeBlockTab value="yarn">yarn</CodeBlockTab>
    </CodeBlockTabs>
    <CodeBlockActions>
      <CodeBlockCopyButton values={install} />
    </CodeBlockActions>
  </CodeBlockHeader>
  <CodeBlockPanel value="pnpm">{install.pnpm}</CodeBlockPanel>
  <CodeBlockPanel value="npm">{install.npm}</CodeBlockPanel>
  <CodeBlockPanel value="yarn">{install.yarn}</CodeBlockPanel>
</CodeBlock>
```

Four things worth knowing:

- **The pill is a shared element.** Only the selected tab renders one, and Motion matches the two `layoutId`s,
  so it travels to the tab that was pressed rather than a second pill cross-fading in place. Press another tab
  mid-flight and it retargets instead of restarting. The labels stay above it, so the pill crosses underneath
  the neighbouring tabs instead of wiping the label of the tab it left.
- **A panel is the content.** `CodeBlockPanel` renders `CodeBlockContent` and takes its props (`wrap`,
  `lineNumbers`, `language`), so a tabbed block keeps the fold, the numbering, the copy affordance and the focus
  ring a plain block has.
- **Panels are hidden, not unmounted.** Every variant stays in the tree behind the `hidden` attribute: a tab
  switch is a look at what is already there, so it cannot lose the reader's scroll position, and only the visible
  source is focusable.
- **The height is the selected panel's.** It changes instantly — the size of the block is information, and the
  one layout animation on this component is the fold. Keep variants that differ by a line or two in the same
  block; a tab that doubles the height wants two blocks.

`defaultTab` is uncontrolled; `tab` with `onTabChange` drives it from outside when the surrounding page has its
own idea of which variant is current.

## Highlighting

Set `language` and a string child is tokenized; leave it out and the same child renders as plain text, which is
what tool output wants. The tokenizer is [Shiki](https://shiki.style) in its JavaScript-regex mode, imported
**dynamically**: a block without a `language` never downloads it, and a block with one downloads a single chunk
plus the grammar for that language.

```tsx
<CodeBlock language="tsx">
  <CodeBlockContent lineNumbers>{source}</CodeBlockContent>
</CodeBlock>
```

Bundled languages: `bash` (`sh`, `shell`, `zsh`), `css`, `diff`, `html`, `javascript` (`js`), `json`, `jsx`,
`markdown` (`md`), `python` (`py`), `sql`, `tsx`, `typescript` (`ts`), `yaml` (`yml`). An unknown language is not
an error — the source stays plain. Add one by adding a row to `languages` in `code-highlight/highlight.tsx`.

Two things are worth knowing about how it behaves:

- **Colours are CSS variables, not fixed hex.** Each token carries `--shiki-light` and `--shiki-dark`, and the
  span reads whichever one the current theme sets. Switching to dark re-colours the block without re-tokenizing.
  The two themes are the **high-contrast** GitHub pair, chosen in the same file if you want your own: the plain
  `github-light` paints parameters in orange at 3.5:1 on white, which fails WCAG AA on any block with a function
  signature.
- **Streaming tokenizes once per line.** The hook keeps the grammar state after the last complete line, so an
  assistant appending a token re-tokenizes the line being written, not the block. Finished lines keep their nodes
  — React does not re-render them.

The first paint is plain: the highlighter is a separate chunk, so it arrives after hydration. If a flash of
uncoloured code is not acceptable, highlight on the server and pass the nodes in — the same tokenizer is exported
as a plain async function for exactly that:

```tsx
// Server Component: Shiki never reaches the client bundle.
const lines = (await highlightCode(source, "tsx")) ?? [source];

<CodeBlockContent lineNumbers>
  {lines.map((line, index) => (
    <CodeBlockLine key={index}>{line}</CodeBlockLine>
  ))}
</CodeBlockContent>;
```

A diff is a `CodeBlockLine` list, not a `language` (see above): the `+` / `−` markers say more than a colour, and a
raw patch passed as a string with `language="diff"` would lose them. The `diff` grammar is there if you want the
colours instead.

Without a `language`, a string child stays **one text node** — the browser appends a chunk to it instead of
reconciling a tree of spans, which is what makes a streaming output block cheap.

## When to use

- A source snippet the reader is meant to copy: an install command, a route handler, a config file.
- An answer from an assistant, where the block sits inside a message and the reader may want the code out of it.
- Tool calls and their output — a shell run, a stack trace, a JSON payload — where the reader scans rather than reads.
- A diff or a patch, where added and removed lines have to be distinguishable at a glance and without colour.
- A long file that would dominate the page: cap it with `maxLines` and let the reader unfold it.
- One snippet in several forms — an install per package manager, a source file and its output — where the reader
  should not have to scroll past variants that are not theirs.

## When not to use

- A single value the reader copies — an API key, a URL, an id. Use the copy button on its own; a bordered code
  surface gives a one-line value more weight than it deserves.
- Inline code in a sentence. Use `<code>`, which the page's typeset styles.
- Content that is not code and not output: a quote, a log line with no structure, a terminal transcript with
  interactive prompts. A block that looks like code but is not sets the wrong expectation about copying.
- A whole editor. This is a viewer; it has no caret, no selection model of its own, and no undo.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CodeBlock` | `variant`, `size`, native `div` props | `variant`: `default` \| `destructive`. `size`: `default` \| `sm`. |
| | `maxLines`, `expanded`, `defaultExpanded`, `onExpandedChange` | Additive fold. Uncontrolled unless `expanded` is passed. |
| | `language` | Additive. Highlights a string child; an unknown name renders plainly. |
| | `defaultTab`, `tab`, `onTabChange` | Additive switcher. Holds the selection the tabs, the panels and the copy button share. |
| `CodeBlockHeader` | native `div` props | Sits above the source and draws a full-width rule between the label and the code. |
| `CodeBlockTitle` | native `div` props | Truncates. The selected tab's text style — 12px, medium, foreground, on the same 24px line box — so a header reads the same with or without a switcher. Wrap it in an anchor to link to the file. |
| `CodeBlockTabs` | `label`, native `div` props | Additive. `role="tablist"`, one tab stop, arrow keys move within it. Needs a `CodeBlock` parent. |
| `CodeBlockTab` | `value` (required), native `button` props | Additive. `role="tab"`; only the selected one renders the shared pill. |
| `CodeBlockActions` | native `div` props | In a header it sits at the end; on its own it floats. |
| `CodeBlockCopyButton` | `value` or `values`, all `Button` props | Copies `value`, or `values[tab]` when the block switches variants. `variant` defaults to `ghost`, `size` to `icon-xs`. |
| `CodeBlockContent` | `wrap`, `lineNumbers`, `startLine`, `language`, native `pre` props | Always `dir="ltr"` and focusable (`tabIndex={0}`; pass `-1` to remove it). `language` overrides the block's. |
| `CodeBlockPanel` | `value` (required), all `CodeBlockContent` props | Additive. One variant: renders the content, stays mounted, hidden while another tab is selected. |
| `CodeBlockLine` | `variant`, native `span` props | `default` \| `added` \| `removed` \| `highlighted`. |
| `CodeBlockFooter` | native `div` props | Sits below the source and draws the matching rule above it. |
| `CodeBlockExpandButton` | all `Button` props | Additive. Renders nothing unless the block overflows. |

`CodeBlockContent` takes its `id` from the block, which is what `CodeBlockExpandButton` points
`aria-controls` at. If you pass an `id` of your own for an anchor link, pass the same value to the button's
`aria-controls` as well.

Highlighting is a second item, installed automatically as a dependency of `code-block`:

| `code-highlight` | Signature | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `highlightCode` | `(code: string, language: string) => Promise<ReactNode[][] \| null>` | For a Server Component or any await. `null` when the language is not bundled. |
| `useHighlightedCode` | `(code: string, language?: string) => ReactNode[] \| null` | Client hook. `null` until the grammar loads, so the caller keeps its plain text. |
| `loadHighlighter` | `(language: string) => Promise<Highlighter \| null>` | The lower-level form: `highlight(code, state)` returns lines plus the grammar state for the next chunk. |

Every part carries a `data-slot` (`code-block`, `code-block-header`, `code-block-title`, `code-block-tabs`,
`code-block-tab`, `code-block-tab-indicator`, `code-block-actions`, `code-block-copy-button`,
`code-block-panel`, `code-block-content`, `code-block-code`, `code-block-line`, `code-block-line-content`,
`code-block-footer`, plus the additive `code-block-viewport` and `code-block-expand-button`), so a consumer can
restyle without a wrapper.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| fold / unfold | viewport `height`, measured and clamped to the content | `geometry.resize` | yes (a second click retargets the spring) |
| floating actions | `opacity 0 → 1` on hover and focus-within | `data.transition` | yes |
| copy | glyph cross-fade + `scale` 0.96 → 1 | `state.morph` | yes |
| fold toggle | chevron `rotate 0 → 180`, label swaps | `state.morph` | yes |
| tab indicator | one pill shared between tabs, `layoutId` | `layout.shared` | yes (a third tab pressed mid-travel retargets it) |
| reduced | fade and rotation stay; the height jumps, the copy glyph swaps without scaling, and the tab pill appears in place instead of travelling | `geometry.resize` resolves to `{ duration: 0 }` | – |
| none | every transition resolves to zero duration; the block is in its end state on the first frame | – | – |

Three notes on the choices:

- The fold animates a **measured** height rather than a `max-height` in a class. A class would need a magic number
  per line count, and it would break the moment a line wraps. The spring is the token's, and the rendered height is
  clamped to the content so it can never settle above or below the real size.
- Under reduced motion the height change is a jump on purpose. Unfolding is information — the reader asked to see
  more lines — and a 200 ms layout tween is exactly the motion the reduced mode exists to remove.
- The tab pill is a shared element only in full mode. Reduced motion drops the `layoutId`, so the pill is painted
  where the selection landed: which tab is current is information, the travel between them is not. A panel change
  never animates its height for the same reason.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Reaches the tab list (once), the selected tab, the copy button, the source, and the fold toggle. |
| Arrow Left / Right | Moves between tabs and selects the one it lands on — a tab list is one tab stop, not one stop per tab. |
| Home / End | Jumps to the first or the last tab. |
| Arrow keys / Page Up / Page Down | Scroll the source once it has focus; a long line or a capped block scrolls without moving the page. |
| Enter / Space | Copies, selects the focused tab, or toggles the fold. |
| Cmd/Ctrl + C | Copies the selection — line numbers and diff markers are excluded, blank lines are kept. |

## Accessibility

- The source is a real `pre` > `code` and is focusable, so a keyboard user can scroll a block that overflows. A
  `max-height` on the content keeps that true for capped blocks too.
- Line numbers are drawn with generated content, so they stay out of the text selection and out of the accessibility
  tree; the code is read as code, without a column of digits.
- The copy button's accessible name is `Copy`, then `Copied`; a polite live region repeats the result, so the tick
  is confirmation, not the only signal. A refused clipboard write leaves the glyph on `Copy` rather than claiming
  success.
- Diff lines carry a `+` / `−` marker next to the tint, so the change survives a monochrome display.
- The fold toggle is a real button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the source, and it is not
  rendered at all when there is nothing to unfold.
- The switcher is the ARIA tabs pattern: `role="tablist"` with a name (`label`, "Language" by default), tabs that
  carry `aria-selected` and point `aria-controls` at their panel, one tab stop with a roving `tabindex`, and
  `role="tabpanel"` panels labelled by their tab. Inactive panels are `hidden`, which takes their focusable source
  out of the tab order.
- The block is `dir="ltr"` throughout, because code reads left to right even on an RTL page. The header follows the
  page's direction.

## Responsive behavior

- `size="sm"` tightens the padding and drops the source to `text-xs` — the right weight for output inside a
  message or a tool row.
- Long lines scroll inside the block, never the page: the source owns the overflow, and the wrapper clips it.
  The bar is thin and drawn in the theme's own grey rather than the OS's, because a native scrollbar follows the
  operating system and not the page — a dark page on a light system would otherwise get a white bar down the code.
- `wrap` is for output, not for source. Wrapped source loses its indentation structure, which is the one thing code
  formatting carries.
- On a narrow screen the header's title truncates rather than wrapping, and the actions stay reachable — a touch
  device always shows them, because there is no hover to reveal them with. The tab list scrolls sideways on its
  own when three tabs and a title do not fit, so the copy button keeps its place. That row scrolls without a bar:
  a track in a 24px control strip reads as a second seam under the label, and the arrow keys and a swipe move it
  anyway.

## Performance

- Without a `language`, a string child is one text node: streaming a chunk does not rebuild a subtree, only the
  changed text is painted. With a `language`, each finished line is one node that is never re-created, and the
  line being written is the only one re-tokenized.
- One `ResizeObserver` per foldable block, and none for a block that cannot fold. The measurement is a read inside
  the observer callback, never during render.
- The fold animates `height` — a layout property, and the one place in this component that touches layout. It is
  scoped to a leaf element whose neighbours do not move, it is clamped, and it resolves to zero duration under
  reduced and none.
- Everything else is `opacity` and `scale` on small elements: two glyphs and a chevron.
- Shiki is a dynamic import. A block with no `language` never loads it; a block with one loads the engine and a
  single grammar, both cached for the rest of the session. `getLoadedLanguages()` is checked first, so the second
  `tsx` block on a page does not re-load anything.
- Tokenizing runs on the main thread. It is fast (a screenful is a fraction of a millisecond in the JS engine), but
  a thousand-line file is not free: cap it with `maxLines`, or hand the nodes in from a Server Component with
  `highlightCode`.

## Notes for AI

- Reach for `code-block` for code, terminal output, tool calls, logs, diffs and stack traces. Never hand-roll a
  `<pre>` — the copy affordance, the focus ring, and the fold are the point.
- Give the block a `value` to copy that matches what is displayed. Passing a truncated string is the most common
  bug: the reader copies less than they can see.
- Tool output is not source: `size="sm"` with `wrap` and a `max-h-*` on the content. Errors use
  `variant="destructive"` on `CodeBlock`; do not recolour the text.
- When a stream is still arriving, keep rendering the same `<CodeBlockContent>` and let the string grow. Do not key
  the block by content, and do not remount it — a remount restarts the fold measurement, drops focus, and throws
  away the cached lines, so the whole block is tokenized again on the next chunk.
- Pass `language` for source, and leave it out for tool output, logs and stack traces: a tokenizer that guesses at
  output colours noise, and the plain path is the cheaper one.
- The first paint is plain while the highlighter chunk loads. Do not hide the block until it is coloured; showing
  the text immediately is the point.
- Use `maxLines` for anything longer than a screenful, with `CodeBlockExpandButton` in the footer. Do not cap the
  block by cropping the string.
- When a snippet has more than one right form — an install for pnpm, npm and yarn, a source and its output — use
  `CodeBlockTabs` / `CodeBlockTab` / `CodeBlockPanel`, and give the header's `CodeBlockCopyButton` `values` so it
  copies the variant on screen. Do not stack two blocks with a hand-rolled toggle, and do not put unrelated files
  behind tabs: a tab is the same snippet in another form, not a second snippet.

items.name: command
items.title: Command
items.description: Search and run actions from a keyboard-driven command palette.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/command
```

For manual installation copy `command/index.tsx`, install `cmdk` and `lucide-react`, and install the
`dialog`, `input-group`, `cadence-utils`, and `cadence-provider` registry dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Command, CommandInput, CommandList, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandItem } from "@/components/cadence/command";

export function Actions() {
  return (
    <Command label="Quick actions" className="max-w-sm rounded-lg border">
      <CommandInput placeholder="Search actions..." />
      <CommandList>
        <CommandEmpty>No actions found.</CommandEmpty>
        <CommandGroup heading="Workspace">
          <CommandItem value="projects" onSelect={() => console.log("projects")}>Open projects</CommandItem>
        </CommandGroup>
      </CommandList>
    </Command>
  );
}
```

## Dialog palette

The Base UI composition keeps `Command` explicit inside `CommandDialog`. The visually hidden title
and description live inside the popup so the portalled dialog remains named.

```tsx
import * as React from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Command, CommandDialog, CommandInput, CommandList, CommandGroup, CommandItem } from "@/components/cadence/command";

export function Palette() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Open palette</Button>
      <CommandDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <Command>
          <CommandInput placeholder="Search actions..." />
          <CommandList>
            <CommandGroup heading="Workspace">
              <CommandItem value="projects" onSelect={() => setOpen(false)}>Open projects</CommandItem>
            </CommandGroup>
          </CommandList>
        </Command>
      </CommandDialog>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Keywords and disabled actions

```tsx
<CommandGroup heading="Account">
  <CommandItem value="profile" keywords={["account", "user"]}>Profile</CommandItem>
  <CommandItem value="billing" disabled>Billing unavailable</CommandItem>
</CommandGroup>
```

## Shortcut hints

```tsx
import { CommandGroup, CommandItem, CommandShortcut } from "@/components/cadence/command";

<CommandGroup heading="Navigation">
  <CommandItem value="settings">Settings <CommandShortcut>Ctrl+S</CommandShortcut></CommandItem>
</CommandGroup>
```

A shortcut is a visual hint; register application shortcuts in the caller. The component does not
install global keyboard listeners.

## When to use

- Search application actions without navigating a menu hierarchy.
- Offer keyboard navigation across grouped commands.
- Present a controlled command palette in a dialog.

## When not to use

- Use `Combobox` to choose a form value.
- Use `DropdownMenu` for a short list without search.
- Use a search page for remote results requiring pagination.

## API

| Part | Props | Default / behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Command` | cmdk root props: `label`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `filter`, `shouldFilter`, `loop` | `shouldFilter=true`, `loop=false`; value is the highlighted command |
| `CommandDialog` | Base UI Dialog root props, `title`, `description`, `className`, `showCloseButton`, required `children` | title `"Command Palette"`, description `"Search for a command to run..."`, `showCloseButton=false` |
| `CommandInput` | cmdk input props, `value`, `onValueChange`, `placeholder`, `disabled` | Typing filters locally; the root supplies the accessible label |
| `CommandList` | cmdk list props, `className` | Scrollable, max height 300px; no height tween |
| `CommandEmpty` | cmdk empty props, `className` | Shown when no command matches |
| `CommandGroup` | cmdk group props, `heading`, `value`, `forceMount` | Give a heading or unique value |
| `CommandItem` | cmdk item props, `value`, `keywords`, `disabled`, `onSelect` | Enter or click runs the action; disabled rows are skipped |
| `CommandSeparator` | cmdk separator props, `alwaysRender` | Hidden during search unless always rendered |
| `CommandShortcut` | span props, `className` | Hint only; no keyboard handler |

Parts merge user classes last and forward refs and remaining props. cmdk retains its `asChild` API;
the Base UI dialog uses `render`. The check glyph follows upstream's `data-checked`; the highlight's
`data-selected` is not a committed choice.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | dialog opacity 0 to 1 and scale from `--motion-scale-in`; backdrop opacity 0 to 1 | `popup.anchored` via Dialog, `duration.base` / `duration.fast` | yes, CSS transitions |
| close | dialog and backdrop fade out, panel scales back in full mode | `exit.fade` via Dialog | yes |
| filter / highlight | instant replacement and background feedback, no row motion | none | n/a |
| reduced | opacity only; scale classes absent | mode durations | yes |
| none | dialog and backdrop durations resolve to zero | zero duration | n/a |

The inline command has no animation. `CommandDialog` inherits Dialog's recipes and mode branches;
it adds no transition of its own. Fixed centering translation is layout, not motion.

Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside
`none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel
geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the
first mounted frame. The preview's **Popup motion** selector changes the local mode on the
same component tree. The Dialog surface retains Base UI callback/render/ref semantics. Command parts use
cmdk’s native string class and object style props; cmdk owns filtering and keyboard selection.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| ArrowDown / ArrowUp | Move highlight, skipping disabled rows |
| Home / End | First / last enabled item |
| Enter | Run the highlighted item's `onSelect` |
| Escape | Close the dialog; an inline command has no dismissal behavior |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focus traversal, trapped inside an open dialog |

## Accessibility

cmdk owns combobox/listbox roles, `aria-activedescendant`, and selected/disabled attributes.
Give `Command` a `label` to name its search field. The dialog supplies a title, description,
focus trap, and focus restoration. Empty results are text, not executable options.
Separators are decorative (`aria-hidden`) because a listbox permits options and option groups.

## Responsive behavior

The inline palette fills its container. The dialog keeps viewport margins and a desktop max width.
The list scrolls independently so the search input stays reachable on short screens.

## Performance

Filtering and list height changes are instant. No layout animation, row stagger, or application
request orchestration is added. T2 source budget: 10 KB gzip; cmdk is a declared dependency.

## Notes for AI

- Put items inside groups, inside a list, inside `Command`.
- Keep `Command` inside `CommandDialog`; the dialog does not create a cmdk root.
- Use item `onSelect`; the caller owns routing and async work.
- `CommandShortcut` registers no shortcut. Related: `combobox`, `dialog`, `dropdown-menu`.
