items.description: Transient notifications with accessible actions and dismissal.
items.docs:
## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/toast ``` For manual installation copy `toast/index.tsx`, install `@base-ui/react` and `lucide-react`, and install `button`, `cadence-utils`, and `cadence-provider`. ## Usage Mount one toaster within your `CadenceProvider`. Call the shared manager from event handlers. ```tsx import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { toast, Toaster } from "@/components/cadence/toast"; export function Notifications() { return ( ); } ``` ## Actions and priority ```tsx toast.add({ title: "Item archived", actionProps: { children: "Undo", onClick: () => restoreItem() }, }); toast.add({ title: "Connection unavailable", type: "error", priority: "high" }); ``` Low priority is announced politely; reserve high priority for urgent information. Actions use a real button and retain their caller-provided handler. Call `toast.close(id)` in the action handler when activation should dismiss the toast. ## Caller-owned progress ```tsx const id = toast.add({ title: "Export queued", type: "loading", timeout: 0 }); // When application state changes: toast.update(id, { title: "Export ready", type: "success", timeout: 5000 }); // Or dismiss explicitly: toast.close(id); ``` The caller owns requests, errors, and state. Promise orchestration is outside Cadence's contract; use `add`, `update`, and `close`. The loading glyph is static in all modes. ## Custom composition ```tsx import { ToastProvider, ToastPortal, ToastViewport, Toast, ToastContent, ToastTitle, ToastDescription, ToastClose, useToastManager } from "@/components/cadence/toast"; function NotificationsList() { const { toasts } = useToastManager(); return toasts.map(item => (
)); } ``` `createToastManager()` isolates a provider from the shared `toast` singleton. Pass it as `toastManager` to `Toaster` or `ToastProvider`. Use `useToastManager()` inside that provider. ## When to use - Brief, nonblocking confirmation after an application action. - An optional undo action with a visible close button. - Caller-owned progress updated from existing application state. ## When not to use - Inline validation errors: use Field and an error slot. - Critical decisions requiring acknowledgment: use Alert Dialog. - Persistent records or long instructions: use page content. ## API | Part | Props | Default / behavior | | --- | --- | --- | | `Toaster` | Base UI Provider props, `children`, `toastManager` | shared `toast` manager; renders portal, viewport and list | | `ToastProvider` | `timeout`, `limit`, `toastManager`, `children` | Base UI defaults: 5000ms, limit 3 | | `ToastPortal` | Base UI Portal props, `container`, `keepMounted` | document portal | | `ToastViewport` | Base UI Viewport props, `className` | fixed bottom right; F6 hotkey | | `Toast` | Base UI Root props, required `toast`, `swipeDirection`, `render`, `className` | native swipe directions and dismissal | | `ToastContent` | Base UI Content props, `render`, `className` | horizontal content layout | | `ToastTitle` / `ToastDescription` | Base UI title / description props | text from the toast object | | `ToastAction` | Base UI Action props | outline Button, size sm; actionProps from toast | | `ToastClose` | Base UI Close props, `children` | ghost Button, icon-sm; label "Close toast", X glyph | | `toast` / `createToastManager` | Base UI manager exports | add / update / close state supplied by caller | | `useToastManager` | Base UI hook | provider's toast list and manager methods | All parts forward upstream props and refs. Classes merge user values last. Button render defaults match pinned upstream. Each rendered part retains its `toast-*` data slot. ## Motion contract | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | open | opacity 0 to 1, scale from `--motion-scale-in` in full | `popup.anchored`, duration.base, ease.out | yes, CSS transition | | close / limited | opacity to 0, exit scale in full | `exit.fade`, duration.base | yes | | swipe | Base UI swipe x/y variables, full only | primitive-owned gesture | yes | | stack / content updates | bottom and natural height update instantly | no layout transition | n/a | | reduced | opacity only; scale and swipe transform absent | duration.base × 0.6 | yes | | none | zero duration, transform absent | zero duration | n/a | Notifications remain expanded in a vertical stack; there is no collapsed height or stack-scale animation. Base UI owns timeout pausing, lifecycle, swipe recognition and removal. No extra animation scheduler is added. Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside `none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the first mounted frame. The preview's **Popup motion** selector changes the local mode on the same component tree. Base UI `className(state)` and `style(state)` callbacks are evaluated before merging; caller utilities and styles win. Native `render`, events and ref cleanup remain owned by the primitive. ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | --- | --- | | F6 | Move focus to the notification viewport | | Tab / Shift+Tab | Traverse action and close controls | | Escape | Dismiss the focused notification | | Enter / Space | Activate the focused action or close button | ## Accessibility Base UI announces notification title and description at the selected priority. Focus is not moved when a toast arrives. Actions and close controls are named buttons. Important content must also exist in persistent application UI; a notification should never be its only location. Timers pause during hover or focus. ## Responsive behavior The viewport keeps 1rem margins on small screens and a max-sm width. On desktop it sits at bottom right. Long descriptions wrap. Keep messages short so stacked notifications do not fill the screen. ## Performance T2, 10 KB gzip source budget. Only opacity, scale and native swipe transform transition. Stack geometry and content sizing update instantly; no measurement occurs during render and no height tween runs. ## Notes for AI - Keep one provider per manager and mount its viewport once. - Use Base UI `render`, retain each slot, and preserve the three mode branches. - Caller state drives add/update/close; do not add request or validation orchestration. - Related: `alert`, `alert-dialog`, `button`, `field`.

items.name: accordion
items.title: Accordion
items.description: Reveal related sections while keeping their headings easy to scan.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/accordion
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/accordion";

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Accordion defaultValue={["shipping"]}>
      <AccordionItem value="shipping">
        <AccordionTrigger>When will my order arrive?</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>Most orders arrive within five working days.</AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

Base UI uses arrays for both single and multiple selection. Keep the value in caller state.

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState<string[]>([]);
<Accordion value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
  <AccordionItem value="account">
    <AccordionTrigger>Account settings</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Your account details.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>;
```

## Multiple sections

```tsx
<Accordion multiple defaultValue={["one", "two"]}>
  <AccordionItem value="one">
    <AccordionTrigger>Delivery</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Track your delivery.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="two">
    <AccordionTrigger>Returns</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Start a return.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

## Disabled and persistent content

```tsx
<Accordion keepMounted>
  <AccordionItem value="locked" disabled>
    <AccordionTrigger>Unavailable section</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>This content remains mounted while closed.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

`keepMounted`, `hiddenUntilFound`, `render`, orientation, refs, and Base UI event details pass through.
A custom panel render must preserve the supplied children and props so measurement and lifecycle work.

## When to use

- FAQ answers that readers scan by heading.
- Related settings sections with optional detail.
- Compact reference material with meaningful section titles.

## When not to use

- Use Collapsible for a single disclosure without grouped navigation.
- Use Tabs for peer views occupying one shared panel.
- Keep essential instructions visible rather than hiding them.

## API

### `Accordion`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `Value[]` | uncontrolled / `[]` | Expanded item values. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value, details) => void` | — | Caller-owned controlled state. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | Permit several expanded items. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable all items. |
| `orientation` | `"vertical" | "horizontal"` | `"vertical"` | Deprecated; retained as state only. |
| `keepMounted` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep closed panels in the DOM. |
| `hiddenUntilFound` | `boolean` | `false` | Allow browser find-in-page to reveal content. |

### `AccordionItem`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `unknown` | generated | Stable identity for controlled state. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable this item's trigger. |

### `AccordionTrigger`

All Base UI Trigger props pass through, including `render`, `ref`, and `nativeButton`. A heading wraps
the trigger. Two decorative icons swap immediately with `aria-expanded`; no rotation is animated.

### `AccordionContent`

All Base UI Panel props pass through, including `keepMounted`, `hiddenUntilFound`, `render`, `style`,
and `ref`. `className` styles the inner content, matching upstream; `style` applies to the panel.
Root and Item classes merge last.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open / close / content resize | Measured height clamped at zero | `geometry.resize` CSS form: `duration.slow` / `ease.out` | Yes, native CSS reversal from current height |
| Initially open | Natural height, no entrance | — | — |
| Reduced | Instant height, no transform | Zero duration | Yes |
| None | Instant height, no transform or transition | Zero duration | Yes |

The CSS form preserves position on interruption rather than spring velocity. Base UI owns panel
mounting, hidden state, keyboard navigation, and find-in-page behavior. An inner ResizeObserver
retargets changes in content without observing the animated panel itself. The closed size is zero.

## Accessibility

Triggers expose expanded state and control labelled regions. Focus stays on the trigger when a
panel toggles. Give each trigger a meaningful heading; do not place interactive controls inside it.
Disabled items are skipped in tab navigation. Content controls remain in normal tab order.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | Toggle the focused trigger. |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Follow normal page order through triggers and open content. |

Base UI 1.6 follows the updated APG guidance without arrow-key roving focus. `orientation` and
`loopFocus` are deprecated passthrough props; neither changes keyboard focus behavior.

## Responsive behavior

The root fills its container. Long headings wrap and the icons retain their size. Content is
remeasured when wrapping changes; there is no fixed maximum height or breakpoint-specific state.

## Performance

T3 budget: 12 KB gzip. One observer per mounted content slot; closed panels unmount by default.
Measurements run after commit and on content resize, never during render. No timers drive motion.
Server-rendered initially open content keeps its natural size before hydration.

## Notes for AI

- Use the Base UI array value API, not Radix `type="single"` or `collapsible` props.
- Preserve all four exports and the trigger-icon slot when customising.
- Keep the measurement wrapper and mode branch when editing motion.
- Related: Collapsible for a standalone disclosure; Tabs for alternate views.

items.title: Collapsible
items.description: Reveal optional detail with a standalone disclosure.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/collapsible
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/collapsible";

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Collapsible>
      <CollapsibleTrigger>Show project details</CollapsibleTrigger>
      <CollapsibleContent>Optional project information.</CollapsibleContent>
    </Collapsible>
  );
}
```

## Controlled

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
<Collapsible open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <CollapsibleTrigger>Project details</CollapsibleTrigger>
  <CollapsibleContent>Caller-owned expanded state.</CollapsibleContent>
</Collapsible>;
```

## Custom trigger

```tsx
<Collapsible defaultOpen>
  <CollapsibleTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Toggle details</CollapsibleTrigger>
  <CollapsibleContent className="text-sm">Initially visible without an entrance animation.</CollapsibleContent>
</Collapsible>
```

Import Button from `@/components/cadence/button`. The primitive supplies button semantics and expanded state.

## Persistent and searchable content

```tsx
<Collapsible>
  <CollapsibleTrigger>Reference notes</CollapsibleTrigger>
  <CollapsibleContent hiddenUntilFound>Find this text with browser search.</CollapsibleContent>
</Collapsible>
```

Use `keepMounted` to retain local content state while closed. `hiddenUntilFound` overrides it and lets
supporting browsers reveal content through find-in-page. Put these props on Content, not the root.

## When to use

- Optional details for one independent section.
- Advanced settings beside a visible summary.
- Supporting reference notes that users may reveal on demand.

## When not to use

- Use Accordion for a group of labelled sections.
- Use Tabs for peer views sharing one panel.
- Keep essential instructions visible.

## API

### `Collapsible`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | uncontrolled / `false` | Controlled or initial expanded state. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open, details) => void` | — | State change request; details support cancellation. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Ignore trigger interaction. |
| `className`, `style`, `render`, `ref` | Base UI Root props | — | Forwarded unchanged, including state callbacks. |

### `CollapsibleTrigger`

All Base UI Trigger props pass through, including `disabled`, `nativeButton`, `render`, `ref`, and
state-based classes/styles. Use `render`, not `asChild`, for a custom element. Supply an accessible name.

### `CollapsibleContent`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keepMounted` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep closed content in the DOM. |
| `hiddenUntilFound` | `boolean` | `false` | Reveal via browser find-in-page; overrides keepMounted. |
| `className`, `style`, `render`, `ref` | Base UI Panel props | — | Applied to the outer panel; classes merge last. |

All primitive props remain available. A custom render must preserve supplied children and props,
including the natural measurement wrapper. The added `collapsible-content-inner` slot is structural.
Outer padding and borders are supported in both `border-box` and `content-box`; expanded content
retains its natural height. During closing, CSS keeps the outer padding/border minimum until Base UI
hides or unmounts the panel. To reach a visually zero-height endpoint before hiding, put that decoration
on a content child. Caller styles are preserved; padding and borders are never animated.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open / close / content resize | Measured height clamped at zero | `geometry.resize` CSS form: `duration.slow` / `ease.out` | Yes, native reversal from current position |
| Initially open | Natural height without entrance | — | — |
| Reduced | Instant height, no transform | Zero duration | Yes |
| None | Instant height, no transform or transition | Zero duration | Yes |

An inner ResizeObserver watches natural content, never the animated panel. Measurements happen after
commit, on resize and when outer classes/styles change. Border-box targets include outer vertical
padding and borders; content-box targets use the natural inner height. Native CSS reversal preserves
position rather than spring velocity. Base UI owns mounting, hidden state and transition completion. No icon animation or extra recipe is added.

## Accessibility

The trigger exposes `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. Content retains Base UI's default div semantics;
add a named region only when the content warrants one. Focus stays on the trigger when toggled.
Disabled controls are skipped in normal tab navigation. Keep interactive content outside the trigger.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | Toggle the focused trigger. |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Follow normal page order through the trigger and visible content. |

## Responsive behavior

No fixed dimensions or breakpoint-driven state. Natural content is remeasured when wrapping changes.
The root and trigger are unstyled; use caller classes or compose Button for visual feedback.

## Performance

T3 budget: 12 KB gzip. One ResizeObserver per mounted content panel, disconnected on unmount.
Closed content unmounts by default. Initially open server content uses natural height before hydration.
No timers or render-time measurements drive animation.

## Notes for AI

- Use boolean `open`, not Accordion's array value API.
- Keep content lifecycle props on Content and preserve the measurement wrapper.
- Preserve all three exports and the full/reduced/none branch.
- Related: Accordion for grouped sections; Tabs for alternate views.

Classes merge last. No custom props or defaults are added. | Export | Element | | --- | --- | | `Table` | `table` | | `TableHeader` | `thead` | | `TableBody` | `tbody` | | `TableFooter` | `tfoot` | | `TableRow` | `tr` | | `TableHead` | `th` | | `TableCell` | `td` | | `TableCaption` | `caption` | Each part's slot is its kebab-case name: `table`, `table-header`, `table-body`, `table-footer`, `table-row`, `table-head`, `table-cell`, and `table-caption`. `Table` also creates a `div` with `data-slot="table-container"` and `relative w-full overflow-x-auto`. Row colour feedback is the upstream CSS colour transition; rows do not enter, reorder, resize, or animate selection. | Mode | Animated properties | | --- | --- | | full | none | | reduced | none | | none | none | No timing token or interruption lifecycle applies. ## Accessibility - Native table, row, header, cell and caption semantics remain intact. Links, buttons and checkboxes inside cells keep their native keyboard interaction; no grid arrow-key model is added. - The wrapper scrolls horizontally on narrow screens; columns are not removed. T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive children and application handlers still need their own client code. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. ## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/carousel ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Carousel, CarouselContent, CarouselItem, CarouselPrevious, CarouselNext } from "@/components/cadence/carousel"; export function Example() { return ( {[1, 2, 3].map((slide) => (
Project {slide}
 ))} ); } ``` ## Multiple visible slides ```tsx {[1, 2, 3, 4].map((slide) => ( Project {slide} ))} ``` ## Vertical collection ```tsx First update Second update ``` ## API and plugins ```tsx "use client"; import { useEffect, useState } from "react"; import { Carousel, type CarouselApi, CarouselContent, CarouselItem } from "@/components/cadence/carousel"; export function WithApi() { const [api, setApi] = useState(); const [selected, setSelected] = useState(0); useEffect(() => { if (!api) return; const update = () => setSelected(api.selectedScrollSnap()); update(); api.on("select", update); return () => { api.off("select", update); }; }, [api]); return ( <> First Second

Project {selected + 1}

); } ``` Pass Embla plugins through `plugins`; keep plugin instances stable. The API is the actual Embla 8.6.0 instance, including events, `reInit`, `plugins`, `scrollTo`, `scrollProgress` and `destroy`. Plugins are never removed by a motion mode. Stop autoplay or independent animation plugins under reduced/none yourself, and provide pause controls. Cadence clamps the engine's interpolation even when a plugin or API call explicitly requests `jump=false`. ## When to use - Browse a short collection of related projects, cards or photos. - Show one highlighted item with explicit previous/next navigation. - Allow touch swiping alongside keyboard and button navigation. ## When not to use - Use Tabs for named views that must remain directly selectable. - Use Scroll Area for continuous reading or long lists. - Keep essential content discoverable without relying on automatic advance. ## API | Part | Contract | | --- | --- | | Root | Native div props/ref; `orientation="horizontal"` (or `vertical`); `opts` and `plugins` use Embla types; `setApi(api)` receives the public instance. | | Track | Native div props/ref/style/classes target the **inner track**. Its fixed overflow-hidden outer viewport owns the `carousel-content` slot and Embla ref. | | Slide | Native div props/ref; group/slide semantics. Default full basis; caller classes size each slide. | | Previous / Next | All Button props, including render, ref, state callback classes/styles and events. Defaults: outline, icon-sm. Caller disabled/onClick override the navigation defaults as upstream does. | | Context hook | Context with API, viewport ref, original options, orientation, navigation functions and canScroll states. Throws outside Carousel. | | API type | Exported Embla instance type (possibly undefined before initialization). | The fixed Base UI API and new-york-v4 visuals are pinned at `96da9cc7f1aa`. Navigation buttons retain the Base API's icon-sm default with the visual source's round size-8 shape. Orientation controls the axis even if opts.axis differs, as upstream does. Options such as startIndex, align, loop, dragFree, watchDrag, breakpoints and direction pass to Embla. For RTL set both native `dir="rtl"` and `opts.direction="rtl"`. ## Motion contract | Phase | Recipe | Behaviour | | --- | --- | --- | | Enter / exit | — | No authored entrance or removal animation. | | Interaction | `data.transition` | `data.transition`, engine form: Embla alone translates the track. Default duration.base maps to 22 attraction units via carouselClock; timeScale scales it. Explicit full-mode opts.duration remains native. | | Interruption | — | Next/previous/drag retarget Embla's existing location and velocity. Release uses the effective base clock, including breakpoint options, instead of a hard-coded release duration. | | Reduced | — | Track and loop relocation transforms retain the correct state position. Direct dragging remains available. All autonomous engine interpolation is zero; no CSS/Motion transform animation is added. | | None | — | Same immediate state positioning, with every engine duration zero even for explicit API/plugin duration requests. | | Buttons | — | Composed Button owns its declared feedback.press recipe; reduced/none remove press scale. Static control placement/vertical rotation are layout. | A mode downgrade settles the existing target without resetting selection. Engine friction, geometry and momentum destinations remain Embla-owned. Independent plugin animations remain caller-owned. Removing the track transform would display the wrong slide and is not reduction. ## Keyboard and accessibility | Keys | Action | | --- | --- | | Tab / Shift+Tab | Reach native controls and any focusable slide content. | | Enter / Space | Activate a focused navigation button. | | ArrowLeft / ArrowRight | Previous / next from inside the region, on both orientations (pinned upstream behaviour). | Supply a region label and per-slide labels, and optionally a polite status as in the preview. The root is not focusable by default; use tabIndex and a visible focus class when desired. Embla scrolls focused offscreen slide content into view. Caller onKeyDownCapture replaces the upstream capture handler; caller onClick similarly replaces the navigation action. This is not a tab widget and does not hide offscreen content from assistive technology. Avoid interactive content whose arrow handling conflicts with the root capture handler. ## Responsiveness and performance Size slides with basis utilities and pair inner negative margins with slide padding. Vertical tracks require an explicit height. Set touch-pan-y on horizontal tracks and touch-pan-x on vertical tracks to preserve cross-axis page scrolling. Leave room for controls outside the viewport. Embla observes viewport/slide geometry and slide mutations, reinitializing snaps as needed; options/plugins reinitialize through the native React adapter. No layout reads happen in render. SSR renders static first-slide markup, then Embla initializes after hydration. No autoplay, virtualization or per-slide Motion instances are bundled. Only track transforms animate. ## Notes for AI - Preserve opts, plugins, setApi, useCarousel and all native part props when adapting examples. - Use the exposed Embla API for selection rather than applying another transform to the track. - Keep selected position under reduced/none; assert the lack of interpolation, not transform:none. - Use Button for individual actions, Tabs for directly named panels, and Scroll Area for long content.

items.name: calendar
items.title: Calendar
items.description: Select dates, multiple days, and ranges with accessible month navigation.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/calendar
```

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Calendar } from "@/components/cadence/calendar";

export function Example() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>();
  return <Calendar mode="single" selected={date} onSelect={setDate} />;
}
```

## Multiple dates

```tsx
const [days, setDays] = useState<Date[] | undefined>([]);
<Calendar mode="multiple" selected={days} onSelect={setDays} max={5} />;
```

## Date ranges

```tsx
import type { DateRange } from "react-day-picker";
const [range, setRange] = useState<DateRange | undefined>();
<Calendar mode="range" selected={range} onSelect={setRange} min={2}
  disabled={{ dayOfWeek: [0, 6] }} excludeDisabled />;
```

## Localized navigation

```tsx
import { fr } from "date-fns/locale";
<Calendar locale={fr} weekStartsOn={1} captionLayout="dropdown"
  startMonth={new Date(2020, 0)} endMonth={new Date(2030, 11)} />;
```

## When to use

- Pick a date in a booking or scheduling interface.
- Select several independent days or a contiguous range.
- Browse adjacent months with keyboard and localized captions.

## When not to use

Use an Input for free-form date text. Compose a Popover for a date-picker field;
Calendar itself is an inline calendar, without field serialization or popup orchestration.

## API

### `Calendar`

All DayPicker 9.13.2 props and discriminated selection types are preserved.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mode | single / multiple / range | undefined | No selection when omitted. |
| selected / onSelect | DayPicker selection type / handler | — | Caller owns selected values. |
| month / onMonthChange | Date / handler | — | Controlled navigation. Otherwise use defaultMonth. |
| showOutsideDays | boolean | true | Show days from adjacent months. |
| captionLayout | DayPicker caption layout | label | Label or native month/year dropdowns. |
| buttonVariant | Button variant | ghost | Navigation button appearance. |
| locale / weekStartsOn | Partial Locale / 0–6 | DayPicker locale | Labels, formatting and week boundary. |
| disabled / hidden | Matcher or Matcher[] | — | DayPicker matching rules. |
| numberOfMonths / fixedWeeks / showWeekNumber | number / boolean / boolean | 1 / false / false | Grid layout options. |
| className / classNames / style / styles | DayPicker styles | — | Caller overrides win. |
| formatters / labels / components | DayPicker overrides | — | Override individual formatters, accessible labels or entire parts. |
| animate | boolean | false | Forwarded upstream API; external DayPicker animation CSS is caller-owned. Do not combine a second CSS clock with Cadence motion. |

### `CalendarDayButton`

Accepts DayPicker's DayButton props (`day`, `modifiers`, native button attributes) plus
`locale?: Partial<Locale>`. Preserves native events, disabled state, classes, styles and
focus management. Selection and range modifiers have the upstream data attributes.
Custom components replace default parts completely and must maintain the same accessibility
and motion contract. A custom Month or MonthGrid also takes ownership of month motion.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Month changes | opacity and signed horizontal transform on the actual grid | `data.transition`, distance.sm | Yes; latest month replaces the target, without remounting the month tree. |
| Reduced | opacity only | `data.transition` reduced | Mode changes settle running motion. |
| None | Immediate grid update | zero duration | No animation is started. |
| Selection / enter / exit | Static selection and range styles | none | No decoration on mount. |

The same grid responds to buttons, native dropdowns, keyboard navigation and external controlled
month updates. Week-count height changes immediately. Caller transform/opacity styles take
precedence over the corresponding animation property. No outgoing duplicate steals focus.

## Accessibility

DayPicker owns grid labels, selected/disabled semantics and roving focus. Native month/year
selects stay keyboard reachable. Pass a meaningful `aria-label` when several calendars appear.
DayPicker 9.13.2 keeps its default navigation labels in English even with a date-fns locale;
provide `labels` to localize those strings. Use the `footer` live region or a separate status for selected values. Do not replace a day
with a non-interactive element in a selectable calendar.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | Previous/next day or week; crosses month boundaries. |
| Home / End | Start/end of week. |
| Page Up / Page Down | Previous/next month. |
| Shift + Page Up / Page Down | Previous/next year. |
| Enter / Space | Select focused day using the active selection mode. |
| Tab | Move between navigation, caption controls and the roving day target. |

## Validation and data ownership

Calendar renders the caller's selection and disabled matchers. The caller owns business rules,
validation, timezone, serialization and form state. No hidden field or schema is created.
DayPicker's required/min/max/excludeDisabled selection behavior is forwarded unchanged.
In 9.13.2, selecting another date at the multiple-mode max resets selection to that date.
With excludeDisabled, a range crossing a disabled date resets its start to the clicked date.

## Responsive behavior

Cells default to 32px and can be enlarged with `className="[--cell-size:--spacing(10)]"`.
Multiple months stack vertically below md and become a row at md. Provide enough space when
customizing cells, week numbers or month counts. The preview is checked at 390px and 1280px.

## Performance

No layout measurements, duplicate month DOM or animation timers. Only the changing month grid
animates; dates and keyboard focus remain managed by DayPicker. The dependency is pinned to
9.13.2 with date-fns 4.1.0. Pass an explicit defaultMonth/today/timeZone when server and client
must agree across timezone or date boundaries. For SSR dropdown captions, pass an explicit locale
(e.g. enUS from date-fns/locale): the pinned upstream formatter uses the environment locale
when locale is omitted, which can differ between server and browser.

## Notes for AI

Keep the discriminated DayPicker selection props together. Do not introduce validation or
remount with a month key to animate. Prefer Calendar inside Popover for a field, and preserve
custom labels, locale and disabled matchers when composing it.

items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/navigation-menu
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuItem, NavigationMenuTrigger,
  NavigationMenuContent, NavigationMenuLink } from "@/components/cadence/navigation-menu";

export function SiteNavigation() {
  return (
    <NavigationMenu aria-label="Main navigation">
      <NavigationMenuList>
        <NavigationMenuItem value="learn">
          <NavigationMenuTrigger>Learn</NavigationMenuTrigger>
          <NavigationMenuContent className="w-64">
            <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs">Documentation</NavigationMenuLink>
          </NavigationMenuContent>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
      </NavigationMenuList>
    </NavigationMenu>
  );
}
```

## Controlled navigation

Use a stable item value. `null` closes the popup. Base UI passes change details with the reason
and cancellation methods through unchanged.

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = React.useState<string | null>(null);
<NavigationMenu value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>…</NavigationMenu>
```

## Active links and custom rendering

Use `active` for the current route. `render` accepts an element or state callback; custom routing
components must forward native link props and refs.

```tsx
<NavigationMenuLink active render={<a href="/docs" />}>Docs</NavigationMenuLink>
<NavigationMenuTrigger className={state => state.open ? "bg-accent" : ""}>
  Resources
</NavigationMenuTrigger>
```

## Retained content

`keepMounted` keeps inactive content hidden, preserving state across item switches while the popup stays mounted. The default portal unmounts on a complete close, so keepMounted does not retain local state across closing the whole menu. Base UI moves content to the shared
viewport and makes outgoing content inert during its exit. Updating children resizes the same popup.

```tsx
<NavigationMenuContent keepMounted className="w-72">
  <NavigationMenuLink href="/guides">Guides</NavigationMenuLink>
</NavigationMenuContent>
```

## When to use

- Primary site navigation with grouped destinations.
- Desktop resource menus with differently sized panels.
- Navigation that needs pointer, touch and keyboard access to the same links.

## When not to use

- Application commands: use `menubar` or `dropdown-menu`.
- Persistent mobile navigation: use `sidebar` or a `sheet` composition.
- Switching local page content: use `tabs`.

## API

| Part | Props | Defaults and behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NavigationMenu` | Base UI Root props, `align` | `align="start"`; `value`/`defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `onOpenChangeComplete`, `actionsRef`, `delay`, `closeDelay`, `orientation`, `render`, ref and native nav props pass through. Automatically appends one positioner. |
| `NavigationMenuList` | Base UI List props | List semantics and keyboard navigation. |
| `NavigationMenuItem` | Base UI Item props | Stable `value` associates trigger and content. |
| `NavigationMenuTrigger` | Base UI Trigger props | Native button, supports disabled, render, refs, callback classes/styles. |
| `NavigationMenuContent` | Base UI Content props | Portaled content, `keepMounted=false`; caller classes/styles merge with primitive state. |
| `NavigationMenuLink` | Base UI Link props | Native anchor; `active`, `closeOnClick`, render, refs supported. |
| `NavigationMenuIndicator` | Base UI Icon props | Static arrow within a trigger; no extra animation. |
| `NavigationMenuPositioner` | Base UI Positioner props | `side="bottom"`, `sideOffset=8`, `align="start"`, `alignOffset=0`; anchor, collision, render, refs and state callbacks pass through. |
| `navigationMenuTriggerStyle` | CVA function | Trigger classes for standalone navigation links. |

The pinned Base UI API exports Positioner, rather than Radix's Viewport export or `viewport` root prop.
Positioner contains the popup and viewport. Root already appends it; do not add a second one. Popup and
viewport have additive `data-slot` hooks. Positioner props still follow upstream composition.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Recipe / tokens | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open | Popup opacity and anchor scale; content opacity | `popup.anchored`, fast clock, scale.in | Native CSS reversal |
| Close / outgoing content | Opacity to zero; popup returns to anchor scale | `exit.fade`, fast clock | Base UI retains exit nodes until completion |
| Switch / update | Shared popup width/height, clamped to available space | `geometry.resize`, slow clock / ease.out | Base UI measures current size before retargeting |
| Reduced | Opacity only; no scale or geometry transition | Fast clock at 0.6×; geometry instant | Live downgrade keeps nodes and focus |
| None | All durations zero, geometry instant | Zeroed CSS tokens | Running transitions finish immediately |

Content switches cross-fade; they do not slide. The positioner follows the active trigger instantly.
Sizing uses Base UI's measured popup variables, not render-time reads or a second animation engine. Trigger activation and in-panel content mutation retarget the resize clock; a value-only controlled switch can adopt the new natural geometry immediately.
Popup and content own token-derived CSS clocks so explicit nested modes and the preview speed work across portals. Caller custom motion must obey the same mode contract.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Enter and leave the navigation without a modal focus trap. |
| ArrowLeft / ArrowRight | Move between top-level items in horizontal orientation. |
| ArrowDown / Enter / Space | Open a trigger; Tab enters its content. |
| Escape | Close and return focus to the active trigger. |
| Enter on a link | Follow the native link destination. |

## Accessibility

Root is a navigation landmark; give multiple navigation regions distinct accessible labels. Triggers
expose expanded state and content association. Base UI owns pointer hover, click/touch activation,
focus guards, disabled triggers and outside/Escape dismissal. Closing does not duplicate content or
remount it to reset motion. Cadence removes aria-hidden from Base UI 1.6’s tabbable focus sentinels within this menu; they remain empty generic spans with their original Tab redirection handlers. Keep link text meaningful and keyboard focus rings visible.

## Responsive behavior

Popup width and height are limited by Base UI's available viewport dimensions. Its viewport scrolls
when content exceeds that space. Supply responsive widths/grids for your destinations; the component
does not replace your information architecture with a mobile drawer. Resize updates anchor geometry
immediately in all modes. Reduced and none never tween width/height.

## Performance

T3: one shared popup, native CSS transitions, and Base UI's existing post-commit measurements and
mutation/resize tracking. No additional geometry observer, timer, layout animation loop or persistent
will-change. Two scoped child-list observers repair newly inserted focus sentinels; they disconnect on unmount. Geometry transitions are limited to the popup; nothing transitions top/left. Inactive
content unmounts by default; keepMounted deliberately retains caller state and its DOM cost.

## Notes for AI

Match the Base UI surface, including render, refs and state callback classes/styles. Do not add Radix
asChild or substitute a command menu. Keep stable item values; do not key the viewport on selection.
Use real links, label the landmark, and keep mobile content within available space.

## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/resizable ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup } from "@/components/cadence/resizable"; export function Workspace() { return (
Explorer
Editor
 ); } ``` ## Vertical layout Set `orientation="vertical"` on the group and give it a definite height. The separator's ARIA orientation describes the divider: horizontal for a vertical group. ```tsx Preview Output ``` ## Collapse and external updates Use the library's public refs. `defaultLayout` is an initial/persisted layout, not a controlled value prop. Apply external changes with `groupRef.setLayout`; no controlled API is invented. `onLayoutChange` reports live updates, while `onLayoutChanged` reports completed changes and `meta.isUserInteraction`. `onResize` reports pixel and percentage sizes with the prior size. ```tsx import { useGroupRef, usePanelRef } from "react-resizable-panels"; export function CollapsibleWorkspace() { const group = useGroupRef(); const panel = usePanelRef(); return (
Files Editor
); } ``` ## When to use - Editor panes whose widths users adjust. - Preview/output workspaces with vertical splits. - Collapsible tool panels with persistent application-owned layouts. ## When not to use - Static columns: use CSS grid. - Hidden disclosure content: use Collapsible or Accordion. - Mobile navigation: use Sheet or Sidebar. ## API | Export | Props and defaults | | --- | --- | | `ResizablePanelGroup` | `react-resizable-panels` `GroupProps`; orientation horizontal, resizing enabled, immediate panel preview. | | `ResizablePanel` | `PanelProps`; min 0%, max 100%, collapsible false, collapsed size 0%, relative resize behavior. | | `ResizableHandle` | `SeparatorProps` plus optional `withHandle` (unset by default). | All native attributes/events, string classes, style objects, `elementRef`, `groupRef`, `panelRef`, constraints, callbacks, disabled state and preview props pass through. This primitive has no Base UI `render`, `asChild`, or callback class/style API. Group and handle classes merge caller last. Panel classes and caller styles target the library's inner content element; `elementRef` addresses its root. Managed flex/display geometry retains library precedence; other caller styles pass through. Handle children follow upstream: the wrapper renders its optional grip instead of caller children. Numeric sizes are **pixels**; use strings such as `"40%"` for percentages. Group layouts map stable panel ids to numeric percentages. Slots: `resizable-panel-group`, `resizable-panel`, `resizable-handle`. Use `elementRef` for DOM access rather than a generic React ref. ## Motion contract T0: declared, implemented and documented recipe sets are empty. Direct manipulation is functional layout, not an authored animation. Pointer, keyboard, collapse/expand and imperative updates apply immediately in full, reduced and none. No spring, timer, geometry tween, opacity reveal, provider, `data-motion` or motion hook is shipped. Mode changes preserve the same panel nodes and input state. | Mode | Authored motion | | --- | --- | | full | none; immediate layout | | reduced | none; immediate layout | | none | none; immediate layout | Caller-added animation is application-owned. Do not transition flex or width/height on these panels: it makes the divider lag behind input and bypasses the geometry recipe budget. ## Accessibility The primitive supplies focusable separators, `aria-controls`, orientation and value bounds/current value. Label each handle. Tab focuses the separator; axis arrows resize by 5 percentage points, Home/End reach permitted limits, Enter toggles the preceding collapsible panel, and F6/Shift+F6 cycle enabled separators. Double-click restores the preceding panel's default size unless disabled. A locked group disables resizing; disabling only a separator still permits indirect panel resizing. Keep critical controls outside a collapsible panel so they remain reachable when it is zero-sized. ## Responsive behavior Constrain the group's height for vertical layouts. Use `min-w-0` on grid parents, percentage constraints for narrow screens and scrollable inner content for long lines. Orientation changes are caller-owned; there is no automatic mobile breakpoint. The preview supports both axes at desktop and 390px. The library adjusts constraints on container resize; at least one panel must preserve relative size. ## Performance No Cadence animation or extra measurement engine is added. The library owns resize observation and pointer/keyboard handling. Keep expensive persistence work in `onLayoutChanged`, not every live update. Percentage defaults can shift slightly during SSR hydration; provide stable ids and consistent initial layout. This T0 source budget excludes the declared third-party dependency; it is not a total bundle claim. ## Notes for AI - Use v4 Group/Panel/Separator props and public refs; v3 direction/PanelGroup APIs do not apply. - Preserve constraints and immediate resizing in all modes. - Use stable ids when persisting layouts and explicit units for panel sizes.

items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/sidebar
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Sidebar, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger, SidebarContent, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuButton } from "@/components/cadence/sidebar";

export function Workspace() {
  return <SidebarProvider>
    <Sidebar><SidebarContent><nav aria-label="Workspace"><SidebarMenu>
      <SidebarMenuItem><SidebarMenuButton render={<a href="/projects" />}>Projects</SidebarMenuButton></SidebarMenuItem>
    </SidebarMenu></nav></SidebarContent></Sidebar>
    <main><SidebarTrigger />Your content</main>
  </SidebarProvider>;
}
```

## Icon navigation

Use `collapsible="icon"` with an icon and text inside each `SidebarMenuButton`. A `tooltip` string
labels the collapsed icon. Keep an accessible name on rendered links. Widths update immediately;
menu children stay mounted on desktop.

## Controlled navigation

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(true);
return <SidebarProvider open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <Sidebar collapsible="offcanvas">Navigation</Sidebar>
  <SidebarTrigger />
</SidebarProvider>;
```

The desktop setter writes `sidebar_state=true|false`, path `/`, max-age seven days. It does not read
that cookie. Read it on the server and pass `defaultOpen` when persistence is needed. Supplying
`onOpenChange` delegates state changes to that callback, as upstream does. Mobile state is separate;
`useSidebar()` exposes `openMobile`, `setOpenMobile`, `isMobile`, and `toggleSidebar`.

## When to use

- Persistent workspace navigation in dashboards.
- Application shells with a compact icon rail.
- Navigation that becomes a modal panel on narrow screens.

## When not to use

Use Navigation Menu for short top-level menus and Sheet for a task panel. This component does not
provide routing, permissions, or application state.

## API

### `SidebarProvider`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| defaultOpen | boolean | true | Initial desktop state. |
| open / onOpenChange | boolean / callback | — | Controlled desktop state. |
| style | CSSProperties | — | Overrides `--sidebar-width` (16rem) and `--sidebar-width-icon` (3rem). |
| native div props / ref | native | — | Forwarded to wrapper. |

### `Sidebar`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| side | left / right | left | Physical panel edge. |
| variant | sidebar / floating / inset | sidebar | Surface treatment. |
| collapsible | offcanvas / icon / none | offcanvas | Hide, compact, or remain visible. |
| dir | string | — | Native panel direction in desktop, static and mobile layouts. |
| className / style / ref | native | — | Desktop container; static sidebar or mobile popup respectively. |

`SidebarTrigger` accepts Button props and calls caller `onClick` before toggling. `SidebarRail`
accepts native button props and is excluded from Tab order; the trigger is the keyboard control.
`SidebarInset` renders a main landmark; use it as the application's main, not inside another main.
`SidebarInput` and `SidebarSeparator` accept their corresponding component props.

`SidebarHeader`, `SidebarFooter`, `SidebarContent`, `SidebarGroup`, `SidebarGroupContent`,
`SidebarMenuBadge`, and `SidebarMenuSkeleton` accept div props. Skeleton supports `showIcon=false`;
its deterministic text width avoids hydration mismatch. `SidebarMenu`/`SidebarMenuSub` render ul;
`SidebarMenuItem`/`SidebarMenuSubItem` render li.

`SidebarGroupLabel`, `SidebarGroupAction`, `SidebarMenuAction`, `SidebarMenuButton`, and
`SidebarMenuSubButton` accept Base UI `render` (element or state callback), native props and refs.
MenuButton supports `isActive=false`, `variant="default"|"outline"`, `size="default"|"sm"|"lg"`,
and `tooltip` (string or TooltipContent props). MenuAction supports `showOnHover=false`.
SubButton supports `size="md"|"sm"` and `isActive=false`. Classes merge caller last; native events
and useRender event merging remain available. `useSidebar` requires a provider.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop offcanvas toggle | transform, own-width translation | `layout.move` | Yes, current position and velocity retarget. |

Full springs between the edge and off-edge position; no mounting reveal. Reduced and none update
position immediately, with no animated transform. Gap, icon widths, label margins and visibility
update immediately in every mode. No layout or height tween is authored. Caller `style.transform`
owns that property and suppresses desktop motion. System reduced motion overrides full; live mode
downgrades stop the running spring without replacing the panel.

Mobile delegates `popup.anchored` / `exit.fade` to Sheet. Button press, tooltip popup and Skeleton pulse
are owned by those dependencies, not extra Sidebar recipes. Their effective mode follows the provider.

## Accessibility

Wrap navigation links in a named nav landmark. `isActive` styles the item; add `aria-current="page"`
to the active link yourself. Offcanvas desktop contents are inert while closed. The mobile Sheet
has a hidden title and description, traps focus, dismisses with Escape/outside click and restores
focus. Place a visible close control inside long mobile navigation when needed.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Ctrl+B / Cmd+B | Toggle desktop state or mobile sheet. Also applies inside inputs, matching upstream. |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Normal links and controls; no menu-style arrow navigation. |
| Enter / Space | Activate the trigger. |
| Escape | Dismiss the mobile sheet. |

## Responsive behavior

Below 768px, collapsible navigation uses an 18rem Sheet. `collapsible="none"` remains static on all
widths. Left/right and all three variants remain supported. Desktop toggles retain child state;
switching between desktop and mobile uses upstream's separate trees and can remount children.
Default mobile closing unmounts content. Store drafts outside Sidebar if they must survive that.

## Performance

Only the desktop offcanvas transform animates. There is no measurement loop, persistent will-change,
timer, width interpolation or validation dependency. Child input values survive desktop state and
motion-mode updates. Render only the navigation items the application needs.

## Notes for AI

Keep the provider, navigation landmark and main content together. Use `render`, never `asChild`.
Do not assume the cookie is read or desktop `open` controls the mobile sheet. Do not animate icon
widths or disclosure height without a separately reviewed measured geometry contract.

items.name: data-table
items.title: Data Table
items.description: An editable payments table with sorting, filtering, selection, visibility, and pagination.
items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/data-table
```

The block installs TanStack Table **9.3.1** and the Cadence Table, Input, Button,
Checkbox and Dropdown Menu items. Manual installation: copy
`registry/cadence/data-table/index.tsx` to `components/cadence/data-table/index.tsx`,
install those registry dependencies, then install `@tanstack/react-table@9.3.1`.
Keep the relative imports and sibling install tree.

## Usage

```tsx
import { DataTableDemo } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";

export function Payments() {
  return <DataTableDemo />;
}
```

This is an editable payments **composition**, not a universal table primitive.
It starts from the [pinned Base example](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/96da9cc7f1aa10580a3741664e2a77c721206c00/apps/v4/examples/base/data-table-demo.tsx)
and [guide](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/96da9cc7f1aa10580a3741664e2a77c721206c00/apps/v4/content/docs/components/base/data-table.mdx).
`Payment`, `columns`, and `DataTableDemo` retain that example's exports.
Edit the column definitions and feature registration for your application.
The current [TanStack React documentation](https://tanstack.com/table/latest/docs/framework/react/overview)
describes v9; v8's `useReactTable` and `get*RowModel` options do not apply.

## Application data

```tsx
import { DataTableDemo, type Payment } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";

const payments: Payment[] = [
  { id: "invoice-1", email: "lee@example.com", amount: 42, status: "pending" },
];

export function PaymentHistory() {
  return <DataTableDemo data={payments} className="max-w-4xl" />;
}
```

IDs must be unique and stable. Sorting and filtering retain selected IDs; replacing
records does not select a different record at the same array index. The caller
owns removal of stale selections when records disappear. Amounts are USD numbers;
status is `pending | processing | success | failed`. The default is five example
payments. Copy payment ID writes the original ID to the browser clipboard; Email
customer is a real `mailto:` link. Clipboard permission/errors belong to the host.

## Controlled sorting and pagination

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import type { PaginationState, SortingState } from "@tanstack/react-table";
import { DataTableDemo } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";

export function ControlledPayments() {
  const [sorting, setSorting] = useState<SortingState>([]);
  const [pagination, setPagination] = useState<PaginationState>({ pageIndex: 0, pageSize: 10 });
  return <DataTableDemo sorting={sorting} onSortingChange={setSorting}
    pagination={pagination} onPaginationChange={setPagination} />;
}
```

Pair each controlled state prop with its matching change callback. Callbacks receive
TanStack value-or-updater functions, so React setters work directly. A state prop
without a callback is read-only; a callback without a state prop observes updates
but takes over updating that slice. Leave both absent for internal state.
The default page size is 10. The header checkbox selects the **current page**;
the status counts selected rows in the filtered collection. Email sorts ascending
then descending, case-insensitively; its filter is a case-insensitive substring.
Filtering resets pagination through TanStack's default auto reset behavior.

## Column visibility and empty results

```tsx
<DataTableDemo columnVisibility={{ status: false }} />
<DataTableDemo columnFilters={[{ id: "email", value: "no-match" }]} />
```

Columns hides Status, Email or Amount. Selection and Actions cannot be hidden.
A hidden Email column keeps its filter state. Empty results span the number of
**visible** columns. Use a corresponding callback to make either example editable.

## Validation and data ownership

The caller fetches records, decides validity and owns persistence. This block
contains no validation, submission, request orchestration or schema API.
All processing is client-side; server pagination, virtualization, editing,
resizing and multi-column filter controls require adapting the copied composition.

## When to use

- Payment lists with sortable emails and small client-side collections.
- A starting point for an application-specific TanStack v9 composition.
- A native table with page-level selection and column visibility controls.

## When not to use

- Static records: use [Table](/components/table).
- Very large datasets: build caller-owned server pagination or virtualization.
- Spreadsheet navigation or cell editing: this example has native table semantics.

## API

`DataTableDemo` accepts native `div` props (including React 19 ref, events, style,
and classes merged last) on `data-slot="data-table"`. Table parts retain their
existing slots. The native table is named Payments and has a visible focus ring.

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `Payment[]` | five sample payments |
| `sorting` | `SortingState` | internal `[]` |
| `columnFilters` | `ColumnFiltersState` | internal `[]` |
| `columnVisibility` | `ColumnVisibilityState` | internal `{}` |
| `rowSelection` | `RowSelectionState` | internal `{}` |
| `pagination` | `PaginationState` | internal `{ pageIndex: 0, pageSize: 10 }` |
| `onSortingChange` | `OnChangeFn<SortingState>` | internal setter |
| `onColumnFiltersChange` | `OnChangeFn<ColumnFiltersState>` | internal setter |
| `onColumnVisibilityChange` | `OnChangeFn<ColumnVisibilityState>` | internal setter |
| `onRowSelectionChange` | `OnChangeFn<RowSelectionState>` | internal setter |
| `onPaginationChange` | `OnChangeFn<PaginationState>` | internal setter |

The exported `columns` are the payment-specific TanStack v9 definitions, not an
additional generic public table API. Customize this file rather than passing
arbitrary columns to `DataTableDemo`.

## Motion contract

No row entrance, reorder, resize or layout motion. Sorting, filtering, pagination
and visibility update native markup immediately without keying the table or input
by state. Surviving rows use stable IDs; off-page rows unmount normally.
T2 describes the composed controls; there is no separate table animation runtime.

| Recipe / cause | full | reduced | none |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `feedback.press` / Button press | token spring scale | no scale | immediate |
| `state.morph` / checkbox or menu check | opacity and scale | opacity only | zero duration |
| `popup.anchored` / Columns or Actions opens | opacity and scale | opacity only | visible on first frame |
| `exit.fade` / menu closes | opacity and scale exit | opacity only | immediate |

Recipes and timing tokens belong to the installed controls. Dropdown Menu uses
its local `duration.fast` clock, including timeScale and reducedDurationScale,
even through a portal inside a differently configured provider. Live downgrade
drops transforms and `none` removes all motion transitions. No measured geometry,
loop, timer, stagger, or permanent `will-change` is introduced by this block.

## Keyboard and accessibility

Native table headers use `scope="col"`; the sorted header exposes `aria-sort`.
Tab reaches the named filter, column trigger, checkboxes, row actions and page
buttons. Space toggles a focused checkbox; Enter activates buttons. Arrow keys
navigate open menus, Escape dismisses and returns focus. No grid arrow-key model
is added to static cells. Each row checkbox includes its email in the accessible
name; the header is Select all. The filtered selection count is a live status.

## Responsiveness and performance

The toolbar and footer wrap. The native Table wrapper scrolls horizontally at
narrow widths; no data columns disappear automatically. Focus the named table
and use arrow keys to scroll, or use touch/pointer scrolling. The composition is
SSR-compatible with deterministic example data. Keep caller arrays stable where
possible; TanStack recomputes client row models when data/state change. This
block is intended for paginated collections, not an unbounded dataset benchmark.

## Notes for AI

- Keep Base UI `render`, Dropdown Menu groups, native table markup and stable row IDs.
- Register v9 features, row models, sorting and filtering functions explicitly.
- Keep data fetching, validation, stale selection cleanup and URL state caller-owned.
- Preserve all three modes of the composed controls; do not animate table geometry.
- Related: [Table](/components/table), [Checkbox](/components/checkbox),
  [Dropdown Menu](/components/dropdown-menu), [Pagination](/components/pagination).

items.docs:
## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/date-picker
```

The block installs Button, Calendar, Popover, their shared libraries and date-fns
4.1.0. For manual installation copy `registry/cadence/date-picker/index.tsx` to
`components/cadence/date-picker/index.tsx`, install those registry items and
`date-fns@4.1.0` plus `lucide-react`. Keep the sibling tree and relative imports.

## Usage

```tsx
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";

export function Appointment() {
  return <DatePickerDemo label="Appointment date" />;
}
```

An editable composition, using the [pinned Base example](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/96da9cc7f1aa10580a3741664e2a77c721206c00/apps/v4/examples/base/date-picker-demo.tsx)
and [guide](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/96da9cc7f1aa10580a3741664e2a77c721206c00/apps/v4/content/docs/components/base/date-picker.mdx),
with new-york-v4's calendar-icon treatment. There is no new date primitive.
The named `DatePickerDemo` export and initially empty single selection remain.
Selection leaves the popup open, including deselection of the selected day.

## Controlled date and clearing

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function ControlledDate() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date>();
  return <>
    <DatePickerDemo value={date} onValueChange={setDate} />
    <Button onClick={() => setDate(undefined)}>Clear</Button>
  </>;
}
```

A present `value` prop, including `undefined`, is controlled. Without it,
`defaultValue` initializes internal state and `onValueChange` observes changes.
A controlled value without a callback is read-only. Keep the ownership model
stable. `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` follow Base UI Popover semantics.
The default month is the selected month when the popup mounts; while open,
external selection changes preserve the displayed month and focus tree. To
navigate externally, pair `calendarProps.month` and `onMonthChange` explicitly.

## Range and presets

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import type { DateRange } from "react-day-picker";
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function Trip() {
  const [range, setRange] = useState<DateRange>();
  return <>
    <DatePickerDemo mode="range" label="Travel dates" value={range} onValueChange={setRange} />
    <Button onClick={() => setRange({ from: new Date(2026, 10, 10), to: new Date(2026, 10, 15) })}>Apply preset</Button>
  </>;
}
```

Range mode uses two months by default, matching the guide's range example.
The first click can produce an incomplete range (`from` without `to`); both
endpoints display once complete. DayPicker owns range rules. Pass `min`, `max`,
`excludeDisabled` or `disabled` through `calendarProps` when your application
needs them. Clear with a controlled `undefined` value. Presets are caller actions.

## Disabled dates and birth dates

```tsx
<DatePickerDemo disabled label="Unavailable" />
<DatePickerDemo label="Birth date" calendarProps={{
  captionLayout: "dropdown",
  startMonth: new Date(1920, 0), endMonth: new Date(2026, 11),
  disabled: { after: new Date(2026, 10, 1) },
}} />
```

`disabled` disables the trigger. `calendarProps.disabled` uses DayPicker matchers
for individual days. Dropdown captions and controlled months retain Calendar's
API. Application rules decide acceptable dates; disabling UI is not validation.

## Locale, date input and time

```tsx
import { fr } from "date-fns/locale";

<DatePickerDemo calendarProps={{ locale: fr, weekStartsOn: 1 }} />
```

The trigger uses date-fns `PPP` with the calendar locale (English by default).
Pass Date objects, not ambiguous date strings. Use `new Date(year, monthIndex,
day)` for local calendar dates; `new Date("2026-11-12")` parses as UTC and can
show the previous local day. This block does not serialize or convert time zones.
For DayPicker `timeZone`, supply dates constructed for that zone, such as
DayPicker's `TZDate`, so trigger and calendar share civil-date fields. The caller
owns persistence, DST policy and UTC conversion.

The upstream guide also illustrates input, time and natural-language compositions.
This copied block focuses on single/range calendar selection. Compose a labelled
native date/time Input alongside it if needed; keep parsing and text drafts in
the host application. No natural-language parser dependency or text validation
is installed. Locale alone does not set direction; set `dir="rtl"` on the host
and `calendarProps.dir="rtl"` when required.

## Validation and data ownership

The caller owns validation, parsing, submission, storage, fetching and time-zone
policy. Use `triggerProps` for `aria-invalid` or `aria-describedby`. No schema,
resolver, validation callback or hidden form input is added. Serialize selected
values explicitly in the application.

## When to use

- Appointment dates and optional calendar selection.
- Travel ranges, with application-owned presets and constraints.
- A starting composition to edit for your application's form.

## When not to use

- An always-visible date grid: use [Calendar](/components/calendar).
- Time-only entry: use a labelled [Input](/components/input) with `type="time"`.
- Free-form language parsing: supply your application's parser and draft state.

## API

`DatePickerDemoProps` is a discriminated union; range values require `mode="range"`.
Native div props, React 19 ref/cleanup, classes and styles go to `data-slot="date-picker"`.

| Prop | Type | Default / behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `"single" \| "range"` | `"single"` |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `Date` or `DateRange` | initially empty; present value is controlled |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: Date \| undefined) => void`, range equivalent | observes selection/deselection |
| `label` | `string` | `"Choose date"`; accessible trigger prefix and popup title |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `"Pick a date"` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false`, disables trigger |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` | Popover props | Base UI ownership and event details |
| `calendarProps` | corresponding optional-selection Calendar props | autoFocus, selected default month; range two months |
| `triggerProps` | `ButtonProps` | outline button; caller classes/styles/callbacks last |
| `contentProps` | `PopoverContent` props | start-aligned, available-size constrained, scrollable |

Selection props (`mode`, `selected`, `onSelect`, `required`) are owned by the
composition. Use Calendar directly for required/multiple selection. Other
calendar overrides remain caller-owned, including month, locale, focus and
components. A custom render must retain a focusable button and the supplied props.

## Motion contract

T2 describes existing control motion. No date label animation, layout tween,
selection-keyed remount, new recipe or runtime is added.

| Recipe / cause | full | reduced | none |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `feedback.press` / trigger press | token spring scale | no scale | immediate |
| `popup.anchored` / open | opacity and token scale | opacity only | visible first frame |
| `exit.fade` / close | opacity and scale | opacity only | immediate |
| `data.transition` / calendar month | token horizontal translation and opacity | opacity only | immediate |

Popover resolves its own `duration.fast` clock with timeScale and reducedDurationScale
inside the portal. Nested full can recover under outer none; OS reduce still wins.
Live reduced drops scale and live none cancels transitions immediately. Calendar
cancels its WAAPI effect on mode changes without replacing the grid or focused day.

## Keyboard and accessibility

Tab reaches the named trigger; Space/Enter opens the dialog. Calendar focuses the
selected enabled day or its initial focus target. Arrow keys move days, Home/End
move within the week, PageUp/PageDown navigate months. Escape dismisses and returns
focus to the trigger. Selecting a day keeps the popup open. Screen readers hear
the popup title, grid month, day labels and selected states. Range selection retains
DayPicker's grid model. Button names include the label and formatted selection.

## Responsiveness and performance

The trigger truncates long labels within the available width. The popup is bounded
by Base UI's available width/height and scrolls; range months stack on small screens
and sit side by side on desktop. No document overflow is required. Deterministic
example dates are SSR-compatible; empty uncontrolled selection renders without
reading the clock. DayPicker's current-month fallback depends on the host clock;
pass `defaultMonth` and `today` for deterministic server/client calendars.

## Notes for AI

- Keep this a registry block with namespaced dependencies and relative imports.
- Keep value presence semantics so controlled undefined clears correctly.
- Preserve stable Calendar identities and Base UI focus/render/event semantics.
- Keep locale and civil-date/time-zone policy explicit in the caller.
- Related: [Calendar](/components/calendar), [Popover](/components/popover), [Button](/components/button).

items.title: Attachment
items.description: Displays file media, metadata, caller-owned upload state, and actions.
items.docs: ## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/attachment ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Attachment, AttachmentMedia, AttachmentContent, AttachmentTitle, AttachmentDescription, AttachmentActions, AttachmentAction, } from "@/components/cadence/attachment"; export function FileCard({ onRemove }: { onRemove: () => void }) { return ( PDF report.pdf PDF · 2.4 MB × ); } ``` ## Upload state Pass `state="idle"`, `"uploading"`, `"processing"`, `"error"` or `"done"` from your application. Uploading and processing pulse the title; the description carries readable status even with animation disabled. An error needs text explaining the failure. Set `aria-busy` on the appropriate region and use a separate polite status for meaningful milestones, rather than announcing every progress update. ```tsx report.pdf Uploading · 64% ``` ## Images and sizes Use `AttachmentMedia variant="image"` with a native image and meaningful alt text. `orientation="vertical"` stacks it above the metadata; horizontal is the default. Sizes are `default`, `sm` and `xs`. The media is dimmed while work is in progress. Supply image URLs yourself; the component never creates or revokes object URLs. ## Trigger and independent actions `AttachmentTrigger` fills the card behind `AttachmentActions`. Give the empty trigger an accessible name. It defaults to a non-submitting button; `render` accepts an element or render function, preserving Base UI event/ref merging. Actions default to ghost Button with icon-xs size and accept Button's callbacks, native props and `render`. Keep actions in AttachmentActions so their stacking order leaves them independently reachable. ```tsx } /> ``` ## Scrollable groups Wrap cards in `AttachmentGroup` for a snapping horizontal row. Native scrolling is immediate and never smoothed by this component. For presentational cards give the group `tabIndex={0}`, `role="group"` and an accessible name; interactive cards can be reached with Tab. Allow the group to shrink within its parent. ```tsx workspace.png ``` ## When to use File previews in composers, upload lists, or message attachments with caller-owned metadata and optional open/remove/retry actions. ## When not to use Use Input for native file selection, Progress for a standalone percentage, and Item for generic content that does not represent a file. Attachment does not implement an uploader, drop zone, file parser or streaming message runtime. ## API | Part | Props and defaults | | --- | --- | | `Attachment` | Native div props; state `done`, size `default`, orientation `horizontal` | | `AttachmentMedia` | Native div props; variant `icon` or `image`, default `icon` | | `AttachmentContent` | Native div props; wraps metadata | | `AttachmentTitle` | Native span props; filename, busy opacity loop | | `AttachmentDescription` | Native span props; metadata/status text | | `AttachmentActions` | Native div props; independent action layer | | `AttachmentAction` | All Button props; size `icon-xs`, variant falls back to `ghost` | | `AttachmentTrigger` | Base UI useRender button props; type `button` without render; render element/function | | `AttachmentGroup` | Native div props; horizontal scroll and snap | Every part preserves its upstream `attachment-*` data-slot (root: `attachment`). Native refs, styles and events pass through; classes merge last. Root also exposes `data-state`, `data-size`, `data-orientation`; media exposes `data-variant`. No File or request state is stored internally. There is no default upload action. ## Motion contract | Cause | Recipe | Full | Reduced | None | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Uploading/processing title | `data.transition` | Opacity pulse via theme `animate-pulse` | Same opacity loop, no transform | `animate-none`, opacity 1 | | Default action pressed | `feedback.press` | Button token spring/press scale | No scale | Instant, no scale | Continuous timing comes from the project's `--animate-pulse` theme token. This replaces upstream's travelling shimmer with opacity to stay in the motion budget. Root/title and default actions expose `data-motion`; live none cancels the loop without replacing nodes. State, removal, size, orientation and media updates are immediate. No entry, exit, layout or geometry recipe is implied. Custom render controls can own their own feedback as with Button. ## Keyboard interactions Tab reaches triggers and actions separately. Enter/Space activate default buttons; a rendered link uses native link behaviour. Disabled actions retain Button's native semantics. A focusable group scrolls with arrow keys; Tab also reveals off-screen interactive cards. Removal focus policy belongs to the caller. ## Accessibility Name every icon-only action and overlay trigger, retain meaningful image alt text, and describe failures in text. The trigger has a visible focus ring. Avoid nested interactive elements inside triggers. Provide a polite live region for upload milestones outside a busy region. Truncated filenames remain in the DOM; a title attribute or your own details view can expose their full visual text. ## Validation and data ownership The application owns native file input `name`, `accept`, `multiple`, `required`, File objects, form submission, validation, upload progress, requests, cancel/retry, URLs and URL cleanup. Attachment forwards `aria-invalid`/`data-invalid` when given; `state="error"` only styles a supplied failure. It never decides which file is valid. The preview's file input reports the selected filename locally and makes no request. ## Responsiveness and performance Cards cap at their parent's width; long names truncate. Groups scroll horizontally with no document overflow when their parent can shrink. Large lists should be paginated or virtualized by the application. The busy opacity loop uses CSS with no per-frame JavaScript or layout reads; none stops it on the next style update. No @shadcn/react dependency or streaming runtime is needed for this pinned API. ## AI usage notes Compose these nine parts; keep upload state and file lifecycle in your application. Do not infer a network operation from the visual `state` value. Prefer stable file IDs as keys so a progress update preserves focus and the native input. There is no message streaming dependency and no reason to remount a composer when a file changes. ## Related components [Button](/components/button) supplies actions, [Input](/components/input) supplies native file selection, [Progress](/components/progress) displays known progress, and [Code Block](/components/code-block) displays textual file contents.
