items.title: Bubble
items.description: Displays conversational content with variants, grouping, reactions, and polymorphic surfaces.
items.docs: ## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/bubble ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Bubble, BubbleContent, BubbleGroup, BubbleReactions } from "@/components/cadence/bubble"; export function Conversation() { return ( Ready for review? The registry is ready. 👍 ); } ``` ## Variants and alignment Choose default, secondary, muted, tinted, outline, ghost or destructive. Bubbles cap at 80% of their container; ghost can use its full width. Start is the default alignment; end aligns a bubble to the opposite inline edge. Include readable error context for destructive content so color is not the only signal. Destructive uses a tinted background and destructive border with foreground text to retain readable contrast in both themes. ```tsx Message failed. Try again from the message actions. ``` ## Consecutive messages BubbleGroup groups surfaces from the same sender. It supplies a small gap; leave more vertical space when reactions overlap. Set alignment on each Bubble. Names, avatars, timestamps and conversation semantics belong to your surrounding UI. ```tsx First thought. One more detail. ``` ## Links and buttons BubbleContent accepts a Base UI render element or function. Use a real button with an explicit type or an anchor with href; their text provides the accessible name. Native handlers and refs, including React 19 ref cleanup, are merged by Base UI. ```tsx }>View attachments ``` ## Reactions Side defaults to bottom and align to end. Both accept the opposite edge. The row uses static positioning transforms, never animated movement. Label emoji-only rows as a single image; for interactive reactions supply named buttons and their pressed state instead. Leave vertical space for the overlapping row. ```tsx 👍🔥 ``` ## Updating text Keep the message ID and rendered element stable when adding text. Children update immediately without replaying entry, moving focus or animating measured height. The application owns chunking, message IDs, transport, cancellation, retry and scroll anchoring. This component neither parses Markdown nor orchestrates a stream. ## When to use Use for conversational text, quoted replies, suggestion buttons and short structured output; combine surfaces into a caller-owned conversation layout. ## When not to use Use Attachment for file metadata, Code Block for syntax-highlighted source, and Alert for a page-level notice. Bubble supplies a surface rather than a complete chat, message scroller, composer or streaming runtime. ## API | Part | Props and defaults | | --- | --- | | `Bubble` | Native div props; variant default/secondary/muted/tinted/outline/ghost/destructive (default: default), align start/end (default: start) | | `BubbleGroup` | Native div props; groups consecutive bubbles | | `BubbleContent` | Base UI useRender div props; render element or function | | `BubbleReactions` | Native div props; side top/bottom (default: bottom), align start/end (default: end) | All four parts retain upstream bubble-* slots (root: bubble), native styles, refs and events. Classes merge last; Bubble styles merge after its local clock. Bubble exposes data-variant, data-align and data-motion; reactions expose data-side and data-align. No additional message-state or validation API is introduced. ## Motion contract | Cause | Recipe | Full | Reduced | None | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | New Bubble enters | `data.transition` | Opacity 0→1, duration.base / ease.out | Opacity only, duration ×0.6 | Opacity 1 on first frame, zero duration | CSS @starting-style performs a one-shot entry. The duration resolves locally through cm.transition("data.transition"), including provider timeScale, so an inner full scope restores its clock inside outer none. Reduced drops animated transforms; this recipe uses opacity in full too. Live none cancels entry on the same node. Existing text, variants, alignment, reactions and resize update immediately. Removal is immediate; there is no exit or layout animation. Caller-provided motion is caller-owned. ## Keyboard interactions Presentational surfaces add no tab stops. Tab reaches rendered buttons, links and reaction buttons. Enter activates buttons/links; Space activates buttons. Interactive BubbleContent has a visible focus ring. Appending text preserves the same focused node. The application owns focus after removing a message. ## Accessibility Keep conversation-level semantics on a surrounding labelled region. Supply readable sender/error context and label reactions. Avoid nested interactive content inside button/link bubbles. Announce meaningful completed updates in a separate polite status region when needed; announcing every chunk can overwhelm assistive technology. ## Responsiveness and performance Long words wrap within a shrinking container. Reactions overlap vertically; give rows sufficient space and keep reaction collections compact. Rich content can use ghost with its own overflow treatment. Entry changes only opacity; no layout reads, per-frame JavaScript, timers or forced remounts. Application pagination or virtualization owns very large histories. No @shadcn/react dependency is needed for this pinned API. ## AI usage notes Compose the four parts with stable message IDs. Text and reaction state remain in your application. Use Collapsible for optional show-more UI and Tooltip/Popover for metadata; those components keep their own motion contracts. Do not invent streaming, validation or networking props on Bubble. ## Related components [Attachment](/components/attachment), [Code Block](/components/code-block), [Collapsible](/components/collapsible), [Tooltip](/components/tooltip), [Popover](/components/popover).

Its top and bottom edges use the shared physics spring, then render as translation and vertical scale on a one-pixel base. Wrapped labels determine the destination's length. Edges stay inside the rail, and interrupted movement preserves velocity. Text and `aria-current` follow the current section immediately. Activating a link smoothly scrolls the actual scrolling host to its heading in full mode. The destination respects the heading's scroll margin and the host's scroll padding; movement stays within the host's scroll bounds. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Active section or label size changes | Indicator translateY / scaleY | `layout.shared` / `spring.morph` | Yes; the existing indicator follows the latest target. | | Section link activation | Native scroll offset | `scroll.navigate` / `duration.page` / `ease.inOut` | Yes; another link retargets from the current position. | | Initial measurement / restored selection | Instant placement, no entrance | — | — | | reduced | Instant indicator placement and section navigation | — | Stops springs; completes an active navigation before paint. | | none | Instant placement and navigation, no animation clock | — | Stops springs; completes an active navigation before paint. | Zero provider timeScale also places the indicator immediately. Restoring full motion keeps the settled position until the next section or size change. A ResizeObserver supplies geometry; no layout is read during render. Navigation uses one token-backed tween, with no separate CSS/native smooth-scroll clock. Wheel, touch, pointer input, scrolling keys, resizing, history traversal and external hash changes cancel it at the current position. Positive clock changes retime the current trip; reduced/none or zero clock complete it immediately. No interrupted trip restarts later. The site's mobile disclosure stays instant. Initial hashes, reload, history traversal and no-JS links keep native behavior; only an explicit unmodified section link activation starts the recipe. ## Accessibility - A labelled `nav` contains an ordered list of native links. - Tab and Shift+Tab move between links; Enter activates the same navigation as a primary click. - The active link has `aria-current="location"` and a stronger text weight. The decorative indicator is hidden from assistive technology. - Heading targets need matching, unique ids. Offset their scroll margin to account for sticky headers. - Native anchors remain usable before hydration and without JavaScript. Automatic tracking requires JavaScript. - Navigation preserves unrelated URL parameters and history state, pushes the new fragment and notifies hashchange listeners. Back/forward use native scroll restoration. - Completion focuses the heading without scrolling a second time. A temporary `tabindex="-1"` is removed on blur/unmount; caller-supplied tabindex is preserved. Interrupted navigation never steals focus. - Modified/new-tab clicks and caller-cancelled clicks retain native behavior. ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | --- | --- | | Tab / Shift+Tab | Move between native section links. | | Enter | Scroll to the focused link's heading, update the fragment and focus the heading on completion. | | Scrolling keys / Tab / Escape | Interrupt an ongoing smooth navigation. | The indicator never receives focus or replaces a link when its destination changes. ## Responsiveness and performance The component fills its parent and wraps long labels. The caller owns placement, sticky position, height limits, and overflow. For documentation layouts, place it in a sticky right column with an independently scrollable list. Smaller viewports can use a native disclosure near the title; a floating disclosure list avoids moving the article when opened. Automatic tracking uses passive window scroll events, resize events, and a ResizeObserver, with cleanup on unmount. It reads heading positions in those callbacks, updates state only when the active id changes, and selects the final heading at the page bottom. It tracks headings present when mounted; remount after dynamically replacing the document or pass new items. The server renders the first entry as current; hydration corrects it for a deep link or restored scroll position. Before measurement, a static border marks the current link, including without JavaScript. The first measured position is immediate. The indicator remains mounted through selection and mode changes. The indicator's two edge values animate; the list's layout does not interpolate. Section navigation measures its destination once on activation, then writes native offsets without per-frame layout reads. A ResizeObserver tracks wrapped labels, font changes, and a mobile disclosure becoming visible. Motion and the shared Cadence provider/runtime are installed dependencies; a provider is optional and system reduced motion is respected standalone. The T3 source budget is 12 KB gzip; dependency and page budgets are measured separately. ## Notes for AI - Build the list from the same heading tree that renders the article so links and ids cannot drift. - Use this Cadence original for document navigation; it has no pinned shadcn counterpart. - Do not use a component instance to generate heading ids or to own application routing.
